Rounds 1 and 3 of the issue #666 audit shipped two capabilities on mobile and recorded that web still lacked them — a §24 inversion, since web is the canonical feature surface and mobile the additive one. Round 7 closes both. **Unsaved changes:** `trackDirty` snapshots a form's committed value and compares on demand, and `UnsavedChangesGuard.svelte` arms SvelteKit's `beforeNavigate` over it. Both of the browser's two departure paths are handled through that single hook rather than by adding a separate `beforeunload` listener: an in-app navigation is cancelled and re-driven through a shared confirm, while a `leave` navigation *is* the browser's `beforeunload` — SvelteKit turns the same `cancel()` into `preventDefault()` + `returnValue`, the browser owns the dialog text, and there is consequently no custom copy to show and nothing to render. Cancelling only while dirty is load-bearing rather than incidental: a permanently-armed `beforeunload` costs the page the engagement penalty browsers apply to one. Like mobile's §478 guard, dirtiness is probed **at navigation time** rather than tracked reactively, for the same reason — a value read at build time goes stale — but the mobile shape was deliberately not ported mechanically, because a `PopScope` predicate and a cancellable navigation event are different primitives with different capabilities. **Gym-session resume:** web's runner previously lost all state to a refresh. It now writes the same `gym_session_draft` metadata key §483 defined, with the identical field shape, and offers the same resume card on `/gym`; `restoreSessionDraft` rebuilds the runner by replaying the ordered outcome list against the current routine, so an edited routine degrades to replay-what-fits exactly as it does on mobile. Sharing the key rather than minting a web-specific one is the whole point: a session interrupted on either platform resumes on the other, which promotes the draft's field shape from a mobile implementation detail to a cross-platform contract — `metadata.md`'s entry, which had said "web and the watches ignore it", now records web as both a writer and a reader.
## 494. A tapped push routes through a pure URL→target mapper and a parked notifier, and a still-running broadcast says so

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 of the issue #666 audit closed the remainder of **I5**. The native-push bridge shipped with an `onOpenNotification` seam, a test for it, and `main.dart` constructing the bridge without ever supplying it — so every push tap opened the app wherever it already was and silently discarded the deep link the worker had stamped. Routing now goes `pushTargetFromUrl` → a `PushTarget` parked in a notifier → `HomeScreen` drains it. Each link in that chain is load-bearing. The mapper is **pure and total**: any base host, a relative path, a trailing slash, query or fragment junk, an unknown path and null all resolve rather than throw, with anything unrecognised degrading to the notifications inbox exactly as `pathForKind`'s own `default:` arm does. The **notifier rather than direct navigation** exists because a tap that cold-starts a terminated app is delivered before any Navigator exists; the target parks and drains on `HomeScreen`'s first frame, the same shape `incomingRouteImport` already uses for a GPX opened from a closed app. Reading **`getInitialMessage()` at attach** is equally load-bearing and was the audit's one correct suspicion: `onMessageOpenedApp` never replays the launch message, so a fix wired only to the stream works warm and fails silently cold — the precise half-fix this replaces. Corrections to the audit text: the target set is **nine** paths, not eight (the bare `/clubs` fallback `eventPath` and `clubPath` return for a row with no id was omitted), and `attach()`'s `Supabase.instance.client.auth` call sat *outside* the bridge's try/catch and throws outright when Supabase is uninitialised, contradicting the class's own L4 doc comment — now guarded, which is also what makes `attach()` testable against an available fake. Club and event targets carry a UUID against slug-addressed screens, so `SocialService` resolves the slug and degrades to the clubs hub on a miss; `/messages` has no mobile surface and lands on the inbox.

The same round found why `live_spectator_screen.dart` was an orphan, and it was not a missing menu item. The recorder pre-creates a zero-duration `runs` row so live spectator pings have a parent, and **every** public surface — web `/share/run/[id]` and mobile `PublicRunScreen` alike — rendered that stub as a finished run of 0.00 km in 0:00. Both now share `isLiveBroadcast` (`runs/live_broadcast.ts` ↔ `live_broadcast.dart`): `concluded_at` is consulted first because it is the positive terminal marker, then a zero `duration_s`, and an **absent** duration fails closed — "live" is a claim about right now and must never be inferred from a missing column. The resulting "Watch live" CTA is the tracker's first in-app entry, and it is deliberately not an invented nav destination: it sits on the surface a spectator already lands on from the feed, which was itself lying about the run. **V10's remainder** closed alongside it — `WorkoutExecutionBand` anchored on the status-bar inset while §485's column anchors at 56, so the two overlapped whenever a run started from a planned workout. `RunTopOverlay` now owns one anchor and all three slots, at `max(56, padding.top)` so folding the band in does not regress a tall cutout. Correction: §485's test could not simply be "extended" to cover this, because it pumps `RunTopBanners` standalone and never sees the band; the composed widget had to be extracted to make the invariant testable at all.
## 495. Data palettes are per-brightness and separated by luminance, and a normalised plot owes a scale

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed the remaining measurable contrast failures. Every figure below was computed against the real tokens, and the audit was wrong in both directions. **Medal pills:** silver drew white on `#94A3B8` at **2.56:1**; bronze, reported as failing beside it, was already **5.02:1** and was left alone. Web's rank-1 gold was the worst of the three at **2.15:1** and had never been reported at all, so gold moved onto a `--color-crown` / `--color-on-crown` pair mirroring mobile's `AppSemanticColors` (5.64 / 10.53:1), which also lifted the segment-crown icon from 1.85:1 to 6.24:1. Silver keeps its metal fill and takes dark ink (6.87 / 6.16:1) — the pill is opaque, so its foreground is free to change and its fill carries the meaning. **S6 (training load):** one fixed trio cannot clear 3:1 in both themes — indigo is 2.57:1 on the dark card (the audit's ~2.6 was right) and amber **1.94:1** on the light card (which the audit missed entirely) — so each brightness carries its own triple. Pairwise 3:1 *between* three series is unreachable once each also owes 3:1 to its card (light's whole usable range is 5.98:1), so what the guard pins between them is a monotone luminance ladder, not a pairwise floor. The same finding's second half was real: the plot was min/max-normalised with no gutter, so CTL 45 and CTL 450 drew identically; both platforms gained round ticks and gridlines, with web's labels in a CSS gutter *beside* the SVG because `preserveAspectRatio="none"` squashes any text inside the viewBox. **S8 (HR zones):** three surfaces carried three different five-colour lists while `intensity_card`'s own comment claimed it matched web `--zone-*` vars that **did not exist** and a run-detail band it **did not match**. Measured, the unaudited run-detail band was the worse of the two: adjacent bands at 1.32:1, the whole ramp spanning 2.11:1, four of five under 3:1. Five pairwise-3:1 bands are arithmetically impossible — four steps of 3:1 needs 81:1 and sRGB offers 21:1 — so the contract is inverted: every band clears 3:1 against its *surface*, and the separators between segments are drawn in that surface colour, which makes each boundary guaranteed visible against both neighbours. **Map attribution:** round 7 left the type size open; §482's 11 px floor applies, and the credit — a link with a neighbour 6 dp away, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception cannot be claimed — also owes a 24×24 dp target. It keeps a bespoke `TextStyle` rather than `labelSmall` because the strip is mounted inside the rasterised share cards: the size follows the theme's floor as a constant, the colour still follows the resolved basemap per §491. Finally, **semantic bases are foregrounds too**: the readiness delta used raw literals (3.15 / 3.25:1 on the dark card) on mobile and bare base tokens (3.28 / 4.14:1) on web, each failing AA in the theme the other passed, so `app_semantic_colors_test` now holds every base to 4.5:1 **as text** on card and scaffold rather than only 3:1 as a banner fill. The §480 literal allowlist shrank by six occurrences and gained no entries.
## 496. The worker emits stable ids and web resolves them, and a surface showing someone else's row links to the public twin

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 traced a live defect out of the push work: `pathForKind` — the single kind→URL map behind the email CTA, the web-push payload and the native-push message — emitted `/events/{id}` and `/notifications`, and **neither is a route**. Enumerating all fifteen kinds against the real route tree found three more the hand-off had missed. `run_completed` → `/runs/{id}` was dead because the trigger inserts one row **per follower**, so the recipient is never the run's owner and the owner-scoped page renders "Run not found" — every "a runner you follow finished a run" email dead-ended. `club_post` → `/clubs/{club_id}` matched `/clubs/[slug]` structurally while resolving by slug, so a UUID matched nothing. And `content_hidden`, added by a later migration, fell through `default:` to the dead inbox path. The root cause is that web already had a canonical routing table, `social/notification_link.ts`, that the worker had silently diverged from. `NotificationRow` genuinely cannot carry the club slug an event URL needs — the projections select one row's own FK columns and `pathForKind` is pure and shared by three render functions — so the rule is now explicit: **the worker emits stable-id URLs and web owns id→canonical resolution.** That is not merely the cheaper option; a slug baked into an email breaks on the next club rename, whereas the id URL is permanent. Both halves shipped, because a fix that only changes what *future* links say leaves every link already sitting in an inbox broken forever — `/events/[id]` and the `/clubs/[slug]` id fallback are therefore load-bearing permanently. The durable part is the guard: `notification_link_guard_test.go` parses the `NotificationKind` union from `types.ts`, walks `apps/web/src/routes` building a matcher per route, and asserts every kind × every FK-presence permutation resolves — proven to fire by reverting the fix. The Go tests had pinned the broken strings, which is exactly how this survived: **a guard on an outbound link must assert that the target resolves, not that the emitter produced a particular string.** The same mistake had been made independently on web, where the social feed linked another runner's entry to `/runs/{id}` and the page presented a public run as deleted — silently, and looking correct to the run's owner. Other-people surfaces link to `/share/run/[id]` and its siblings; only own-data surfaces use the owner routes. One more rung was missing under that lesson: **resolving is not arriving.** The `/clubs/{id}` half forwards inside its own route, and a same-route param change is the one navigation SvelteKit serves by reusing the component rather than remounting it — so `onMount`, the only caller of the club page's fetch, never fired again and every id link landed on the correct canonical URL and then sat on "Loading club…" for good. The Go guard was green throughout, correctly: it proves a path matches a route, which is a weaker claim than the page rendering the thing the link named. The forward therefore re-enters `load()` itself after the `goto`, passing the resolved slug down as an argument rather than re-reading the reactive `slug` — after `goto` resolves the derived has not necessarily propagated, so a pass that re-read it could see the uuid again and forward again. Bounded twice over: only a uuid forwards (`isEntityId` at the call site, and `fetchClubSlugById` returns null for anything else), and a canonical slug is never a uuid. `tests-e2e/clubs/id-deep-links.spec.ts` asserts the resolved page's **title** rather than its URL, which is what makes an empty arrival fail.
## 497. Text inside a fixed box is bounded three ways, by what the box is for

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed **V12**. The audit named 23 sites; a depth-0 scan finds **17**, of which **14 were real** — the gap is brace-matching that counts a spacer `SizedBox` nested anywhere inside a card that also holds a `Text`. Two more genuine sites existed that no literal scan can see, so 16 were fixed in total. The fixes divide by what the box *is*. A **layout** box in a scrollable column grows (`ConstrainedBox(minHeight:)`, or `IntrinsicHeight` with `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` where a strip must stay uniform). A **chart label lane** is a text-derived dimension and scales through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context)`, preserving the 1.0x geometry exactly. Text inside a **fixed-diameter graphic** whose size is load-bearing — a progress ring, a macro ring, a calendar day dot, an avatar, the run screen's Start circle — takes `BoxFit.scaleDown`, so 1.0x is untouched and a larger setting is fitted to what the graphic can hold, which is strictly more legible than the crop it replaces. Two findings matter beyond the mechanism. The this-week strip's fill bar rode an `Expanded` lane that the doubled labels squeezed to **exactly zero**, so the chart rendered blank for precisely the users who set large text — a fixed height can delete data, not merely clip it. And the Start circle was **already broken at 1.0x**: English "START" fills 117.5 of the 124 px interior, so French "DÉMARRER" was breaking mid-glyph before text scaling entered the picture — locale is a text-scale axis. Corrections to the audit text: `segments_panel.dart:824` does not exist (the nearest height wraps a spinner that is the other branch of a ternary from the text), and `event_detail_screen`'s "18 around a `fontSize: 10`" is not a box height at all but ui_kit's `IdentityAvatar`, a real clip fixed at the root for every avatar in the app. Deliberately unchanged and recorded so a later sweep does not "finish" them: `home_screen`'s 64 px nav items (58 px of content at 2x), the run screen's 56 px lap badge (45×32 inside 56, consistent with §486), photo tiles that bound images rather than text, and the fixed-canvas share rasterisers. The next sweep should match **computed** heights, not only literals: `nutrition_screen`'s week chart reads `barArea + 24` and overflowed 12 px per column.
## 498. A destructive mobile confirm is built by `confirmDestructive`, and a swipe is not an affordance

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed **U7** and **C11**, and the audit had the second one backwards. Counted on `main`: 88 `AlertDialog`s, of which 26 use two `TextButton`s — and **21 of those already carried destructive emphasis**, leaving only 3 unmarked, not the ~20 the audit claimed. Rounds 4–7 had effectively finished that family one dialog at a time; the unmarked-destructive problem had migrated to the `FilledButton` side, where 11 of 58 carried emphasis. (Counting this correctly requires stripping *nested* `AlertDialog` blocks first, or a parent inherits credit for its child's emphasis.) `lib/widgets/confirm_destructive.dart` now owns the shape — cancel first and unstyled, confirm second in the error colour, barrier dismiss resolving `false` — and `confirmDiscard` delegates to it, so one `AlertDialog` construction serves the whole family. The confirm **label is required** and must name the consequence rather than agree with the question: colour is a second signal a colour-blind reader may not receive, so the verb has to carry the meaning alone. **Destructive** means it destroys data, or a relationship the user cannot restore on their own — delete, remove, clear, erase, discard, revoke, unlink, deny, leave. It does not mean merely consequential: reconnecting an integration, un-archiving a conversation, replacing an active plan and an upsert-only restore are all recoverable by the same user from the same surface, and prompting alike on both teaches the user to dismiss without reading. The tempting "one-way ⇒ destructive" test was rejected — abandoning a plan is one-way and destroys nothing. A source guard in `architecture_guards_test.dart` classifies every dialog and fails an unemphasised destructive confirm outside a reviewed exempt set, so the classification is made deliberately rather than by omission.

The U7 sweep found a live bug inside itself. The coach archive drawer carried the app's only list-row `Dismissible`, and its `confirmDismiss` read `(_) => _deleteArchive(t)` — which *performs* the delete and returns whether it succeeded. A stray swipe erased an archived conversation with **no prompt and no undo**, while the row's subtitle advertised the gesture in seven languages. Destructive row actions now use the `PopupMenuButton` idiom the rest of the app already uses, behind `confirmDestructive`, and a guard fails any new `Dismissible` outside `top_banner.dart`, where dismissal destroys nothing. An inline icon button that is the *only* affordance on its row stays — it is visible and labelled, and the rule is against hidden destruction, not inline destruction; all 29 `Icons.delete` sites were classified and none mixes idioms. Long-press multi-select stays on runs and routes, where bulk delete is real, as a secondary accelerator over a visible per-row path — though it still has no discoverability hint on either screen, which is owed to a later round.
## 499. `pubspec.lock` is committed, and a test may not leak a timer the library owns

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8's integration run surfaced a defect none of the audits could have: **`main` was red in CI and no commit of ours had caused it.** `pubspec.lock` was gitignored, so every fresh checkout — CI included — resolved the newest versions the constraints allowed. `postgrest 2.9.1`, `supabase_flutter 2.17.1` and `realtime_client 2.13.0` were published at 08:47 on 2026-08-05, hours after the last green run on `main`, and `realtime_client 2.13.0` arms a 50 s pending-disconnect timer from *inside* `RealtimeChannel.unsubscribe`. Screens call that from `dispose`, so the timer does not exist until the tree is torn down and no amount of pumping inside a test body can drain it: 34 widget tests across the four channel-holding screens began failing `!timersPending`. The lockfile is now committed. These are applications, not libraries, and the lockfile is the only thing that makes CI, a fresh worktree and a developer's checkout resolve the same code — its absence is also why parallel agents kept verifying against a dependency set neither CI nor each other had. Upgrades become a deliberate act with their own CI run, which is what Dependabot is already wired for. **This was diagnosed twice before it was diagnosed correctly**, which is the more useful lesson: an agent reported the failures as pre-existing, and a fresh worktree at `main` appeared to confirm it — the control that settled it was running the *same commit* in the *main checkout*, which differed only in resolved dependencies. When a test fails in one tree and passes in another at the same SHA, the difference is the environment, and an unpinned dependency graph is the first place to look.

Pinning alone would have been a crutch, so the tests were fixed too. `test/realtime_drain.dart` wraps `testWidgets` with an unmount-and-pump-past-the-timer teardown, and the nine test files that mount a channel-holding screen use it. The full mobile suite now passes on **both** resolutions — 2.11.0 and 2.13.0 — so the pin holds a proven-green baseline rather than hiding an incompatibility, and the eventual Dependabot bump is pre-verified. The rule this leaves: a widget test must not leak a timer, including one a library arms on teardown where the app has no handle to cancel it; the drain belongs in shared test support, not copy-pasted per file, because the next library to do this will hit the same nine files.
## 500. The horizontal axis adds a fourth mechanism — the row reflows — and every width in this issue was measured in the wrong font

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed the horizontal half of §497. The vertical three transpose directly (a box grows via `minWidth`; a lane is text-derived through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf`; text inside a graphic whose size is load-bearing takes `BoxFit.scaleDown`), and width needs a fourth that height did not: **the row reflows**. A `Row` of text becomes a `Wrap`, and `WrapAlignment.spaceAround`/`spaceBetween` lay a single run out exactly as the `Row` did — so 1.0x is byte-identical and the reflow only fires when the content genuinely does not fit. It is preferred to ellipsis wherever a truncated label stops being a name: "Carboh…" is not a macro. The four sites divide cleanly — run-detail's split lanes are an *aligned column*, so they scale (a per-row intrinsic width would go ragged and misalign the bars), while the ring strip, the map credit strip and the mileage toggle are *runs of independent items*, so they wrap.

**The measurement finding outlasts the mechanism, and invalidates figures throughout this issue.** `flutter_test`'s default font is fixed-advance — every glyph exactly one em — so every absolute width quoted by the original audit *and by §497* is 2–6× too large. Measured against real Roboto via `FontLoader` across all seven ARB locales at 320/360/411 dp, the map credit strip is 31–84 px over at 411 dp rather than 181, and the nutrition ring strip is clean in English at 1.5x rather than 55 px over. The standing rule that follows: **a committed guard may not assert an absolute fit**, because CI cannot render the device's font. Pin the derivation — that a lane grew by the same factor as the text it holds, that a label stayed inside its container — which is font-independent and holds *a fortiori* under the wider test font. Measure absolutes against a real proportional font before quoting them anywhere.

**`SegmentedButton` is retired from any container narrower than its intrinsic width, and §486's exemption is amended.** That exemption treated it as a framework-managed internal with no knob to bind, which is right for narrow width; the same fact makes it fail text scaling in *both* directions. Given room it pushed its labels 88 px past a 411 dp card; given a bounded parent it squeezed its segments and clipped the labels *inside* them with no ellipsis and no exception — French "Semaine" got 66.7 px of the 109.9 it needed at 320 dp / 2x. Reflowing the container alone would have hidden the burst and kept the clip, so the control was replaced with chips in a `Wrap`, which also restores the M3 checkmark it had suppressed for width, so selection is no longer colour-only. Corrections to the audit: the depth-0 scan finds **505** numeric `width:` arguments, of which **34** enclose text and only **19** are real text lanes. Deliberately unchanged: `home_screen:739`'s nav caption, which ellipsizes cleanly and is §497's recorded exemption; the mileage card's spotlight-headline `Row`, a short stat beside an `Expanded` sibling that §486 swept and left; and the 13 remaining `SegmentedButton` sites, which carry the same exposure and are owed a measured sweep of their own.
## 501. An aligned text lane is `TextLane`, and a fixed box around text fails two ways, only one of which looks like a bug

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed 16 lanes across 11 files, measured against real Roboto per §500. **Six were live at 1.0x**, not the three the survey named: French "Semaine de fin de programme" needs 186.4 px of a 70 px box, Portuguese "Desaquecimento" 105.7 of 90, "28 de mar." 66.1 of 56 — and beside it "10:35 AM" needs 57.9, a two-digit hour clearing a box a one-digit hour fits, which is why the survey read the time as a 1.5x problem. Both rank lanes lose at 1.0x on a four-digit rank the survey never sampled.

**The audit's word for the failure was wrong throughout, and that is why fifteen of these shipped.** None of these `Text`s sets `maxLines`, so nothing clips. A label with a break opportunity **reflows inside its box** and makes its row taller than the column around it; one without **paints straight over the lane beside it**, because a `SizedBox` does not clip. The first is invisible as a bug and the second reads as a rendering glitch — neither reads as "text too wide for its box", which is what everyone was looking for. Twelve sites take `TextLane` (ui_kit): the literal read as a *floor* through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf`, collapsing §497's mechanisms 1 and 2 into one widget, so 1.0x is pixel-identical, the lane tracks the scale, and content that still outruns it widens the lane rather than losing characters. Three needed a different shape, and the difference is the durable lesson. The plan-preview phase is a localized *phrase*, and no floor rescues a 186 px phrase in a 70 px row, so it takes §486's treatment — `Expanded` + ellipsis on the label, flex removed from the two numerics so **a value can never be the thing that truncates**. The workout-structure row is a term beside its value, where a lane is actively dangerous: a `Row` sizes non-flexible children before giving what remains to `Expanded`, so an unbounded floor can starve the value to zero — §497's "a fixed height can delete data" recurring on the other axis. That pair reflows instead. A narrow source guard keeps the class closed without fighting the `BoxFit.scaleDown` graphics §497 settled, and it names all 15 pre-fix boxes at the exact line numbers the audit quoted, covering a re-plan-preview lane no widget test can reach.
## 502. A stat row reflows on a text-derived column width, a toolbar has three slots, and a FAB's clearance is derived rather than picked

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed C2, C4 and C5, and the audit's numbers were low on all three. Run detail's secondary row was one `Row` of up to eight `Expanded` cells: **40.0 dp each** on a 360 dp phone, under every value it draws — and because `_StatSmall` ellipsises rather than overflows, **nothing threw**. No debug banner, no test, just an unreadable screen for the hilly-race-with-a-chest-strap case. `_StatGrid` derives its column count from the width a cell needs *at the current text scale*, so eight stats become two rows of four at 1.0x and four rows of two at 2.0x, and the secondary row finally shares a column grid with the primary row above it. The same grid took the heart-rate summary row, which was three unbounded `_StatSmall` in a bare `Row` and genuinely overflowed at 2.0x — a §486 site the round-5 sweep missed because its texts sit two widgets down.

Route detail's toolbar carried six concurrent owner actions. A Material toolbar spends 72 dp before the title and 48 per action, so the title gets `width − 88 − 48n`, and six leaves **0 dp — not a crushed name, no name at all**; the audit said 24, having assumed 48 for the leading slot Flutter gives 56. `run_detail_screen` had solved this by hand for four actions and left a comment saying so, so `AppBarActions` is that answer as one widget, and `sim_watch_screen` — a third instance nobody had counted — takes it too. A `destructive` action is never promoted into a visible slot: a toolbar icon carries no label, and §498's reasoning about naming the consequence applies before the dialog as well as inside it.

The FAB finding was the one where every existing number was a guess: four screens reserved nothing, six reserved four different values, and the largest still under-cleared a stacked pair by 60 dp. `fabScrollClearance` reads `MediaQuery.padding` rather than `viewPadding`, which is what makes it composable — a `SafeArea` above the caller, or a parent `Scaffold` with a `bottomNavigationBar`, has already consumed the nav bar and reports zero, and adding it again would leave a dead band. **Two audit claims did not survive measurement** and are recorded so a later round does not "fix" them: route detail's fixed 88 was *adequate*, because its list sits inside a `SafeArea` and Flutter 3.41 zeroes `viewPadding` for its descendants — **§C20's diagnosis is stale for this Flutter version**; and `plans_screen`'s comment that "Scaffold does NOT automatically pad FABs" is likewise stale, its compensating `Padding` having floated the button ~48 dp too high on 3-button navigation ever since `endFloat` learned `minViewPadding`. The general lesson is the one the 0 dp title makes concrete: a layout constant that was true of some Flutter version decays silently, so the durable form is a helper that derives the number and a guard that fails the next screen which hard-codes one.
## 503. A status token is a foreground or a fill, never both, and a chip tint is measured where it lands

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 finished the web half of §495. **96** sites across 46 files still set `color: var(--color-success)` / `var(--color-danger)` directly — success at **3.282:1** on the card and **2.968:1** on the page, below even the 3:1 non-text floor — and all moved onto the `-text` pair. Measuring the swap honestly exposed two things a plain-surface figure hides, one of them a defect in §495's own work. **The dark `-text` tokens were aliased to the base hue**, which reads 5.286:1 on the card but **4.059:1 on the same-hue chip tint** most of those sites actually paint: the token comment's claimed parity with mobile's `AppSemanticColors` was true in light and false in dark. Both now carry mobile's real pair, and the lockstep is asserted rather than described. And three RSVP pills stacked a tint over an already-tinted parent — 18% over 14% composites to 29.5%, giving **3.345:1** — so a status tint carrying same-status text is now mixed against an opaque surface, which cannot compound.

The ban is on **foreground** use across `color` / `fill` / `stroke` / `-webkit-text-fill-color`; fills, tints, borders and the white-on-`-strong` pairing are what these tokens are for. That distinction rests on a single lookbehind character, so an 18-case fixture table pins the matcher in both directions — six must-flag, twelve must-spare — and the guard was proved to fire six ways, including by deleting the boundary and watching the fixtures catch it. Two further data palettes S8 never reached were folded onto the shared ladder: the intensity split bar, whose amber is 2.148:1 on the light card but whose real defect is **1.032:1 against its own partner in dark** — `--color-primary` flips to coral and coral *is* the amber, so the split bar showed no split at all — and the dashboard's per-zone bars, the fifth HR-zone list in the codebase and the worst measured yet, with z3 and z4 **1.016:1** apart in light and z1–z4 inside **1.08:1** in dark. Two bands can be pairwise 3:1 where five cannot, so easy/hard take `--zone-1`/`--zone-5` rather than a third bespoke pair. The zone-name tints were deleted rather than recoloured: `--zone-5` is 3.592:1 and cannot be text, and a label tinted a hue its own bar does not draw is §489's mislabelled-key defect one level up. **Left open with numbers:** `css_token_guard.test.ts` only fails on *fallback-less* `var(--x)`, so **129 fallback-hidden references to tokens that do not exist** survive across ~41 files — `var(--chip-fg, #335)` at **1.344:1** on the dark card, `var(--color-error, #b71c1c)` at 2.460:1, `var(--text-muted, #6b7280)` at 3.344:1. Those declarations never track the theme at all; it is the same bug class that guard's own doc comment describes, wearing a fallback.

## 504. A loading surface is chosen by the shape it will settle into, and the two named primitives grew a third host

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 10 of the issue #666 audit closed the remainder § 492 deliberately left: the **14** bare `Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator())` loaders, verified present on `main` at exactly 14 sites, and the two hand-rolled empty states the round-4 V9 sweep never enumerated. § 492's line was right that these were not a mechanical swap — but the reason is narrower than "per-surface judgement", and naming it is what made the sweep finishable. `ListSkeleton` is a `ListView` with `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics`: the viewport is doing nothing but layout, yet it still **requires a bounded height**, which is precisely what a loader occupying one section of an already-scrolling screen does not have. Two of the fourteen sat in exactly that host — `run_social_section`'s comment list, mounted as one child of the run-detail and public-run scroll columns, and `workout_detail_screen`'s re-link picker, whose loaded state is a `shrinkWrap` list inside a dialog's `Flexible`. So `ListSkeleton` gained a `.section` named constructor: the same rows, the same 900 ms pulse and the same reduced-motion pose, laid out as an intrinsic-height `Column` instead of a viewport. One widget with two hosts rather than a second widget sharing a private row — and deliberately **not** a single always-intrinsic implementation, because a `Column` overflows where a viewport clips, and ten bounded call sites already depend on the clip.

The remaining twelve divide by the shape the surface settles into, which is the rule the convention now states. **Rows in a bounded host (7):** `club_detail`'s Routes and Templates tabs, `settings_body_metrics` and `settings_safety` (a settings form *is* a stack of rows), `session_detail`'s step list, `watch_screens_editor`'s screen cards, and `coach_screen`'s thread pane inside its `Expanded` — all `ListSkeleton`, with `hasLeading: false` wherever the loaded rows carry no leading column, plus `coaching_athlete`'s three stacked cards at 120 dp. **Mixed layout (3):** `challenge_detail`, `live_spectator` and `public_route` take `FullBodyLoader` — a map beside stats has no row rhythm to stand in for, and a skeleton that invents one is a worse lie than a spinner. **A composite (1):** `profile_screen`'s whole-profile load, which § 492 flagged as "neither a list nor a plain body", is now the two primitives composed into the layout it becomes — a `.section` header block, the `Divider`, and an `Expanded(ListSkeleton)` — so each tab's own `_tabScope` skeleton takes over without a reflow. Reaching for a fourth primitive there would have been the mistake; composition was already sufficient.

Both hand-rolled empty states were in **unbounded** hosts (`period_summary_screen`'s `_buildEmptyState`, one child of the screen's `ListView`; `watch_screens_editor`'s `_EmptyState`, one child of the editor's), so § 485's host-adaptive contract carried them with no change to either host's scrolling — pinned on both by asserting `EmptyState` nests no `SingleChildScrollView` of its own. `period_summary_screen`'s `RepaintBoundary`→PNG share path was not touched (theme-free exempt). No new i18n: every converted site reuses `commonLoading`, and both empty states keep the keys they already had. The durable part is a two-part source guard beside § 492's avatar trio, proven to fire by probe: `lib/` now holds **zero** bare centred spinners (was 14) and **zero** `class …EmptyState` declarations (was 2), and the guard's message names which of the three treatments to reach for, because the trap was never a bug in one file — it was the shape every screen reached for while nothing named existed to reach for instead. Correction to § 492's text: the 14 line numbers had drifted by rounds 8-9 (e.g. `challenge_detail_screen:184`→`:177`, `watch_screens_editor_screen:429`→`:409`, `club_detail_screen:1393`/`:1510`→`:1384`/`:1501`); the file set was exactly right.

## 505. A chart takes its marks from `ChartPalette` and its header from `ChartCardHeader`, and the brand accent is not a data colour

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 10 closed **S7**. Five dashboard data-visualisation surfaces carried four colour systems and, counted properly, *three* header typographies plus a fourth surface with none: `ThisWeekStrip` a `titleSmall`, `MileageTrendCard` and `IntensityCard` a `labelMedium` eyebrow on `colorScheme.outline`, `TrainingLoadChart` a `titleMedium`, and the activity heatmap no header at all. Two of the audit's five bullets did not survive re-measurement and are recorded so a later round does not "fix" them: `intensity_card.dart` no longer holds Material-2 swatches or a Tailwind literal (round 8 moved it onto `hr_zone_palette`, and the quoted `:172-178` is now the separator-gap `_SegmentedBar`), and `TrainingLoadChart`'s "Tailwind hexes" are §495's measured per-brightness triple. What *was* still true is the part the audit stated most weakly — "theme primary ramp" — and it was the worst thing on the screen. `ChartPalette` (ui_kit) is now the one home, with three scales because charts need three shapes of answer: **categorical** `series` (§495's triple, relocated verbatim), **ordinal** `zones` (the five HR bands, moved out of the mobile-only `hr_zone_palette.dart` that two surfaces read while the other scales lived in ui_kit), and **sequential** `ramp`, which is new. `ChartCardHeader` is the one header, and it paints in `onSurfaceVariant` rather than `colorScheme.outline` — `outline` is §487's 3:1 *boundary* token and reads **4.058:1** on the light card, so as the 11–12 sp type these cards carry it was under 1.4.3's 4.5:1 on every one of them.

**`colorScheme.primary` is not a chart colour, and the heatmap is why.** Composited and measured against its card, the heatmap's four levels — `surfaceContainerHighest`, then primary at 35 % / 65 % / 100 % — read **1.164 / 1.952 / 4.038 / 11.005:1** in light and **1.316 / 2.102 / 4.063 / 7.766:1** in dark. Two of four levels were under 1.4.11's floor in both themes, and the failing pair is the semantically load-bearing one: the zero tiles *are* the calendar frame that says which day a filled tile is, so an invisible frame costs the filled tiles their meaning as well as its own. The sequential `ramp` replaces the alpha ladder (**3.897 / 7.228 / 13.386** light, **3.859 / 7.126 / 13.149** dark, adjacent steps ~1.85:1), and the zero tile is treated as a **track rather than a level** — it keeps a faint fill and gains a hairline in the line token §487 already holds at 3:1 (3.531 / 3.330:1), which is §487's own "separation comes from the hairline, not a tonal fill" one level down. The ramp is constructed as a tint ladder from the card toward `series.first`, so `ramp.last == series.first` and a single-series bar chart (`palette.bar`) draws the same colour as the heatmap's busiest day: there is one intensity ladder in the app rather than three that drift. The deeper reason to ban the accent is that its *hue is not stable across brightnesses* — dusk in light, coral in dark — so a mark painted in it means "data" in one theme and echoes an interaction affordance in the other. §503 recorded exactly this firing on web, where the intensity split bar's two halves landed **1.032:1** apart in dark because `--color-primary` flips to the same coral the warm series already used. One `primary` survives, count-pinned: the week strip's *today* ring, which is a state marker and is the one mark on that strip that must **not** read as a bar.

**The sweep found a live defect §495 had introduced in its own fix.** §495 gave the training-load plot labelled gridlines so a min/max-normalised series would carry a magnitude — and drew them at `outline` × 0.5 × 0.45, which composites to **1.297:1** on the light card and **1.410:1** on the dark one, with the dashed zero datum at **1.852 / 2.284:1**. The ticks were labelled and the lines they labelled could not be seen, so the scale the ADR added was decorative. Gridlines now take `theme.dividerColor` and the zero datum `onSurfaceVariant`; the dash is what still distinguishes them, which is what the original comment already claimed. The general rule this leaves: **an alpha multiplier is not a contrast argument.** A token guarded at 3:1 stops being guarded the moment a caller thins it, and two multipliers compounding (0.5 at the call site, 0.45 in the painter) is exactly how a 3.5:1 token became 1.3:1 with nobody writing down a number. Enforcement is two guards. `packages/ui_kit/test/chart_palette_test.dart` computes every ratio in the palette — 3:1 per mark per surface, monotone ladders, `ramp.last == series.first`, and that nothing aliases `primary` or `secondary` — and was proved to fire by substituting the old composited `#B5AEBA`, which it reports at 1.952:1. `apps/mobile_android/test/chart_surface_guard_test.dart` (both twins) count-pins `colorScheme.primary` and `colorScheme.outline` per chart surface and requires each to reference both `ChartCardHeader` and `ChartPalette`, so a sixth chart card cannot quietly open a fifth colour system; `dashboard_screen.dart` is scoped to its `_RunHeatmap` region because the file is a whole screen. Also closed here: **S16**, ui_kit's `ElevationChart` — exported, referenced by nothing in `apps/` or `packages/`, blanking on a flat run (`range == 0 → return`), dividing by zero on a single sample, and carrying hardcoded English. It is deleted rather than fixed; the run-detail screen's own private `_ElevationChart` is a different widget and is the one that ships. **Left open with numbers:** after this sweep `colorScheme.outline` still appears **325 times across 66 files** under `apps/mobile_android/lib`, of which **58** are the single-expression `?.copyWith(color: … .colorScheme.outline)` form that is unambiguously *text* at **4.058:1** on the light card. The rest mix text with icon and border tints, where 3:1 is the correct bar, so the class needs a pass that classifies each site rather than a regex — but every text one among them is the same defect this entry names, wearing a different card.

**The relocation broke two web guards, and only the integration branch could see it.** Both scales were the mobile side of a cross-language lockstep asserted from web: `contrast_guard.test.ts` read `--chart-fitness`/`-fatigue`/`-form` out of `training_load_chart.dart`'s `TrainingLoadPalette` and `--zone-1`..`--zone-5` out of `hr_zone_palette.dart`. Moving both into `ChartPalette` deleted the file one guard read and the symbol the other matched, so the pair failed the moment the branch met the rest of round 10 — invisibly to the agent that made the move, which ran no web tests, and to the web agent, whose tree still had both files. The guards are repointed at `chart_palette.dart` and now read the scale **by name** (`series:` / `zones:` inside `static const light|dark = ChartPalette(`) rather than by ordinal position, which is the durable part: a positional match would have gone on passing against whichever list happened to come first in the new file, and a palette with three scales in it makes that a live hazard rather than a theoretical one. Re-proved by perturbing `zones[0]` and watching the guard name the drift. The general point is one about verification scope rather than about charts: a **cross-language lockstep guard lives in the other language's test suite**, so a change that satisfies every test in its own stack can still break it, and only the branch that holds both stacks at once will say so.

## 506. A fallback on an undeclared token is a hardcoded value in a var() costume, and it blinded two guards, not one

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§503 left this open with numbers and the numbers were right: **130** references across **39** files (it said 129/~41) were written `var(--missing-token, #hex)`, so the declaration was pinned to that literal in both themes and never tracked the theme at all. All three quoted figures reproduce exactly — `var(--color-error, #b71c1c)` at 2.460:1, `var(--text-muted, #6b7280)` at 3.344:1, `var(--chip-fg, #335)` at 1.344:1 on the dark card. **The third is measured on the wrong background, and it is §503's own trap sprung on §503**: that chip also paints `var(--chip-bg, #eef)`, equally frozen, so the text lands on `#eef` at **10.49:1** — legible, and glaringly light-on-dark rather than unreadable. The correction matters because it re-ranks the defect: the fallback form's harm is that it *freezes the theme*, not that it always fails contrast, and a fix justified purely on contrast would have missed the worse cases. The genuinely worst were unreported: `var(--color-on-primary, #fff)` at **2.081:1** in dark, because `--color-primary` flips from dark teal to light coral and white rides a fill that moved underneath it; and muted text at **2.815:1** (`#666`) and 2.873:1 (`#667`) on the dark card, with `#889` failing the other way at 3.483:1 in *light*. Six roles were minted rather than left as hexes (`--color-on-primary` 7.073 light / 9.120 dark, `--color-warning-light` completing the success/danger triad, a `--chip-bg`/`--chip-fg` pair, `--radius-pill`, `--font-mono`, `--sidebar-collapsed-width`); the rest routed onto existing tokens, worst case now 4.738:1. Two traps are recorded because both look like the obvious answer: **`--color-bg-tertiary` is byte-identical to `--color-surface` in dark**, so it cannot fill anything sitting on a card (1.000:1) — the chip pair therefore aliases `--color-border`/`--color-text` (10.83 / 11.01:1), `--color-text-secondary` being unusable at 4.34:1 for 0.75rem type; and a token naming a layout slot that does not exist (`--app-header-h`, a header this layout has never had) is deleted, not declared. Several "fixes" here were not contrast fixes at all but theme fixes — a `#e5e7eb` track or `#f3f4f6` panel blazing at 13–14:1 on a dark card where subtlety was intended.

The durable half is one character in `css_token_guard.test.ts` — `\)` becomes `[,)]` — with the undeclared set still derived from the real declarations in `app.css` plus each file's own, never a hand-list. The rule it draws is **existence, not syntax**: a fallback on a *declared* token stays legal, because it is the documented default for a component custom property a parent sets per instance (`style:--x={...}`), whereas a fallback on an undeclared token is a literal wearing a `var()`. An 18-case `MATCHER_FIXTURES` table pins that character in both directions (10 must-flag incl. nested `var(--a, var(--b))` checking *both* names; 8 must-spare incl. declarations and `style:--x` directives), and it was proved to fire both ways — reverting the boundary fails two fixtures, and an injected `var(--definitely-not-a-token, #fff)` is reported with its file:line. **The finding that outgrew its own scope is that the same one-character gap sat in `contrast_guard.test.ts`.** `FOREGROUND_TOKEN_OFFENDER` also required the fallback-less form, so **28 live §503 violations were invisible to §503's own guard**: a fallback on a *declared* token is dead code (the token resolves and the fallback is never used), so `color: var(--color-warning, #b45309)` painted 2.048:1 warning text while reading as guarded. Eight surfaced when the sweep stripped dead fallbacks off `--color-warning`/`--color-success`; twenty more — all `color: var(--color-danger, #hex)` at 4.137:1 on the page and 4.576:1 on the card in light, under AA — only surfaced when the boundary moved. All take the `-text` pair (5.664 / 6.265:1). §503's foreground-vs-fill rule is not merely preserved but was the thing that caught the sweep over-reaching: the guard rejected eight `color:` sites the mechanical pass had put on base tokens, and a `border-color` a `\b` boundary had wrongly promoted to `-text` is fixed as a border. **The lesson generalises past CSS: a guard that matches one syntactic form of a construct silently exempts every other spelling of it, and the exempted spelling is where the violations accumulate** — precisely §496's "assert that the target resolves, not that the emitter produced a particular string," one level down. **Left open with numbers:** the separate hex-literal item, deliberately sequenced after this one so no fallback hex could be allowlisted as legitimate, now stands at **453 six-digit hex literals across 72 files** in `apps/web/src` `.svelte`+`.css` — down from the audit's correctly-measured 539/88 — and still has no web equivalent of mobile's `status_color_literal_guard_test.dart`.

## 507. A notification kind ships with real copy in every locale or a recorded in-app-only exemption

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 fixed where notification deep links *pointed*. This closes what they
*said*. `email_i18n.go`'s catalogue carries a `"default"` entry — "You have a
new notification on Threkir." with an "Open Threkir" CTA — as the fallback for a
kind an older running worker predates, draining a queue a newer deploy is
filling. It had quietly become the resting place for kinds we already knew
about: `plan_assigned`, `achievement` and `challenge_complete` had no entry, and
`lookupEmailStrings` fell through for all three. Because one catalogue feeds the
email, web-push and native-push renders, every channel said the same nothing at
once.

The mechanism is that nothing anywhere failed. The notifications AFTER-INSERT
triggers enqueue an email job *and* a push job for **every** kind with no
allowlist — the headers on migrations `20270107_001` and `20270208_001` assert
the opposite ("in-app only unless added to those channels' allowlists"), and
that claim is simply false; no such allowlist exists. The only kind-level gate
is `importantKinds`, which suppresses a kind under the default `important` mode
but not under `all`, so any recipient who had opted into everything was being
mailed content-free notices. And the guard that looked like it covered this,
`TestEmailCatalogueParity`, checks the catalogue against **itself** — every
locale carries every `en` key — which by construction cannot see a key missing
from `en` too. The audit's guess that `comment_reply` was also missing was
wrong: `keyForKind` collapses it onto `comment` deliberately.

Three corrections landed. **Copy** for the three emailable kinds in all six
locales, reusing the nouns the web inbox already localizes (achievement /
Erfolg / succès / logro / アチーブメント / conquista) so the mail and the bell
don't name the same thing differently. **Deep links** at the entity rather than
a list page — `/plans/{plan_id}`, `/challenges/{challenge_id}`,
`/share/badge/{achievement_id}`, matching web's `notificationLinkFor` — which
required `plan_id`, `achievement_id` and `challenge_id` in all three
`FetchNotificationFor*` projections, since one `pathForKind` serves three
renders and a partial projection degrades one channel silently. Each recipient
here is the entity's owner or participant, so none of it repeats round 8's
`run_completed` mistake of mailing an owner-scoped URL to a non-owner; the badge
target is the public share page, which needs no session at all. And **guards**
that read the `NotificationKind` union out of `apps/web/src/lib/types.ts` — the
same cross-language source the round-8 link guard reads — failing unless a kind
has copy or a recorded exemption, and additionally asserting the rendered
subject differs from the default so copy that is present but cloned from the
fallback fails too.

`content_hidden` we deliberately did **not** write copy for. It is now the sole
member of `inAppOnlyKinds`, honoured by both `shouldEmail` and `shouldPush`.
Three reasons: it has no destination (web's `notificationLinkFor` returns `null`
for it by design, so an outbound message would carry a CTA with nowhere to go);
it is a *provisional* automated action from `auto_hide_target` that a human
reviewer may reverse within hours, and a permanent copy in a mailbox overstates
that finality; and it fires off a report count, which a coordinated reporting
campaign can drive — mailing and pushing it would hand the campaign a channel
the recipient cannot mute per-kind. The inbox row still carries the notice, so
nothing is withheld from the user and the transparency obligation is met on the
surface that can also show the reversal. The exemption is enforced explicitly
rather than by omission from `importantKinds`, because that omission only covers
the default mode.

The same class of defect was live on the mobile inbox and is fixed in the same
round: `_verbFor` listed ten of fifteen kinds and fell through to
`profileNotifGeneric`, "{name} interacted with your activity" — not merely vague
but wrong, since nobody interacted with anything when a plan is assigned, and
for `content_hidden` it credits a named actor with an automated moderation
action. Six arms added, strings across all seven ARBs, and a generated
per-kind test reading the same union.

What we left: the two migration headers that state the false allowlist
invariant stay as written (migrations are forward-only), so the correction lives
in `apps/job_worker/CLAUDE.md`'s NotificationKind three-file rule and in
`docs/features/email.md` instead. `plan_update`'s and `event_*`'s existing copy
was not rewritten — only the three missing entries were added and
`plan_update`'s link was upgraded alongside `plan_assigned`, since they share
one `pathForKind` arm and one FK. The audit's companion claim that
`NotificationKind` is absent from `check_constraint_unions.mjs`'s `PAIRS` is
**stale** and was not acted on: the pair is present, the guard passes, and the
effective CHECK (migration `20270218_001`, which supersedes the `20270211_001`
reconcile) matches the 15-value union exactly.

## 508. `/runs/[id]` gained a non-owner branch — the owner fetch stays owner-scoped, and entitlement is resolved separately against `public_runs`

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 found that `run_completed` notification links were dead because the trigger fires one row **per follower**, so the recipient is never the run's owner, and it fixed the emitters by pointing them at `/share/run/{id}`. That closed the *links*. It left the *surface*: `/runs/[id]` — the canonical signed-in run page — rendered "Run not found" for every run the viewer didn't own, including a **public** run by a runner they follow that RLS would happily have let them read. The consequence was that the whole comment + kudos capability, which has existed since §32, had no reachable signed-in home for someone else's run; `RunSocial` already derives `isOwn` from `runOwnerId` and already mounts inside `RunShareView`, so the UI was built and only the door was missing. Several e2e specs had written the 404 into their headers as a permanent property of the app, and one journey step asserted it outright ("a non-owner ALWAYS sees not-found there regardless of `is_public`") — the standing lesson that a guard which pins current behaviour will happily pin a bug.

The fix deliberately does **not** relax `fetchRunById`. Its `.eq('user_id', userId)` is not incidental scoping: it is the only read path that downloads the *unclipped* GPS track from the owner's Storage folder, so widening it would put an unclipped trace one refactor away from a stranger's screen. Instead the page resolves the two questions separately. Ownership is still `fetchRunById`. Entitlement is a new `fetchPublicRunAttribution`, which asks the `public_runs` view — and because that view runs as its owner with `where is_public = true`, **a returned row *is* the entitlement**, no second predicate to keep in sync. It projects `user_id` and nothing else, so no caller can ever render a run field from it; the row and the privacy-zone-clipped track both come from `RunShareView`, the same component `/share/run/[id]` mounts, which is the single place that calls `fetchClippedTrackForRun` → the `clip-public-track` Edge Function (§33). The clean answer here really was "a non-owner view *is* the share view with signed-in social attached", and building anything else would have been a second render path to drift.

Two structural properties make owner-chrome suppression safe rather than diligent. First, the non-owner row is **never assigned to `run`** — it lives in a separate `otherRunOwner` state and takes a sibling `{#if}` branch, so every owner affordance (edit, delete, visibility, gear assign, save-as-route, rematch, GPX) is unreachable by construction rather than by a list of `{#if isOwner}` guards a later edit can forget. Second, every owner-only background fetch (matched track, route suggestion, linked workout, HR-zone settings, `get_my_profile`) sits behind an early return. `cross_user_link_guards.test.ts` pins both: that the `otherRunOwner` branch precedes the not-found branch, and that the only fresh source ever assigned to `run` is `fetchRunById`.

Worth recording what the RLS actually permits, because the finding's framing ("let a **follower** comment") does not match it. There is no follower-visibility and no club-visibility on runs. Base-table SELECT is owner (`users own their runs`, 20260405_001) or active coach (20261103_001); `private.is_run_visible_to`, which gates kudos + comment reads and writes, is owner OR `is_public` OR active coach, with the block filter on top (20270204_001). So "a follower" is really "any signed-in viewer of a public run", and the new branch grants exactly that and nothing more — a private run by someone you follow still lands on not-found, pinned in both directions by the visibility-propagation journey (renders when public, not-found again after re-privatising). The coach's read of an athlete's *private* run is deliberately **not** routed here: the policy grants the row, but the raw trace stays owner-only (§98), so that surface remains `/coaching/athletes/[id]`.

The feed and worker links stay on `/share/run/{id}` and that is not now redundant: the share pages are anon-reachable and indexable, while `/runs/[id]` sits behind the layout auth-gate. The rule generalises to a second half worth stating alongside §499's "link other people's rows to the public twin": **an owner surface a stranger can plausibly reach needs a non-owner branch, not a 404** — people paste URLs out of the address bar, and a public row presented as deleted is the same silent failure in a different place.
## 509. A stat cell is `StatTile` at one of three emphases, the row it sits in is `StatGrid`, and eight of the twelve near-copies were the same widget while four were not tiles at all

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 closed **V8**, the audit's largest duplication finding, and the audit's own count needed both halves correcting. ui_kit's `StatCard` was real and dead — exported, imported by nobody, a `Card` + `Column(value, label)` — so it is deleted rather than adopted. Of the twelve private reimplementations the audit named, **`_LiveStats` is not a widget at all** (a `run_screen` data class holding elapsed / distance / pace / track) and **`_StatsOverlay` and `_CollapsedStatsBar` are not tiles** (the frosted map overlay that *composes* the cells plus every recording control, and a clock beside a hold-to-stop button with no stat in it). `_SegmentStatsCard` is a dismissible `Card` of inline `label: value` chips in a `Wrap`, not a stacked pair. Counted properly there were **eight** duplicate value-over-label tiles, and they had drifted to **six** value type sizes (`headlineMedium`/`headlineSmall`/`titleLarge`/`bodyMedium`, two of them at different weights), two label sizes, two muted colours, and **three different answers to "the value is too wide"** — `FittedBox` scale-down, `Flexible` + ellipsis, and nothing.

**The third answer was a live defect, and one file already had the diagnosis written on it.** `public_run_screen` carried the comment *"Expanded, not spaceAround: an intrinsically-sized cell has no bound for its FittedBox to scale against, so a long value overflowed the row instead of shrinking"* — and `public_route_screen`'s and `period_summary_screen`'s hero rows were exactly the shape that comment describes, an intrinsic cell in a `spaceAround`/`spaceEvenly` `Row`, both with no `FittedBox` at all. An ultra's `104:32:11` or a four-digit `1234.56 km` bursts either row. The lesson is not about stats: **a `BoxFit.scaleDown` is a claim about a bound the parent has to supply**, so the fix belongs in the layout, not the leaf. `StatGrid` is that layout — it bounds every cell with a `SizedBox`, so the scale-down always has something to scale against, and a caller cannot get the tile without the bound.

`StatTile` takes **three named constructors rather than parameters**, because the tiers differ in which fields even exist: `.small` is the only one with an icon, `.medium` the only one with tabular figures, `.large` the only one with a label-trailing slot. A single constructor would have carried four fields that are meaningless on two of the three tiers, which is the god-widget the twelve near-copies were the other end of. Standardising the hero tier on `headlineMedium` (four of six sites) over `headlineSmall` and on `bodySmall` (four of six) over `labelSmall` makes the two public share pages' numbers visibly larger; that is the intended outcome of having one ramp, and the FittedBox they gain makes it safe. Muted text takes `onSurfaceVariant`: writing a **new** shared primitive against `colorScheme.outline` would have baked § 505's 4.058:1 finding into the widget nine call sites now depend on.

**§ 502's `_StatSmall` + `_StatGrid` were adopted, not merely moved.** They were already the right answer for run detail, and the derivation `_kStatCellMinWidth` records — a paced secondary value needs ~64 dp at the 14 sp body size, so 72 leaves the value whole and lets only the label truncate — travelled into ui_kit with the constant rather than being re-guessed. Its reflow behaviour and the four tests that pin it are unchanged; per § 500 the ui_kit tests assert only *derivations* (a cell grew by the factor the glyphs did; every cell cleared the declared floor), never that some string fits some width.

The header half was **two kinds wearing one name**, not three copies. `settings_screen` and `route_picker_screen` had the same uppercased `labelSmall` list-group eyebrow (differing only in letter-spacing and weight) and take ui_kit's `SectionHeader`, which carries no padding of its own because a list group's inset belongs to the list. `dashboard_screen`'s is a `titleMedium` **section title** — a heading, not an eyebrow — and stays: folding it in needs a kind flag, and `ChartCardHeader` (§ 505) is a third thing again, the chart-card title with a note slot. The audit's "~69 files inlining `titleMedium.copyWith` for the same purpose" is wrong by an order of magnitude in the direction that matters: **21 occurrences across 12 files** use that form at all, and they are page and card headings, not section eyebrows.

**The two week ribbons are not duplicates, and the part that was duplicated was the header.** `this_week_strip` and `current_week_strip` differ in their data contract (the real calendar week's activities vs. the plan's `start_date + week_index*7` bucket of planned workouts) *and* in every mark they draw (a distance-scaled fill lane per day vs. a workout-kind card with a left accent and a completion check). Consolidating them would delete a feature. What was genuinely duplicated is the title-plus-count header: `ThisWeekStrip` already used `ChartCardHeader`, `CurrentWeekStrip` hand-rolled a `titleSmall` + `bodySmall` `Row`, and it now takes the shared header — which incidentally moves its counter off `colorScheme.outline` and lets the counter drop to its own line instead of the title ellipsising. Its test asserted eight `Expanded` (seven day cells plus the header's bounded title); a `Wrap` header contributes none, so the assertion now says seven, which is what it always meant.

Enforcement is `apps/mobile_android/test/stat_tile_guard_test.dart` (both twins), proved to fire on all four of its rules: the set of stat-named `StatelessWidget`s under `lib/` is closed against a map whose *values are the reasons* the four residual non-tiles are not tiles; the seven migrated surfaces must go on referencing `StatTile`, so adoption cannot be undone one screen at a time; the `_SectionHeader` set is closed the same way; and `StatTile` / `StatGrid` / `SectionHeader` may not be redeclared locally, since a local shadow would satisfy every other rule while reopening the drift. **Deliberately left, with reasons in the guard:** `_PeriodStatCard` and recap's `_StatCard` (label *above* the value, inside a `Card`, one of them with two sub-detail lines and a tap target), `feed_screen`'s `_Stat` (start-aligned with an uppercased label — the feed card's grammar), `route_share_card`'s `_Stat` (a rasterised share card on a fixed dark canvas, § 482's theme-free exemption), and the streak card's and gym-exercise screen's inline hero numbers, which paint the value in a semantic colour beside a baseline icon and so are not a value-over-label pair at all.

## 510. `colorScheme.outline` is a boundary, muted type is `onSurfaceVariant`, and a boundary token has no headroom to be thinned

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 closed the class §505 left open with numbers, and re-measuring moved the numbers in both directions. **Re-derived on `main` at 7d240a0fc: 322 occurrences of `colorScheme.outline` across 66 files** under `apps/mobile_android/lib`, not 325 — the file count was exactly right, the occurrence count three high (`colorScheme.outline` unbounded, which also catches `outlineVariant`, gives 328; word-bounded gives 322). The **58** single-expression `?.copyWith(color: … .colorScheme.outline)` sites were exact. `packages/ui_kit` held **three** more that §505's count had not looked at, one of them text. The 325/66 pair is internally inconsistent: 66 files is exactly right for the mobile package alone, whose occurrence count is 322 — and 325 happens to be mobile plus ui_kit, which is the wrong sum for the stated scope and the right one for the scope the guard now uses.

**The classification, not a regex.** Each site was decided by its innermost *enclosing* constructor: **218** sit directly inside a `TextStyle` / `TextTheme.<style>?.copyWith|apply|merge`, **80** inside an `Icon` / `IconButton`, **4** inside a `BorderSide`, **2** inside a `BoxDecoration`, and **18** had no enclosing constructor at all — a colour held in a local, returned from a `_kindColor` helper, or produced by a `switch` arm. Reading each of those eighteen found **17 that reach a `TextStyle`** and one that reaches only an `Icon`, so **235 moved and 87 stayed** in the mobile package, plus one moved and two stayed in `ui_kit`. After the thinning pass below converted five more marks onto the line token, **84 `outline` marks survive** across both — every one an icon, a border, a divider or a fill. The derived group is the part a regex could never have got: `workout_review_section`'s `final muted`, `readiness_card`'s neutral rung beside `semantic.success`/`danger`, `live_spectator`'s badge tuple, `gym_detail`'s visibility chip and the plan surfaces' `_kindColor` all painted type through a variable.

**The rule for icons is that there is no rule to make.** WCAG 1.4.11 sets one floor, 3:1, for a meaningful mark and a decorative one alike; the decorative/meaningful split changes only whether 1.1.1 owes it a label, which is a different guard. So no icon was spared on the grounds of being decorative — every surviving `outline` mark was checked against the fills it actually lands on (card, scaffold, the three `surfaceContainer` steps: 4.058 / 4.058 / 3.486 / 3.659 / 3.864 light, 5.117 / 6.009 / 3.890 / 4.551 / 5.169 dark) and clears 3:1 on all of them.

**The audit's headline number was right and its scope was too narrow.** `outline` is 4.058:1 on the light card, and it fails 4.5:1 on **every** light surface (down to 3.481:1 on `tertiaryContainer`) — but it reads **5.117:1 on the dark card**, so "outline fails as text" is false as stated. The honest claim, and the one the property test asserts, is that `outline` cannot be *relied* on as text while `onSurfaceVariant` can: 8.459:1 light card, 9.474:1 dark card, 11.125:1 dark scaffold, 7.267 / 7.627 / 8.055 on the container steps, and **5.465:1 on its worst real background** (dark `tertiaryContainer`, the fill a completed plan-calendar cell takes). §503's trap fired here as designed: three of the moved sites paint on a *tint of their own colour*, and measuring on the card would have hidden them — `onSurfaceVariant` on `onSurfaceVariant@12%` over the card is 6.995 / 7.282, and at 15% 6.656 / 6.763, against 3.544 / 4.310 and 3.422 / 4.110 for the `outline` they replaced. The swap repaired the tint case rather than merely the plain one.

**A second defect rode along, and it is the one §505 had already named.** Three of the moved sites were also *thinned*, so the swap alone would have left them failing: the dashboard goal placeholder at `× 0.6` is **3.054:1 light** even as `onSurfaceVariant`, and the plan-calendar out-of-month numeral was `× 0.4` **inside an `Opacity(0.55)`** — two multipliers compounding to **1.432:1 light / 1.675:1 dark**. Five more thinnings were on non-text marks and each was under 1.4.11's floor: the dashboard tappable-card chevron at `outline × 0.6` (**2.134 / 2.715**), its two card hairlines at `outline × 0.18` (**1.229 / 1.307**) and `primary × 0.25` (**1.585 / 1.668**), and the onboarding + setup-wizard pending dots and unselected card edges at `outline × 0.3` / `× 0.25` (**1.423 / 1.584** and **1.337 / 1.471**). The card edges take the line token §487 already holds at 3:1 (3.531 / 3.330); the tappable edge takes full `primary` (11.005 / 7.766) so the pair still reads apart, and colour is not its only cue because the chevron carries it too. The generalisation is that **a boundary token has no headroom at all**: its entire guarantee is a 3:1 floor, and 0.6 — the strongest multiplier anywhere in the tree — already spends it. That makes the ban absolute and allowlist-free for `outline`, `outlineVariant` and `dividerColor`, which is a stronger statement than §505's "compute the composited ratio", and it is why an `Opacity` widget counts as a multiplier too.

**Enforcement is a classifier pinned in both directions, not a ban.** `outline_text_token_guard_test.dart` (both twins) walks brackets backwards from each occurrence and takes the verdict of the innermost still-open one. That bracket-depth bookkeeping is the whole boundary between this and a backwards regex, so **24 fixtures** pin it — six must-flag (including a `Text` nested inside a filled `Container`, which its host must not spare), twelve must-spare (including a `Border.all` reached through a named factory, and an `Icon` that follows a *closed* `copyWith` in the same argument list), and six that must be refused. The thinning matcher carries its own nine (five must-flag across all three tokens and both the same-line and wrapped forms, four must-spare: two tokens with foreground headroom being tinted, and the two bare boundary reads that are the correct use). It was proved to fire four ways: deleting the depth bookkeeping flips one must-spare fixture to `mark` and another to `text`; reintroducing a text site in `lib` and one in `packages/ui_kit` each names its file and line; and dropping the derived allowlist entry fails with the count. A third verdict — `derived`, failing unless count-pinned per file on §480's model — is deliberate rather than a gap: the seventeen text-bearing locals prove syntax cannot decide them, and a guard that silently spared them would have been the more dangerous artefact. Comments and string literals are blanked to spaces before scanning, offsets preserved so line numbers survive; `chart_card_header.dart`'s own header explains why it does *not* use `outline` and would otherwise have been reported for saying so.

**§505's scope hole is closed, and closing it needed no allowlist.** `status_color_literal_guard_test.dart` walked `Directory('lib')`, so relocating two palettes into `packages/ui_kit/lib/src/theme/chart_palette.dart` took their hexes out of the ban's reach *without changing the allowlist* — a file that is no longer scanned needs no exemption, which is exactly why the omission was invisible. It now scans `lib` + `packages/ui_kit/lib`, and the allowlist **did not grow**: measured against the ban list, none of `chart_palette`'s per-brightness hues is one of the enumerated Tailwind/Material status literals, so a count-pinned entry there would match nothing and the guard's own "expects N but found none — remove it" rule would reject it. The finding's suggestion to add one was wrong for a good reason, and the "can only shrink" property survives intact. `ui_kit` is the only shared package carrying colour at all; the other four hold no `Color`. Proved by planting `0xFFEF4444` in `chart_palette.dart` and `Colors.green` in `run_map.dart`.

**Left open with numbers.** (1) The plan surfaces' out-of-month `Opacity(0.55)` survives, so that day numeral reads **2.732:1 light / 3.831:1 dark** even at full `onSurfaceVariant` — better than the 1.432:1 it was, still under AA. 1.4.3's "incidental" exemption covers an inactive component, and an out-of-month cell *with a workout* is wrapped in an `InkWell`, so it is not covered; unwinding an `Opacity` that dims a whole cell is a layout change on a plan surface, not a token change. (2) The workout-kind palette that `plan_calendar` and `current_week_strip` share is a seven-entry categorical scale of *hardcoded literals* used as label text, none of them on §480's ban list and none ever measured: tempo `#C98ECF` is **2.300:1**, interval/walk-run `#D97A54` **2.767:1** and marathon-pace `#E6A96B` **1.852:1** on the light card (6.353 / 5.282 / 7.891 dark — the light theme is the whole failure). That is §495's per-brightness data-palette problem in a surface the chart work never reached. (3) **31** sites still thin a non-boundary theme token (`primary` at 0.06–0.6, `onSurface` at 0.4, `primaryContainer` at 0.4–0.5); most look decorative but none is measured.

## 511. Web gets mobile's count-pinned status-hex guard, and the frozen FILL turns out to be the commoner defect

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§506 left this open with numbers and they reproduce exactly: **453** six-digit hex literals across **72** files in `apps/web/src` (`.svelte` + `.css`), with no web equivalent of mobile's `status_color_literal_guard_test.dart`. The breakdown the audit never gave is what made the item tractable: **9** live only in comments (contrast notes citing their own measured hexes — documentation, and a guard that flags those pushes a future editor toward deleting the reasoning), **125** are the `app.css` custom-property declarations that are the vocabulary's one legitimate home, and of the remaining **318** only **141** were even a status hue. **99** occurrences were swept across 37 now-clean files, leaving 354/35; **48** banned-hue occurrences across 21 files are allowlisted, each entry naming a reason.

**The frozen fill, not the frozen ink, was the defect.** §503 measured foregrounds; the pattern that actually dominated here is a status *chip* whose fill is a pale Tailwind literal. A confidence chip's `#d1fae5` reads **14.253:1 against the dark card it sits on** — a mint panel blazing on dark purple — while its own `#047857` ink was a respectable 4.835:1, so a fix justified on foreground contrast alone would have graded that chip as fine and left it. Ten such chips took the `-light` fill + `-text` ink pair (worst case 4.454:1, both themes). The genuinely-failing foregrounds were elsewhere and were repetitive: one `.error-banner .material-symbols { color: #ef4444 }` copied onto **26** surfaces, below AA in three of four theme/surface combinations (3.402:1 on the light page, 4.295:1 on the dark card), now 5.664–7.719:1 on `--color-danger-text`. The worst measured were the star/crown golds §495 had lifted without reaching their siblings: `#facc15` at **1.531:1** as an icon on the light card, under even the 3:1 non-text floor, plus `#fbbf24` 1.669, `#eab308` 1.918, `#f5b30a` 1.853 — twelve rules onto `--color-crown` (6.239 light / 8.963 dark).

**The single highest-traffic finding is in `app.css` itself, and it is §506's own token going unused at its most important call site.** The shared `.btn-primary` rule paired a frozen `color: #FFFFFF` with a `--color-primary` fill that flips from dark teal to light coral, so the app's primary button drew **2.081:1** label text in one of two themes; `--color-on-primary`, minted by §506 for exactly this, reads 9.120:1. It survived because §506 hunted the `var(--color-on-primary, #fff)` *spelling* — the bare literal was invisible to a var()-shaped guard. That is why this guard exempts app.css *declaration lines* rather than the whole file.

The allowlist is §480's shape — file → hex → exact count, so a new literal in an exempted file still fails and a migrated palette forces its entry's removal — over three exemption classes: app.css declarations, data palettes (badge tier metals, medal metals, workout-kind tints, chart-series gradients, cartographic markers), and **fixed canvases that never follow the device theme** (the `@media print` sheet, where a token would resolve to the *screen* theme and print dark-on-dark; and the race-day brand hero). Two entries carry numbers rather than a promise. The print sheet's amber was deepened from `#b26a00` (4.238:1 on paper, under AA) to `#9E5C00` (5.270:1) — a fixed canvas exempts a literal from *theming*, not from contrast. And a gold star over a **fixed** 0.65-black scrim keeps `#fbbf24`, because `--color-crown` is deliberately the dark gold for light surfaces and would read **1.123:1** there against 4.196:1 for the literal: the naive token swap is 3.7x worse, which is §503's "measure it where it lands" pointing the other way for once.

**Then the same one-character lesson recurred one level down.** §506 ruled that a fallback on a *declared* token stays legal, being the documented default for a per-instance component custom property (`style:--x={...}`). That rationale does not survive the token being **global**: nothing sets `--color-primary` per instance, so the fallback can never apply, and all **25** were frozen at values the tokens had long since moved off (`#4f46e5`/`#3b82f6`/`#2563eb` for a primary that is now teal, `#e5e7eb` for a cream border, `#374151` for near-black text). Dead code that reads as the colour at the call site is worse than no comment — the next editor believes the blue. So the line is **where** the token is declared, not whether a fallback is present. Deleting them uncovered a live violation the fallback had been hiding from `contrast_guard.test.ts`, whose deepest-chip-tint floor is **read out of the source**: `color-mix(… var(--color-danger, #d33) 22%, transparent)` never matched that read, concealing a `--color-danger-text` label at **4.250:1** on the block toggle's hover state. Both its tints now mix against an opaque `--color-surface` per §503, landing where they were measured (5.189 / 4.652:1 light, 5.419 / 4.717:1 dark). **The generalisation §506 drew about spellings holds for guards that derive their thresholds from source too: a floor read out of the tree inherits every blind spot of the pattern it reads with.**

**Left open, with numbers, so silence is not mistaken for coverage.** 172 literals across 29 files carry hues outside the declared status vocabulary and are untouched: 64 cartographic/MapLibre paint, 59 other paint (provider brand hues, Apple/Google button blacks, modality identity greens), 20 gradient stops, 16 inline SVG art and brand logo marks, 12 identity-palette declarations. Three named items were measured and deliberately not fixed.
