The **landing page's four feature-icon accents** sit on a theme card and read 5.425 / 3.126 / 2.308 / 2.531:1 in light and 2.392 / 4.069 / 5.530 / 5.044:1 in dark — each fails in one theme — but only two of the four are status hues and the durable fix is to move the whole set onto the accent `-text` tokens, a design change to the marketing page. The **race-day hero** paints `color: white` at 2.803:1 on its own orange stop, three `.feasibility` inks at 2.295–3.572:1, and a toggle at 3.763:1 — a redesign of a fixed canvas, not a token routing. The **sidebar user-avatar** paints white on `--gradient-primary`, whose light-mode third stop and dark-mode first two stops give 2.081 / 2.153:1; that is §481's contrast-clamped-identity-avatar problem, and no hex swap fixes a gradient carrying a light stop. Also out of the ban's declared scope by construction: 67 three-digit shorthands and 232 `rgb()`/`rgba()` colour literals.

## 512. An auth-gated in-app page still emits the share canonical, and `seo.md`'s render map is now a guarded contract rather than prose

**Date:** 2026-08-05

`docs/features/seo.md` asserted that "Runs already carry this on `/runs/[id]` → `/share/run/[id]`", and `share/run/[id]/+page.svelte`'s own comment asserted the same fold from the other end ("so search engines fold the in-app `/runs/[id]` surface (which canonicals here) onto this single public page"). `/runs/[id]` had **no `<svelte:head>` at all** — no canonical, no meta, nothing. A fold claimed in two places and performed in none. The honest complication is that the obvious reading of the doc is also the wrong one: `/runs/[id]` sits behind the layout auth-gate, so a crawler never reaches it, which argues the canonical is *unnecessary* rather than that the doc was right.

It was resolved on consistency first and merit second. Three of the four folds the table already listed — `/routes/[id]`, `/u/[id]`, and (before this round) the run row's absence — sit behind exactly the same gate, and they emit anyway; only `/clubs/[slug]` and `/clubs/[slug]/events/[id]` are anon-reachable, because `isAnonAllowed` lets anon through to public clubs and their events. So "auth-gated therefore unnecessary" does not distinguish the run page from two siblings that already do it; adopting it would have meant deleting three rows and contradicting §205's design, not deleting one prose sentence. The merit case is separately sound and §508 supplied it: a signed-in non-owner now renders a public run there, so the in-app URL circulates the way a share URL does, and a canonical is the machine-readable statement of where the public home of that content is — read by link-preview fetchers, inherited free by any later prerendered or anon-reachable variant of the surface, and costing one `$derived` string with no data load. **The rule is now one rule: an in-app page with a public share twin emits the canonical, and reachability is not the test.**

The deliverable that matters more than the tag is the guard, because the render map is exactly the doc that goes stale invisibly — nothing about a route breaks when the doc stops describing it, and round 8 already found `/events/{id}` and `/notifications` named there as routes that did not exist. `seo_render_map_guard.test.ts` parses both of `seo.md`'s tables and holds three things: every backticked path in either table resolves to a real route; every canonical-consolidation row's in-app page actually emits a `<link rel="canonical">` built from a `build<X>ShareCanonical` (not hand-rolled, so the doc and the share page cannot disagree about the target); and — the direction that stops the table going stale by omission — no page may emit such a canonical without a row. It found a fourth defect on its first run: the map named `/learn/category/[c]` where the route's param is `[category]`. What it deliberately does **not** check is the `Mode` and `<head> owner` columns; whether a surface is prerendered or Lambda-SSR is not decidable from the route file (it depends on the CloudFront behaviours and the Lambda dispatcher), and a guard that guessed would force the doc to describe the code instead of the contract.

Two render-map corrections came out of the same pass and are recorded in the doc so a later round does not re-flatten them. The blanket "auth-gated, not indexed" row lumped `/clubs/*`, `/events/[id]`, `/live/[id]`, and `/recap/*` — all anon-reachable — in with `/dashboard` and `/settings`; those surfaces stay out of the index because they serve the empty shell and canonical elsewhere, not because a gate turns the crawler away. And `/share/session/[id]` + `/share/workout/[id]` were absent from the map entirely: they are real public routes with real inline heads, but no Lambda dispatches them, so in prod an unfurler gets the shell, they emit no canonical, and their in-app twins (`/sessions/[id]`, `/gym/[id]`) hand-roll a `location.origin` share URL rather than a builder. That is left open and named rather than silently fixed — finishing them is step 2 of *Adding a new indexable surface*, i.e. a `share_<x>_meta` builder plus a dispatcher branch, not a one-line canonical.

## 513. The web dashboard's calendar heatmap was retired on purpose, so the unmounted component is deleted — a live twin on the additive platform is not evidence of a canonical gap

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 set out to close a finding recorded after round 10: `CalendarHeatmap.svelte` was referenced only by `security_guards.test.ts`, sat on no route, and carried a hardcoded Tailwind indigo ramp (`#C7D2FE`..`#4F46E5`) tracking neither theme. Two readings were available. **Dead code**, so delete it on §492's `ElevationChart` precedent. Or **an unmounted feature**, since mobile ships the same 7 x 20 grid live in both twins (`_RunHeatmap`, painting §505's `ChartPalette.ramp`) — which would make it a §24 inversion, the additive platform carrying something the canonical one lacked, and the fix a mounting plus `--heat-*` tokens in lockstep with mobile.

The second reading was taken, built, and **wrong**. `git log -S` on the dashboard route settles it: `3c86b8fc3` (2026-05-16) replaced that card with the Training intensity card, and said why — presence-per-day *"duplicated what the Mileage chart + Streak stat already convey."* The component survived the removal; the decision did not survive the reading of it. So the honest conclusion is the first one after all, and it is now recorded rather than inferred: `CalendarHeatmap.svelte`, its `calendar_heatmap.ts` logic module and that module's test are **deleted**, along with the `--heat-*` tokens and the ramp lockstep the mount had justified. Mobile keeps `_RunHeatmap`: web is canonical for *what the product is*, and a platform may still decline a surface the other ships — §24 makes mobile additive, not obliged, and it does not run in reverse.

**A live twin on the additive platform is not evidence of a gap on the canonical one.** That inference is what made a deliberate product retirement look like drift, and it is the durable lesson: before mounting anything the canonical surface does not mount, read the history of the route that does not mount it. Two smaller rots came out with the component and are worth noting as the reason unmounted code is worth deleting rather than keeping: its tooltip carried a hardcoded English `"No run"` in a file the i18n sweep had otherwise finished, and it formatted dates through `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, ...)` under a comment claiming the runtime locale. Neither was reachable, so neither was ever wrong in production — and neither would have been caught by any guard, because the guard that read this file only checked its `role="img"`. That guard's heatmap clause is gone too; a component whose only reader is a test asserting it is accessible is a component with no users.

## 514. Undo is a DEFERRED mutation, not a compensated one — and it replaces the confirm rather than joining it

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 closed **U8**, the last unclosed HIGH-lineage box from the original UX audit. Round 4 shipped only its *retry* half (§484); the *undo* half never existed on either platform. Counted on `main` at 7d240a0fc: the single occurrence of "undo" in the web app was `routeNew.undo`, the route builder's local waypoint stack — editor state, not a committed mutation. Every destructive action was confirm-then-gone.

Three contracts were available and only one of them can be honest. A **compensating inverse** (re-insert the deleted row) mints a new server id, cannot restore children the delete cascaded, and cannot re-upload a Storage object's bytes — it hands back a *different* row while claiming otherwise, which is worse than offering nothing. A **soft delete** is the right shape for a *trash* feature but costs a `deleted_at` column on every adopting table, a read-path filter everywhere, and a retention story; it is scoped, not half-built. So undo is a **deferred commit**: the row leaves the caller's local list immediately (the action feels done) while the server mutation is *held* for the undo window, so `Undo` cancels a timer and **cannot fail** — nothing was ever destroyed while the offer stood. `core/undo_queue.ts` is the rune-free core (14 host tests), `stores/undo.svelte.ts` the reactive shell, `UndoBar.svelte` the surface. The queue has **one slot**: a second destruction commits the first rather than stacking bars whose ordering the user would have to reason about. Restore is a list *snapshot* put back, not an insert-at-index, so ordering survives, and a commit that later fails restores too — a list must never claim a row is gone while the server still holds it. The window also commits on client-side navigation (`beforeNavigate`, honouring the intent on a surface the user has left) and on `pagehide`, where the fetch may not survive a tab close; that failure direction is deliberate — the row reappears on the next load rather than being destroyed with no way back.

**Confirm and undo are alternatives, not partners.** §498 made destructive confirms consistent; a modal *followed by* an undo bar is two dismissals for one intent, and the modal is precisely what teaches a user to click through without reading. Three deletes moved to undo and **dropped their `ConfirmDialog`**: the `/nutrition` food-log entry (the app's most frequently deleted row, re-typed in seconds), the route condition report (one tap to re-file, author-or-owner scoped), and the run comment/reply. The comment case applies one behaviour to both the author's own delete and the run owner's *moderation* delete — with the mutation deferred the actor can put it back untouched, which is more than the modal offered once dismissed, and a button that asks on some rows and not others reads as a bug; its optimistic filter drops the replies with the parent, mirroring the `parent_comment_id ON DELETE CASCADE`. Everything else keeps its confirm, for three stated reasons: the delete cascades something the actor could not reconstruct (a run and its track blob, a route, a club, an event, a plan, the account), the row is an authored reusable artefact rather than a line of data (a saved meal, a recipe, a gym routine, a session plan), or — the constraint the sweep discovered — **the affordance sits inside a `Modal`**, whose Tab trap makes an undo bar over it unreachable by keyboard. That last one is why the gear wear-log delete, which looked like an ideal candidate, was built and then reverted: an undo only mouse users can reach is not an undo.

**A timed undo is an accessibility surface, and pause-on-hover does not satisfy WCAG 2.2.1** (pause belongs to 2.2.2; 2.2.1 wants turn-off, adjust, or extend). The `undo_window_s` universal preference therefore carries a `0` = *no time limit* choice — the bar then waits for an explicit dismiss or a navigation — and an absent or corrupt bag value falls back to the 8 s default and **never to `0`**, so a garbage bag cannot silently pin every deletion open until the user navigates. Hover and focus additionally pause a running window. The offer is announced once through a `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` / `aria-atomic` region that is **always mounted** with only the bar conditional inside it — a live region that enters the DOM already carrying its content is not announced by most screen readers — and the countdown is deliberately kept out of that region, because a ticking number re-announces on every tick. Both bar buttons carry the 44 px tap-target floor, now policed by `comment-tap-targets.spec` alongside the row buttons that open the bar.

**Mobile gets none of this yet** and that is not drift to close first: web is canonical per §24, recording-side undo has no equivalent surface on the wrist, and the phone's `confirmDestructive` family (§498) stays as-is until a Dart twin of the queue is written.

## 515. A merge resolution is a code change, and the guards on the branch are what audit it

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 ran five agents into one branch and the integration step made two mistakes of its own, both caught by machinery rather than by reading. They are recorded because the round's other nine agents will keep producing the same collisions.

**A whole-file conflict resolution silently discards correct work.** Two Flutter agents legitimately edited six of the same files — one migrating private stat classes into ui_kit, the other recolouring muted type off `colorScheme.outline`. Git auto-merged most of it and conflicted only where one agent recoloured the body of a class the other deleted. Resolving with `git checkout --ours` on those *files* took each file wholesale from one side, throwing away the hunks git had already merged successfully elsewhere in them — a resolution that reads as correct in the conflicted region and is wrong twenty lines away. The other agent's brand-new `outline_text_token_guard_test.dart` failed with **13** surviving text sites, which is how it was found; the merge was rewound and redone hunk-scoped, keeping only the conflicted region's chosen side. **The mechanical rule: resolve inside the markers, never by taking a file.** The two agents had in fact converged — the new ui_kit primitives were already written against `onSurfaceVariant` precisely so §510's finding could not be baked into a widget nine call sites depend on — so the correct resolution preserved both intents, and the guard is what proved it.

**A pre-existing e2e spec is a recorded decision, and it outranks an agent's reading of the code.** The dashboard heatmap mount (§513) passed every check its author could run — full web unit suite, `svelte-check`, its own new Playwright spec — and failed CI on a spec that asserts the *absence* of the card it added, whose name says `replaces the old Activity heatmap`. Nothing in the component's source records why it was unmounted; only the route's history does. Two rounds running, the thing that caught a plausible-but-wrong change was a test written by someone who had already thought about it: round 10's `run-visibility-propagation-journey` had pinned a 404 as permanent and had to be corrected, and this round's `page.spec.ts` pinned a retirement and was right. The distinction is worth stating, because both look identical from inside the diff: **a spec that pins the absence of something is either a stale guard or the only surviving record of a decision, and only the history of the surface tells you which.**
## 516. The workout-kind palette becomes a measured `ChartPalette.kinds` scale that paints marks only, and the text guard grows from one token to every unmeasured colour source

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 of the #666 audit found the plan-calendar workout-kind palette and did not fix it. It was `static Color _kindColor(ThemeData, WorkoutKind)`, **duplicated byte-for-byte in `plan_calendar.dart` and `current_week_strip.dart`** — six `Color(0xFF…)` occurrences over **three distinct hexes** (`#C98ECF` tempo, `#D97A54` interval, `#E6A96B` marathon pace), not the seven round 11 reported. Web carried the *same three hexes in four more places* (`PlanCalendar.svelte`, `CurrentWeekStrip.svelte`, `/plans/[id]/+page.svelte`, `/plans/[id]/workouts/[wid]/+page.svelte`), so the palette had six homes and no owner.

**Round 11's ratios were measured against the wrong surface.** It reported tempo 2.300:1, interval 2.767:1 and marathon pace 1.852:1 — the ratios against the *card*. A day cell never paints on the card: it paints on `surfaceContainerHigh` or, when the workout is complete, on `tertiaryContainer`. Measured there the light figures are **1.973 / 2.373 / 1.589** and the dark ones **3.665 / 3.047 / 4.552**, not the 6.353 / 5.282 / 7.891 it quoted. The rule §503 already states — *measure on the surface the site actually paints* — was the thing that made the finding two-to-four times worse than reported.

**Three hues, two roles, and only one of them legitimate.** The colour was drawn as a 3 px cell edge (a mark: 1.4.11's 3:1) *and* as the colour of the uppercase kind label (type: 1.4.3's 4.5:1). Nothing measured either, because none of the hues is on §480's ban list — the palette was assembled out of brand tokens (`#D97A54` *is* `AppTheme.coralDeep` and web's `--color-secondary`; `#E6A96B` *is* `--color-warning`), plus `colorScheme.primary` for the long run and `theme.dividerColor` for the rest day. The rest label therefore painted in a §510 boundary token at **3.029:1** on the light completed-day fill, and the guard could not see it because a `switch` arm has no enclosing constructor to classify.

**The resolution: one measured scale, painting marks only.** `ChartPalette` gains a fourth scale, `kinds` — six entries, one per workout-kind group, per brightness, in `packages/ui_kit`. It is a **sibling of `series`, not more entries on it**: `series` means the three training-load curves and is pinned at three by the web lockstep, so overloading it would conflate two legends and break a guard in the other language's suite. Every entry clears **3:1 against every surface the edge is drawn against** — both cell fills, the card behind the grid gap, the scaffold, and web's plain surface and completed-day fill. Light, on the tightest of them (`tertiaryContainer`): **13.109 / 9.759 / 7.395 / 5.618 / 4.228 / 3.206**. Dark, same surface: **8.354 / 6.919 / 5.657 / 4.634 / 3.828 / 3.149**. The kind **label** moves to `colorScheme.onSurface` (13.663:1 worst light, 8.430:1 worst dark) and web's `--color-text`.

**A second, 4.5:1 twin scale was measured and rejected.** Keeping a tinted label would have needed six entries all clearing 4.5:1; on dark, white is only 9.324:1 against `tertiaryContainer`, so six rungs from 4.5:1 up can step at most **1.157** apart — six shades that are one shade in greyscale, which is the exact failure §495/§503's ladder exists to prevent. Six pairwise-3:1 marks do not exist either (five such steps need **243:1**, sRGB offers 21:1), so what is pinned between the entries is a monotone luminance ladder: **1.316 light, 1.207 dark**, against an achievable ceiling of `(9.324/3)^(1/5) = 1.255`. List order *is* the ladder, and its direction is hue temperature, not session prominence — §489 fixes which hues can occupy which end, and prominence is not what tells one kind from another.

**Kind identity never depended on hue after this, and demonstrably could not have before.** Nine kinds share six marks, so the hue alone cannot name a kind even with full colour vision. Every site already renders the localized kind word beside the mark (`workoutKindLabel`), and Flutter's semantics carry the full string even when the 1/7-width cell ellipsizes it, so the word is the identity channel and the hue is redundant reinforcement. Two widget tests per platform pin that the mark is the scale entry and the label is the text token, so the tint cannot come back.

**The out-of-month dim was destroying the floor it sat inside.** `plan_calendar` wrapped each cell in `Opacity(0.55)` and web in `opacity: 0.35`, which composites text *and* background: at 0.55 `onSurfaceVariant` falls to **2.582:1**, and at 0.35 web's `--color-text` falls from 14.283:1 to **2.051:1**. A cell carrying a planned session is content, not chrome, so the dim now applies only to empty cells. The residual — an *empty* out-of-month cell's day numeral, still dimmed — is a live finding, not a claim of correctness.

**The guard grew from one token to a family, because the class was never about `outline`.** §510's `outline_text_token_guard_test.dart` already classified each occurrence by its innermost enclosing constructor and distinguished text from mark, so it was widened rather than duplicated. It now scans three families in text position — the boundary tokens (`outline`, `outlineVariant`, `dividerColor`), the `ChartPalette` scales, and raw `Color(0x…)` literals — plus two rules the constructor walk cannot see: a **`foregroundColor:` argument** is matched by parameter name, because its enclosing `TextButton.styleFrom(` also takes a `backgroundColor` and so cannot decide (this caught two button labels on an unmeasured `#8B5CF6`, **3.828:1** on the light card); and a **`Color`-returning helper holding raw hexes** must be named in an allowlist with where its value lands, which is the round-12 shape exactly and forces a new palette into a measured home. Raw literals in text position are count-pinned per file, each entry naming the *fixed* surface that makes a fixed hex measurable at all — `#9CA3AF` at 7.677:1 on the share cards' `#0B0A1F` panel, `#1E293B` at 10.364:1 worst on a map-pin chip, `#0F172A` at 7.747:1 worst on the cluster disc. Six perturbations prove the six new rules fire, and the derived allowlists can only shrink.

**The lockstep lives in the other language's suite, by scale name.** `apps/web/src/lib/contrast_guard.test.ts` reads `chart_palette.dart` by scale name, so `--kind-1..6` ↔ `ChartPalette.kinds` is asserted from the web side, per brightness, alongside a source guard that fails any `color:` reading a per-kind custom property on any of the four web surfaces. Renaming the const list key was perturbed and fails there — the trap §515 recorded.

## 517. A `fontSize:` literal is a step spelled out by hand, and an alpha on a non-boundary token is a measurement nobody took

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 12 closed the two remainders §482 and §510 left, and both counts in the brief needed re-deriving.

**V11's remainder is 58, and 31 of the 58 were already exempt.** Measured on `main` at b4c015737, `apps/mobile_android/lib` carries **67** `fontSize:` sites: 58 numeric at ≥ 11, 7 numeric below it, and 2 non-numeric. The 58 was exact. What the brief did not know is that **31 of them were surfaces `AppTheme` deliberately does not reach** — the same classes §482 and §495 had already recorded, just never counted: the four fixed-canvas rasterisers that paint hardcoded hexes through a `RepaintBoundary` to a PNG (`finisher_certificate_card` 9, `run_share_card` 7, `route_share_card` 5, `period_summary`'s `_PeriodShareCard` 6, four of those below 11), the map overlay chips and pins §482 named (`run_detail`'s map-match pill, `routes_heatmap`'s cluster bubble, `live_run_map`'s two marker pins, `route_builder`'s waypoint pin), §497's two load-bearing graphics on the run screen (the Start circle inside `BoxFit.scaleDown`, the 200 px countdown numeral), and `main.dart`'s `ErrorWidget.builder`, which is installed before any `MaterialApp` and has no `Theme` to read a step from — the same reason the icon beside it already took `AppSemanticColors.dark` statically. **So 27 were real, and all 27 moved.** The 7 sub-11 sites are all inside that exempt set and none has stopped being exempt.

**The exception the classifier exists for is not a screen, it is an argument.** `IdentityAvatar.fontSize` is a *graphic* dimension — the widget's own default is `size * 0.42` and §497 wrapped the glyph in `BoxFit.scaleDown` — so a `fontSize:` there is not on the type scale at all, and two of its three call sites were re-deriving that default by hand (56 → 24, 32 → 14). The guard classifies by innermost enclosing constructor rather than banning the token, exactly as §510's does. Correction to §497: `event_detail_screen`'s `fontSize: 10` was described there as "a real clip fixed at the root for every avatar in the app", which fixed the *clip* — the literal itself survived, and it is this class, not an oversight.

**The literal that mattered most was 13, and 13 is not a step.** `AppTheme`'s `textTheme` overrides only `labelSmall`; the rest resolves Material 3's steps, so the legal sizes are 11 / 12 / 14 / 16 / 22 / 24 and up. Eight of the 27 wrote 13 — between `bodySmall` and `bodyMedium` — and the rule taken is that **a between-steps value snaps upward**, never down: shrinking type to reach a step is a legibility regression dressed as a cleanup. Two derived facts decided the *form* of each fix rather than its size. First, `ThemeData.textTheme` read straight off `AppTheme.light` carries **no geometry whatsoever** — Material applies the locale's geometry in `ThemeData.localize` at build time — so the scale can only be pinned inside a pumped tree, and a test that reads the getter compares nulls and passes for the wrong reason. Second, the M3 geometry styles are `inherit: false`, so naming a step *replaces* the ambient style instead of merging into it; that is safe only because every step already carries `onSurface`, and it is why a host that supplies its own foreground (a `FilledButton`, a `TextButton`) has its `fontSize:` **deleted** rather than replaced — naming `titleMedium` on a button label would have repainted it `onSurface` over a dusk fill. `type_scale_test.dart` pins both facts alongside the steps and the ambient defaults the deletions rely on. It also caught one worth recording: §482's `chipTheme.labelStyle` exists only to carry the selected/unselected `WidgetStateColor`, and `RawChip` resolves `chipTheme.labelStyle ?? chipDefaults.labelStyle` — an OR, not a merge — so a chip label has **no size of its own** and falls through to the ambient step, which is the same 14 by coincidence rather than by design.

**§510's "31 sites thin a non-boundary token" is not reproducible, and the real figure is 35.** Its own enumeration (`primary` 0.06–0.6, `onSurface` 0.4, `primaryContainer` 0.4–0.5) gives **19** at b4c015737 and **21** at 7d240a0fc; every non-boundary `colorScheme.*` thinning gives **34** and **45**; subtracting the nine `outline` thinnings that round removed gives 36, not 31. No shape reproduces 31 at either commit. The honest set — every alpha on a theme token that is not one of the three §510 bans — is **35**: the 34 reached through `colorScheme` plus one reached through a local `scheme` alias in `safety_nudge_banner`, which is how that site escaped §510's count in the first place and why the register's matcher accepts both spellings.

**Eight of the 35 failed, and the classification is by what the pixel *is*, not by how decorative it looks.** Text owes 4.5:1 composited, an icon or border or any meaning-carrying mark owes 3:1 composited, a wash owes nothing but is recorded. §503's trap fired on six of them, which stack a tint on an already-tinted parent: measuring on the plain page reports them passing. The failures: the dashboard coach-card subtitle at `onPrimaryContainer × 0.8`, **4.470:1 light** — under AA by a margin no eye catches, which is why it shipped, and 5.276:1 in dark so only one brightness ever failed; four container boundaries that were the only thing separating a panel from its page, since each panel's own fill composites to 1.06–1.26:1 and is simply invisible (`missing_map_tiles_hint`'s `error × 0.3` at **1.402 / 1.493**, the run screen's `_FirstRunPrompt` at `primary × 0.18`, **1.371 / 1.423**, and both create-plan cards at `primary × 0.4`, **2.149 / 2.318**); the last-run placeholder's only content, an icon at `primary × 0.6`, **3.148 light / 2.847 dark** — passing in light and failing in dark, the opposite way round from §510's `outline` finding; the elevation chart's scrub crosshair at `onSurface × 0.4`, **2.421** over the faintest band it crosses; the calorie goal line at `secondary × 0.7`, **2.006**; and the calorie-trend bars' not-today hue at `primary × 0.45`, **2.350 / 2.384**. Each border and icon took its token at full strength (3.271–10.337); the two chart marks did not, for the reason below.

**The generalisation is that un-thinning is not always the fix.** `colorScheme.secondary` is coralDeep on parchment and reads **2.767:1 on the light card at full strength**, so dropping the goal line's alpha would have left a 1.4.11 mark failing — the defect was the *token choice*, and the line took `outline`, the 3:1 mark token §510 left for exactly this (4.058 / 5.117). The calorie bars are the §495 case one level down: both hues now clear 3:1 against their card (9.454 / 5.903 and 3.486 / 3.890) but are only 2.712 / 1.518 apart from each other, and pairwise 3:1 between series is arithmetically unreachable once each also owes 3:1 to its surface — so the today/not-today distinction moved onto the weekday label's weight, a non-colour cue, rather than onto a third bespoke hue.

**A fill whose presence is a state signal is not a wash, and four of them were relying on the tint alone.** At 1.00–1.26:1 against the untinted neighbour the tint cannot be the cue, so 1.4.1 needs one beside it. Two already had one and are recorded as passing (`runs_screen`'s multi-select forks `check_circle` / `radio_button_unchecked` and carries `Semantics(selected:)`; `profile_screen`'s grouped notification row carries an unread-count badge). The single notification row had **nothing** — its own grouped sibling twenty lines below had the badge — and took the dot, reusing the existing `profileNotifUnread` string so no ARB moved. Two are **left open with numbers**: `plan_detail`'s "today" workout row (`primaryContainer × 0.5`, 1.003 / 1.140) and `segments_panel`'s viewer row (1.076 / 1.017) each have no in-row cue at all, and the honest fix is a marker or a label, not a stronger tint.

**The remaining 26 are a register, not an allowlist.** `thinned_token_register_test.dart` (both twins) count-pins them per file with the role and the number, so a *new* alpha anywhere fails until somebody measures it, and a migrated file forces its entry's removal. Two sub-findings came out of writing it. The nine `surface × 0.85–0.95` panels over the live map have **no deterministic background at all**, so the honest floor is checked against the extremes a tile can be — white and black — which bounds every tile between them (type reads 9.165–14.272, the live-share pill's `success` label 4.839 / 6.397). And `gym_execution_band` looks identical to `workout_execution_band` but is *not* an overlay: it sits on the page, where in dark a `surface × 0.95` fill is a **lighter** panel on a **darker** scaffold (1.163:1), so its `dividerColor` border carries the whole separation. The two are measured separately for that reason.

**§510's deferral of the plan calendar rested on a false premise, and the item had a sibling.** It recorded the out-of-month `Opacity(0.55)` as "a layout change on a plan surface, not a token change". `Opacity` has **no layout effect at all** — it sizes and positions its child exactly as if absent and composites the layer afterwards — so the fix was always a constant. Its figures also need correcting: measured on the fills a cell really takes rather than on the bare page, the day numeral read **2.511:1 light** (completed cell) and **2.909:1 dark**, not 2.732 / 3.831. What is true, and is the durable rule, is that **an `Opacity` around a subtree containing text is a contrast multiplier on that text, so its value is bounded above by 1.4.3 rather than chosen by taste** — and both the glyph and the fill behind it are inside the layer, so the pair must be measured *after* dimming. The retired-gear tile is the same defect at 0.65 (muted type **3.427:1 light**), and both subtrees wrap an `InkWell`, so 1.4.3's incidental-text exemption covers neither. One shared token, `AppTheme.dimmedSubtreeOpacity` at 0.85, clears every text pair on every fill either surface can take, in both brightnesses; the derived bound is **0.82** and the test computes it by stepping down rather than restating it, so the constant can neither drift stronger nor be left needlessly weak.

**One classifier gained a rule rather than an exemption.** Moving the crosshair onto `outline` made §510's guard report a `derived` occurrence, because the idiomatic `Paint()..color = …` cascade leaves `Paint(` already closed by the time the walk starts, so the enclosing bracket is the `canvas.drawLine(` call. The fix was to add the `Canvas.draw*` ops to the mark set — a colour handed to a draw call is a painted mark by construction — and deliberately **not** `drawParagraph`, whose colour always reaches the canvas through a `TextStyle` and is therefore decided by the inner host. The three source guards now share one scanner (`test/source_scan.dart`): the backwards bracket walk that decides which constructor encloses an occurrence is the load-bearing part of all of them, and a second copy is a second place for the depth bookkeeping to drift.

**Left open with numbers.** (1) The two state-carrying tints above (`plan_detail` 1.003 / 1.140, `segments_panel` 1.076 / 1.017) owe a non-colour cue. (2) `AppTheme`'s own component themes paint **coralDeep on parchment at 2.767:1** in two places nobody has recorded: the light `navigationBarTheme`'s selected icon and the `floatingActionButtonTheme`'s `parchment`-on-`coralDeep` pairing, both marks owing 3:1. It is the same number §510 flagged inside the workout-kind palette, so the token is the common cause and the palette work is the natural place to settle it. The rest of that bar measures clean and is recorded here so a later sweep does not re-derive it: light unselected label `haze` 5.102:1, dark unselected `parchment × 0.55` on midnight **5.709:1**, dark selected icon 9.120:1. (3) The `chipTheme.labelStyle` OR-not-merge above leaves every chip label sizeless; it lands on 14 by coincidence and would take a literal in `AppTheme` to fix properly, so it is pinned as an observed fact rather than repaired. (4) `activity_loader`'s `opacity: 0.5` calls are inside a drawn figure with no text and are outside the dimmed-subtree rule by construction.

## 518. Web's `--color-border` becomes the 3:1 line token and the fills move off it, because 551 of its 566 call sites were lines and 11 were tracks

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§511 recorded the numbers and they reproduce exactly: `--color-border` is **1.458:1** on the light card and **1.328:1** in dark, so web had no token that guaranteed a visible boundary at all while mobile's whole card/divider grammar rests on one (§487). Round 11 minted a `--heat-0` hairline for one surface as a stand-in and §513 then deleted that surface, so the gap was unmitigated. The brief's framing — that mobile keeps a *decorative* `dividerColor` beside a *structural* `outlineVariant` — is wrong and worth correcting: §487 pinned `parchmentLine` **simultaneously** as `dividerColor`, `dividerTheme.color` *and* a `colorScheme.outlineVariant` override, which is exactly why 105 sites moved without a call-site edit. Mobile has one line token, not two, and the web answer had to be one as well.

**The classification is line-vs-fill, not decorative-vs-structural, and the property decides it.** Enumerated on `main` at `b4c015737`: **566** occurrences across **146** files. By the CSS property the value lands in — back-scanned to the nearest `;`/`{` rather than matched at line start, which is what the 12-occurrence discrepancy between the two counting methods was — **397** `border`, **63** `border-bottom`, **45** `border-top`, **18** `border-color`, 12 logical/`-color` longhands, **16** `background`, **2** `stroke`, one `--sidebar-border` alias, one `--chip-bg` alias, three quoted JS map values, and three inside a `color-mix`/comment run. Reading the sixteen `background` sites one at a time split them cleanly and *not* along the property: **eight are lines drawn as a fill** — three `.key-stats` grids whose 1px `gap` shows the parent colour through, `.action-divider`, `.popover-divider`, `.or-rule::after`, `.timeline::before`, and `SplitPane`'s 6px drag handle — and **eight are genuine fills**: five progress-bar tracks, an inactive `ConsistencyCard` week cell, the `.race-unverified` chip, and a skeleton shimmer stop. So `background` had to stay out of the ban in *both* directions, and a regex over properties alone would have moved eight dividers onto a fill token.

Given 551 lines against 15 non-lines, the token keeps its name and its job: **`--color-border` becomes the line token** at mobile's `parchmentLine` `#8A806A` / `duskLine` `#786A9A` — web's light surfaces *are* mobile's (`parchment` = `--color-bg`, `parchmentDim` = `--color-bg-tertiary`, `duskDeep` = `--color-surface`, `midnight` = `--color-bg`), so the values transfer and bring a cross-platform lockstep with them: **3.906 / 3.531 / 3.313 / 3.112** light and **3.330 / 3.911 / 4.068** dark, every one over 3:1. Minting a second token instead would have meant 551 call-site edits *and* left the default fail-open, so a future `border: 1px solid var(--color-border)` would have been wrong by construction. The 15 non-lines move to **`--color-fill-subtle`**, holding the exact value `--color-border` shipped with, so nothing that was a fill moved a pixel. That is §503's rule one role over: **a border token is a line or a fill, never both.**

**Three classes fell out that the brief did not anticipate, and one of them inverts.** (1) **Text.** Three `kindColor`/`KIND_COLOR` maps carried `rest: 'var(--color-border)'`, and the consumer applied that string to a 3px `border-inline-start` *and* to the label's `color:` — one entry serving as a boundary and as type at once, which is §510's "derived" verdict on the web side. As text it read **1.458 / 1.328:1**; raising the token would have left it at **3.906 / 3.330**, still under AA, so it takes `--color-text-tertiary` (**5.782 / 5.510**). Mobile's `_kindColor` still returns `theme.dividerColor` for the same arm at 3.531:1, which §510's open item (2) already owns; the divergence is upward and deliberate. (2) **Decorative.** The two chart gridlines are the one class honestly below the floor — a gridline is reference ornament inside a graphic, not a component edge — so they take the fill token, `ElevationProfile`'s `opacity: 0.5` on top of it is left alone (1.200:1, unchanged), and `stroke` is therefore excluded from the ban rather than silently failing. (3) **Inverting.** `/runs/[id]`'s `.match-pill` sits on a *fixed* `rgba(20,22,38,0.78)` scrim over the basemap: the old value read **6.084:1** there and the new one reads **2.366:1**, so the raise makes it worse. Its label was independently broken at **1.402:1** (`--color-text-secondary` on a near-black pill in light mode). Both foregrounds are now fixed literals measured against the worst composite — the scrim over a white tile — at 8.022 and 4.111:1. §511's "the naive token swap is 3.7x worse" pointing the other way, found by looking at what each border actually lands on rather than at the border itself.

**Enforcement is the property boundary, pinned both ways.** Six additions to `contrast_guard.test.ts`: the 3:1 floor per theme against every surface token; the `parchmentLine`/`duskLine` lockstep read out of `app_theme.dart`; `--chip-fg` on `--chip-bg` at AA (the fill token's own contract, 10.831 / 11.005); and three source scans — a fill token may not draw a `border`/`border-*`/`outline`, the line token may not paint text, and it may not be thinned toward `transparent` or a surface token. The thinning ban had to spare the **19** `color-mix(<accent> N%, var(--color-border))` borders, and the reason it can is measurable: an accent mixed into the line moves contrast **up** in both themes, because the accent is darker than the line in light and lighter in dark. Proved by six planted violations, each naming its file and line, plus a divergent-but-*passing* dark value that fails only the lockstep. `--sidebar-border`'s dark override, a `rgba(247,243,236,0.08)` at **1.170–1.220:1** over the sidebar gradient, is deleted so the nav rail's edge follows the token (**3.669–4.068**).

**Left open with numbers.** The line token clears 3:1 on every plain surface but **not** on eight dark tinted-gradient cards: on `color-mix(--color-primary 12–14%, --color-surface)` it reads **2.551–2.998:1**, because dark `--color-primary` is a light coral that pulls the card *toward* the line. It was 1.017–1.195 before, so the change is a 2.1–2.5x improvement in the worst place, and no single dark value fixes both — going lighter loses the plain card, going darker loses the tint, and mobile is under the same squeeze. Second, `--color-fill-subtle` sits at **1.162–1.622:1** against the surfaces it lands on, so five progress-bar tracks are invisible as *shapes*; that is deliberate rather than deferred — a progress bar is identified by the fill inside it, not by its own edge, and the guard says so instead of asserting a floor it does not intend to hold. Third, the twelve raw-hex borders in the tree are all cartographic, brand-button or print-sheet, so a "no hex in a border" rule would need a twelve-entry allowlist duplicating §511's; it is not added.

## 519. Three surfaces §511 measured and dropped, re-measured: two of the three figure sets moved, and the sidebar avatar's fix was already written on the other platform

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§511 left three surfaces "measured and deliberately not fixed". Re-measuring first was the right order, because **two of the three sets of numbers did not survive it.**

**Landing feature icons — reproduced, and §511 measured on the right surface.** The four accents read **5.414 / 3.120 / 2.309 / 2.533:1** light and **2.386 / 4.082 / 5.543 / 5.045:1** dark on the 10% tint each paints over the card, against §511's 5.425 / 3.126 / 2.308 / 2.531 and 2.392 / 4.069 / 5.530 / 5.044 — the same figures to within 0.02, the drift being 8-bit rounding of the composite. Each fails in exactly one theme, which is the whole point: a *fixed* hue cannot suit both a near-white and a dark-violet card, so fixing only the two that happened to be on the ban list would have left the other two broken and the guard silent about it. Each is now a base token's **12%** tint under its own theme-aware `-text` ink — the pairing the status chips already use, so both halves flip together — landing at **5.914 / 5.244 / 5.649 / 4.838** light and **6.205 / 5.971 / 6.565 / 6.054** dark. The four are chosen for spread rather than meaning, because colour carries nothing here: the icon, heading and body each say what the card is. Their two allowlist entries are gone, forced out by the guard's own "expects N but the file paints none" rule.

**Race-day hero — the pastels were measured on the wrong background, and the honest numbers are worse.** `color: white` at **2.803:1** on the orange stop is exact, and the toggle's 3.763:1 is its active label on a white pill. But the three `.feasibility` inks are **1.989–3.021:1**, not 2.295–3.572: the rule paints `background: rgba(255,255,255,0.15)`, and 2.295–3.572 is the pastels on the *bare* gradient. §503's trap sprung a third time, and it also means the `::before` dot — `currentColor`, so the same ink — was under the 3:1 non-text floor, which nobody had noticed. Two further defects were unreported: the toggle's `rgba(255,255,255,0.4)` edge at **1.494:1**, and `.check-detail`'s `opacity: 0.85` compositing to **3.693:1**. The gradient now runs between the two theme-**independent** `-strong` fills — which exist precisely as "dark enough for white text", are already AA-pinned there, and are *forbidden* a dark override — so white reads **5.420 / 5.841 / 6.056** across the ramp. The verdict pills stop being pale pastels on a translucent veil and become dark inks on one near-opaque white pill (**4.862 / 6.084 / 7.367** worst case), which collapses three per-verdict veils into one and removes an unreachable 3.802:1 unclassed state. **Inset sub-panels on a mid-tone canvas must be deeper than it, not lighter** — a light veil spends the only foreground's headroom, so 0.10–0.12 white left its own white text at **4.274–4.463** where 0.12 black gives **6.578**. The active label takes a fixed `#8F2F24` (8.077:1) chosen *not* to re-spell `--color-danger-strong`'s value, since a literal that duplicates a token is what the hex guard's token-value group exists to catch and a `-strong` token may not be a `color:`. Eight of nine allowlisted literals are gone; the survivor is the verdict green, at a count of two because the confidence chip and the feasibility pill are the same role on the same pill.

**Sidebar avatar — §511's figures are exact, and §481 had already written the fix.** White on `--gradient-primary` is **2.081 / 2.153:1** on its light-mode third stop and its two dark-mode stops. §511's conclusion that no hex swap fixes a gradient carrying a light stop is right, and the generalisation is that **a gradient needs its own foreground contract**: the disc takes a two-stop `--gradient-avatar` built from token pairs that flip *together* with `--color-on-primary`, so one declaration resolves per theme (white on `#2C5F6E`/`#A24A2C` = 7.073/5.912; `#120D22` on `#F2A07B`/`#B9A7E8` = 9.120/8.818) and the guard resolves **every** stop rather than the pair it was written with. The unexamined half was worse: `Avatar`'s `seed` mode painted white on `hsl(hue, 50–55%, 55%)`, where a fixed white **fails AA on 297 of the 360 hues** and even picking the better of white-and-ink bottoms out at **3.975:1** across the magentas — so luminance-picking alone, which is how §481 is usually summarised, is necessary and *not sufficient*. Mobile's `identity_avatar.dart` already solved it and web now carries a faithful port: nudge the lightness out of the dead band one step at a time in the direction the better ink already favours, then pick the ink by computed contrast. Worst case over the whole wheel is **4.500:1**, and only **86** hues move at all, so legible avatars keep their historical colour. The port rounds to 8-bit channels before measuring because `HSLColor.toColor()` does and the loop exits a hair above the threshold — in float, a boundary hue stops one step early. The `sat` prop is deleted: its only effect was to break the guarantee. The hue **hash** stays divergent from mobile's (`| 0` here, `& 0x7fffffff` there), because each is pinned to its own history and changing either recolours every existing avatar — so the parity pair is the clamp, not the hash.

**One thing this round did that the previous two did not, and it is why the pastel regression is now caught twice.** The pastel arrived as a higher-specificity `.feasibility.feas-behind` override, and a source scan cannot tell which of two competing declarations wins. So the hero carries both a computed-contrast guard that derives its floor from the panel's own declarations — the stops must be the `-strong` pair, then every veil is composited over the **worst** stop *including the midpoint*, which neither end measures — and a Playwright assertion on the resolved `getComputedStyle` pair, which is the only place the cascade is actually run.

## 520. `/share/session` + `/share/workout` join the entity-SSR set, and a share route now has to prove all three of its wirings exist

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 11 recorded, in `seo.md` and in [§ 512](decisions.md), that
`/share/session/[id]` and `/share/workout/[id]` were share surfaces in name
only: real public routes with real inline `<svelte:head>`s, but no Lambda
dispatched them, no CloudFront behaviour pointed at one, and neither emitted a
canonical — so in production every crawler and chat-app unfurler got the empty
SPA shell, and a link pasted into Slack showed a bare URL. It could name the
gap but not close it in scope. Round 12 closes it along the whole path
`seo.md § Adding a new indexable surface` step 2 prescribes: a
`share_session_meta` / `share_workout_meta` builder pair (pure
`build<X>ShareTitle` / `Description` / `Canonical` / `JsonLd` +
`buildShare<X>Head` + `render<X>HeadTags`), two branches in the shared
`share-entity` dispatcher — which goes from four paths to six, still one
Lambda, still no rasteriser — and the two matching `/share/<x>/*` behaviours.

Three decisions inside it are worth the ink.

**The head goes English and unit-stable, replacing localized, viewer-reactive
strings.** Both pages built their `<title>` from `m()` and their
og:description from `formatWeight`, which reads the viewer's
`preferred_unit`. Under the dev-server path that made the unfurl a function of
*whose scraper touched the link first* — the same run of kilograms rendered
`lb` for one viewer and `kg` for another, and the title changed language. The
builders take the posture `share_meta.ts` has documented since the first share
page: canonical kg, UTC dates, English, assembled by hand rather than through a
locale tag. The visible page keeps its localized copy and its per-viewer weight
formatting; only the `<head>` is frozen. This is deliberately *not* an i18n
regression to be fixed later — a per-viewer OG tag is the bug.

**`WebPage` + `BreadcrumbList`, not `ExercisePlan`.** schema.org has a type
that looks made for a yoga sequence, and it is refused: `ExercisePlan`'s
supertype chain runs through `MedicalEntity`, so adopting it would publish a
person's training as medical structured data, and it describes a plan rather
than a performed session. `WebPage` + breadcrumb is what a recorded run
already uses for the same reason, and it keeps the two new surfaces consistent
with each other. Neither emits `primaryImageOfPage`: there is no per-entity OG
PNG here, and pointing that property at the brand card would misdescribe the
page.

**Neither surface is sitemap-enumerated**, unlike the four `share-entity`
siblings. A public gym workout is the athlete's own training record; listing
every one of them would build a crawlable training-log directory, which is the
objection that already keeps profiles out of the sitemap. Session plans are
held to the same line for now — link-discoverable, not crawl-enumerated. The
privacy floor underneath both is the redacted projection, not a filter written
here: a workout is read only through `public_gym_workouts` /
`public_gym_sets`, which omit `gym_workouts.notes` and per-set `rpe`
(migrations 20270313_001 / 20270327_001), and a plan's per-item `cue` /
`tempo` are rendered in the visible sequence but kept out of the head, because
an og:description reaches strangers out of context.

The in-app twins `/sessions/[id]` and `/gym/[id]` now emit a canonical onto
those share pages and build their copy-share-link from the *same* builder — on
`location.origin`, so a preview host still yields a preview link while the
path can never drift from the canonical's. That makes seven rows in the
canonical-consolidation table, and § 512's `seo_render_map_guard.test.ts`
proved its own worth by failing the moment the two pages started folding
without a row.

One guard is new, because the doc could only ever have caught half of this.
`share_entity_dispatch_guard.test.ts` cross-checks the three places that must
agree for a share route to unfurl in production — the route directory on disk,
the CloudFront `path_pattern`, and the dispatcher branch — plus that each
branch renders through a `build`/`render` pair rather than a hand-rolled
string, which would sidestep the escaping guard. Nothing breaks locally when
those drift: the dev server runs the `PageLoad` either way, so the page looks
finished while prod serves the shell. That asymmetry is the whole reason this
gap survived from the day both pages shipped until round 11 read the table
carefully.

## 521. An in-modal delete may offer undo — the focus trap widens to admit the bar, rather than the delete keeping its confirm

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§ 514 shipped the deferred-commit undo bar, adopted it on three deletes, and left two things open. Round 12 closed both.

**The four enumerated adoptions all belong to the undoable class, and all four landed.** The test § 514 set is whether the mutation can be *cancelled* rather than compensated, and whether the row comes back byte-identical — so a cascade, a Storage object, or a server-minted id disqualifies. None of the four has any of those. The **notification** dismiss is the strongest case in the app: the row is *system*-minted, so a stray tap was the one destruction the user could not undo by re-typing, and nothing hangs off it. The **route review** delete is scoped by `(route_id, user_id)` — the table's own unique key, not a passed id — with no children. The **route marker** delete removes one pin whose `position_m` is derived server-side, which survives precisely *because* the deferred delete never touches the row (a compensating re-insert would have had to re-derive it). The **gear wear-log** observation is one line of text its owner typed. Six confirm-dialog i18n keys across six locales became dead and were deleted; `deleteNotification`, the single-row helper, became dead and was deleted with them (every dismiss now batches through `deleteNotifications`, which the issue #350 N+1 guard follows into the shared `dismiss` helper).

**Bulk is one intent, so it is one slot — the queue needed no widening.** Dismissing a collapsed group of N notifications is a single user intent expressed once, so it gets one bar, one `commit` that deletes all N ids in one query, and one `restore` that puts the whole list snapshot back. § 514's one-slot rule is about *separate* intents (a second destruction commits the first), not about rows; reading it as a per-row rule is what makes bulk look like a contradiction. The alternative — coalescing two *separate* destructions into one bar so a rapid dismisser can undo both — was refused: "Undo" would then have to mean "undo both", a claim the user never made, and it would resurrect rows they deleted deliberately. What bulk *did* force was a correction to where the optimistic write goes. The unread badge is now decremented inside `commit`, not at defer time, because while the offer stands the rows are still on the server and still unread: the truthful count includes them, and an early decrement disagrees with every `refresh()` for the whole window — *indefinitely*, for a user on the `0` = no-time-limit setting. **The list is the optimistic surface; a server-sourced aggregate is not.**

**The in-modal question is answered by widening the trap, not by exempting the delete.** § 514 recorded that the gear wear-log undo was built and reverted because the affordance lives inside `Modal.svelte`, which traps Tab, leaving a fixed bar over it reachable by pointer alone. The trap itself is not the bug and cannot go: the page behind is still in the DOM (no `inert`), so without it a keyboard user tabs out of the last control into the obscured page. Three options were on the table — port the bar into the dialog's DOM, teach the trap to admit a designated region, or make "in-modal deletes keep their confirm" permanent. The third was rejected because the classification would then be driven by an implementation detail of the host widget rather than by whether the action is reversible, which is the only thing § 514's contract is about; the first was rejected because physically relocating a global singleton on modal open is fragile and would have to be undone on close. So: any rendered `[data-modal-trap-include]` host outside the dialog joins the ring, and `UndoBar`'s always-mounted region carries the attribute. Nothing pending means no focusables, so the ring is bit-for-bit the dialog's own whenever no offer stands — the change is inert until it is needed.

The WCAG reading matters, because the citation is not the obvious one. **2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) was never violated** and is not what this fixes: focus could always leave the dialog via Escape, and widening the ring does not change that exit. The violation was **2.1.1 (Keyboard)** — an operable control that no key sequence could reach. **2.4.3 (Focus Order)** is what dictates *where* in the ring the bar goes: the included focusables are appended **after** the dialog's own, because the offer is a consequence of the action the user just performed inside the dialog, and that ordering is written as an explicit `[...dialogRing, ...outerRing]` concatenation rather than left to DOM order — the region lives in the root layout, so a document-order ring would put the undo buttons before or after the dialog depending on nothing meaningful. Tabbing onto the bar also fires its `focusin`, which pauses the countdown, so arriving by keyboard does not cost the window (2.2.2), and `undo_window_s = 0` remains the 2.2.1 answer — which matters more here than anywhere else, since reaching this bar costs a keyboard user a Tab traverse of the whole dialog.

**The resolution is guarded, not commented.** `undo_modal_trap_guard.test.ts` pins the trap's include query, the exclusion of hosts already inside the dialog, the dialog-first ring order, and the attribute's placement on the always-mounted region rather than the conditional bar — plus, per surface, that each adopter defers and no longer carries the confirm state it replaced. A keyboard-only Playwright leg drives the whole gear flow with Tab and Enter and never clicks the bar. Two pre-existing specs had to be corrected rather than deleted, both § 515 cases. `markers.spec.ts`'s "delete-dialog cancel button is localized" is really a guard on `ConfirmDialog`'s *default* `cancelLabel` (a hardcoded English `Cancel` once leaked into every locale) that merely used the marker dialog as its vehicle; it was retargeted at the share confirm on the same page, which also omits the label. `review.spec.ts`'s "cancelling the delete confirm keeps the review" was pinning that one tap cannot lose the review — now Undo's job — and its replacement asserts the stronger property the confirm never offered: after Undo the server row carries the **same id**, because it was never touched.

**Mobile is still owed the whole feature** and this round widens the gap by four surfaces rather than closing it, which is correct under § 24: the queue's pure half is a clean parity-pair candidate, but the host is not — a `SnackBar`-with-action must survive a route pop, and Flutter has no `Modal` Tab trap to widen because it has no Tab.

## 522. A scale built to exactly meet a floor cannot survive a later alpha, and a broken merge seam in a guard file fails silently

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 12's five agents produced two integration findings that no single agent could have seen, both in the same file pair, and both only visible by *composing* two independently-correct changes.

**Two correct fixes were jointly wrong.** §516 gave the plan calendar a measured `ChartPalette.kinds` mark scale, sized so its quietest entry clears 1.4.11's 3:1 against the deepest fill a cell edge is drawn on — worst **3.206:1** light, **3.149:1** dark, i.e. no headroom by construction, because six categorical marks cannot be pairwise-separated *and* individually generous. §517, in the same file, replaced a per-site `Opacity(0.55)` with a shared `AppTheme.dimmedSubtreeOpacity = 0.85` whose bound it derived honestly against the pairs it could see (text at 8–13:1, which 0.85 barely touches). Composed, the dim lands on the mark: at 0.85 the quietest mark reads **2.944 / 2.944 / 2.697 / 2.584** on the four light fills — under 3:1 on **every** light fill — and 2.755 on the dark completed-day fill, five of eight brightness×fill combinations. Neither agent's tests could fail, because each measured its own change against the tree it branched from. The resolution splits the two branches by what they draw: a cell **carrying a workout** is never dimmed (it paints a mark with zero headroom), a cell **without** one keeps the 0.85 dim (it paints only a day numeral, which has 8:1 to spend). The general rule: **a floor met exactly is a floor that forbids every later multiplier**, so a scale's doc comment must say which of the two it is — generous enough to be dimmed, or exact and therefore load-bearing — and the guard should assert the exclusion is still *needed* rather than merely enforced, so the rule retires itself if the palette ever gains headroom. Both were added.

**The merge itself broke a guard file, and a guard file breaks quietly.** Resolving a conflict in `contrast_guard.test.ts` by keeping both agents' appended blocks cut a `for` loop mid-body, so esbuild refused the file and the runner reported one failing *file* rather than 53 failing assertions. The suite went from 3312 tests to 3259 and still read as "3258 pass, 1 fail" — a green-looking number that had silently stopped checking every colour ratio on web. §515 recorded that a merge resolution is a code change; this is its sharper form: **when the file you break is the thing that does the checking, the failure presents as one line of noise rather than as the defect it hides.** The tell is the *count*, not the status — a test total that drops after a merge is a merge that deleted checks. Compare totals across a merge, not just pass/fail.
## 523. Mobile undo hosts the offer in a root `Overlay`, not a `SnackBar` — because a barrier drops the snack bar out of the semantics tree, and because the queue must outlive the route

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§ 514 shipped deferred-commit undo on web and closed by saying mobile got none of it, "until a Dart twin of the queue is written". § 521 widened the gap by four surfaces and named the three things closing it would need: the twin, a `SnackBar`-with-action host that survives a route pop, and a mobile read of `undo_window_s`. Round 13 closed all three, and the middle one turned out to be the wrong shape.

**The queue is a clean parity pair; the host is not, and could not have been.** `undo_queue.dart` mirrors `core/undo_queue.ts` case for case — 14 host tests each, same fake clock, same properties: the mutation is HELD rather than performed and compensated, so undo cancels a timer and cannot fail; one slot, where a second destruction commits the first and disarms its timer; `restore` puts back a list *snapshot* so ordering survives; a commit that later fails restores **and** reports; `pause`/`resume` spend only the remaining time and keep the published `id` + `windowMs` stable. Web's `createUndoQueue(deps)` factory reads as a Dart `UndoQueue(UndoQueueDeps)` constructor, an idiomatic shape difference of the same kind § 278 already accepted for `password_change`'s union-vs-class. The Dart corrupt-value list also covers `8.5` and `true`, which JS's `typeof` + `Number.isFinite` gate rejects for free. The **hosts** share nothing: web's widens a Tab ring, and Flutter has no Tab ring.

**A `SnackBar` cannot host an undo offer on this platform, and the reason is measurable rather than aesthetic.** A snack bar is rendered inside its route's `Scaffold`. A modal route's barrier carries `BlockSemantics`, which drops every node painted before it in the same container — that is, the whole route beneath the dialog. Dumping `semanticsOwner.rootSemanticsNode` with a dialog up and a snack bar raised yields the barrier and the dialog and **nothing else**: not the snack bar, not the screen behind it. The snack bar is still *painted*, which is exactly what makes the trap subtle and why a widget-finder assertion would have passed. So TalkBack and VoiceOver can neither announce nor reach it — WCAG **2.1.1**, the same violation § 521 fixed on web by admitting the bar into the dialog's ring. An `Overlay.insert` entry, by contrast, lands above every entry currently in the overlay including the barrier, and `Navigator` only ever positions *route* entries relative to other routes' entries, so a manually-inserted top entry stays above a dialog pushed later too. Measured for a dialog, for a `showModalBottomSheet`, and in both orderings. The upshot is that the in-sheet gear wear-log delete — the one § 514 built and reverted, and § 521 had to widen the trap for — needs **no** mechanism of its own here. Both halves are pinned in `undo_bar_test.dart`, the negative one included, so a later round cannot "simplify" the host back into the dead end. There was a second, independent reason already on the record: `showSnackBar` and `ScaffoldMessenger.of(context)` have been banned in `lib/screens` / `lib/widgets` by an architecture guard since round 8, because Material's snack bar docks at the bottom where it covered the recording screen's Pause / Stop / Lap. Either reason alone is disqualifying. The brief's "`SnackBar`-with-action host" was therefore a correction, not a specification.

**A route pop does not flush, and that is the stronger reading of "the row must land, not vanish".** The queue is a top-level singleton and its `Timer` belongs to it, not to any `State`, so popping the surface the row was deleted from cannot cancel the pending commit — the mutation lands on its own schedule whether the user stays or not. Web flushes on `beforeNavigate` because its bar describes a list the user has left; here forcing an early commit would be the *only* way to lose the offer, so mobile deliberately diverges and lets the pill ride over the next screen. The cost is paid at the call site instead, and it is the same cost the deferred contract already implies: `commit` may not touch a `BuildContext` (anything localized is resolved at defer time and handed in as `message`), and `restore` must open with `if (!mounted) return;` because it runs on undo *and* on a commit failure, either of which can land after a pop. Every adopting list is rebuilt from the server or from the local store on its next load, so an undo whose surface has gone self-heals rather than desyncing. Both rules are enforced per call site by paren-matched source guards over every `DeferredDestruction(...)` literal, alongside a guard that the host still says `rootOverlay: true` and never `ScaffoldMessenger`, and one that the recording screen and account deletion keep confirm-then-gone. The one place mobile is weaker than web: when a commit fails *after* the user has navigated away, the failure banner is dropped rather than reported, because `onCommitError` is the call site's `showTopBanner` and that context is gone. Building a second global banner mechanism to close a case bounded by an 8-second window was refused; the restore itself is unaffected, since nothing was deleted.

**All seven of web's surfaces adopted, with the same classification and the same three disqualifiers.** Food-log entry, route condition report, run comment/reply, notification dismiss, route review, course marker, gear wear-log observation. Two took a shape web did not have. The **food entry**'s list is derived from `LocalFoodStore` rather than held in state, so its optimistic removal is a hidden-id set instead of a list snapshot — the stored row is not touched at all while the offer stands, which is a *stronger* form of the same contract: the entry returns bit for bit, pending sync state included, and a test asserts the stored map is unchanged. The **notification group** dismiss forced a real fix rather than a shaping choice: mobile had only a single-row `deleteNotification` and `_dismissGroup` looped it, so dismissing a collapsed group of N fanned out into N round-trips. It is now one batched `deleteNotifications(ids)` mirroring web's, and the single-row helper is gone. Per § 521, the unread badge is still not adjusted at defer time — while the offer stands the rows are on the server and still unread, so the truthful count includes them. Everything else keeps its confirm for § 514's three stated reasons, and `confirmDestructive` (§ 498) remains the shape for all of them.

**`undo_window_s` needed the editor on mobile, not just the read.** A consumer without an adjust route fails WCAG **2.2.1** outright: the `0` = *no time limit* choice is the "Turn off" mechanism, and a phone that can only read the key leaves the user racing a countdown they cannot switch off from the device they are holding. So Settings → Preferences carries the row beside dark mode, mirroring web's placement. The value is mirrored into `Preferences.undoWindowS` and persisted locally, so a pick honours the *next* deletion even while the bag write is queued and survives a cold start offline; `_RunAppState` forwards it into the host, keeping the dependency direction app → widget rather than putting a widget import in the preferences model. Fail-safe on both platforms: a **present-but-corrupt** value normalises to 8 s and never to `0`, while an **absent** key leaves a deliberate local choice alone rather than resetting it — the distinction matters because `_applyUniversal` runs on every sign-in. Mobile's pause trigger differs from web's for want of a hover: the window pauses while the app is not resumed, so an incoming call does not silently burn the offer down. The countdown is a `1 - controller.value` rule under `ExcludeSemantics`, kept out of the announced label for § 514's reason — a ticking number re-announces on every tick.

**Nine pre-existing tests had to be rewritten rather than deleted, and one had to be retargeted.** The confirm/cancel/confirm-deletes trios on nutrition, gear, run-social, route-review and route-markers were pinning the old shape and became the new one's tests. Two are § 515 cases. `route_detail_review_delete_test.dart`'s "cancelling the confirm dialog does not delete" was really guarding that one tap cannot lose the review — now Undo's job — and its replacement asserts the stronger property the confirm never offered: after Undo the server was never called, so the row keeps its own id. `nutrition_screen_test.dart`'s `#501` focus-leak test merely *used* the delete confirm as a vehicle for "a field-less surface following a dismissed name dialog must not resurface the IME"; it was retargeted at the undo pill, which is field-less for the same reason, rather than dropped along with the dialog. One mechanical lesson worth recording: **deferring the mutation moves the delete tap out of `runAsync`.** Those tests wrapped the tap because the delete did file I/O; now the tap only arms a timer, and wrapping it creates that timer in the real zone where `pump(Duration)` cannot advance it at all — the commit then never runs and the assertions fail in a way that reads like a missing restore. Tap in the fake zone, `pump` past the window, and alternate with `runAsync` only for the I/O the commit itself does.

## 524. The theme file measures itself: accent coral splits into a fill and a mark, a chip's size stops being a coincidence, and a cartographic hue goes back on the map

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 13 closed the four items §517 left open on the mobile theme. Every figure in the brief was a lead rather than a fact, and three of them moved.

**`AppTheme` is where the tokens are declared, which is exactly why nobody re-measures it.** Two of its own component themes had been painting `coralDeep` on `parchment` at **2.767:1** since §482 — the light `navigationBarTheme` selected icon and the FAB's `parchment`-on-`coralDeep` — and neither figure was the one that mattered. §503's trap fired on both, in opposite directions. The navigation bar's **selected icon is drawn inside the indicator pill**, not on the bar, so its background is `coralDeep@0.18` over parchment (`#F2DDD1`) and the real reading is **2.337:1** — the 2.767 that had been recorded was the flattering one. The FAB is the mirror image: a FAB is a *fill* carrying its own elevation and shadow, so under the foreground-XOR-fill rule the boundary is not the fill's to earn and only the **glyph** owes 1.4.11's 3:1. The fix therefore moved the foreground (`ink` on `coralDeep`, **5.757:1**) and left the coral fill alone, which is the opposite of what "raise the failing token" would have done. The rest of that bar reproduces §517's numbers except one: light unselected `haze` **5.102:1** and light selected label **15.928:1** are exact, dark selected icon is 9.120 **on the bar** but **6.034** on the pill it actually sits in, and dark unselected `parchment × 0.55` is **5.693:1**, not 5.709 — `withOpacity` quantises the alpha to 140/255, and the composite is `#908B91`.

**The token was the common cause, and the value was already measured — on the other platform.** §517 guessed the palette work was the natural home. It was half right: the answer is a second coral, not a deeper one, because `coralDeep` is a legitimate *fill* (the FAB background, the indicator tint) and only ever failed as a *mark*. That is §503's rule one role over, and **web had already solved it and recorded the number** — `--color-secondary` is `#D97A54`, mobile's `coralDeep`, and `--color-secondary-text` is `#A24A2C`, minted for exactly this in issue #368 when the base read 3.06:1 as text. So `AppTheme.coralMark` takes web's value rather than inventing a fourth burnt coral, and light `colorScheme.secondary` becomes it, which repaired **7 mark sites across 6 files with no call-site edit** — five icons, a hydration pip and a sparkline stroke, no text among them, so the slot is a foreground in this tree and §503 says it may not also be a fill. Four of the seven paint on `secondaryContainer` rather than on a plain page, where the old coral was **2.366:1** and the flattering 2.767 would again have been the wrong figure. It clears **AA**, not merely 3:1, on every light surface (worst **4.566:1** on `primaryContainer`, **4.570:1** on the `secondaryContainer` those four use) and **4.515:1** on the indicator tint it composites over, so §522's warning is answered by construction: the mark has headroom to be tinted, unlike `ChartPalette.kinds`. Dark needs no twin — its `secondary` is `lilac` at ≥ 4.330:1 — which is also why web's dark `-text` token aliases straight to its base. Both halves of the pair are now asserted from web's `contrast_guard.test.ts`, one new self-contained `test()` appended rather than woven into an existing loop, which is the merge-safe shape §522 asked for.

**It also falsified a live assertion, and the honest repair was to name the colour rather than the slot.** §517's calorie-goal-line pin asserted that `colorScheme.secondary` at full strength is under 3:1 — the finding that decided the line should take `outline` instead of simply losing its alpha. With light `secondary` moved, that assertion became false and the test failed. The premise was historically true and is still the reason the line draws a boundary token, so the pin now names `AppTheme.coralDeep` directly. **A test that pins why a past decision was right must reference the value that was wrong, not the slot that held it** — a slot can move underneath it and turn a correct record into a false one.

**`RawChip`'s OR was a size problem, not a colour problem, and it is why the exception exists.** §517 recorded that `chipTheme.labelStyle ?? chipDefaults.labelStyle` is an OR, so §476's `labelStyle` — which exists only to carry the selected/unselected `WidgetStateColor`, because that is the only thing `RawChip` resolves — displaced M3's `labelLarge` outright and left **every chip label in the app with no size of its own**, landing on the ambient 14 by coincidence. The two properties cannot be separated: the override that buys legible selected chips costs the step. So the step is restated in `AppTheme` beside the colour, and the four values were checked against all three of Material's locale geometries before being written — `labelLarge` is **14 / w500 / 0.1 / 1.43 in englishLike, dense and tall alike**, differing only in `textBaseline`, and `inherit` stays true so the locale's family and baseline still arrive by merge. Hardcoding therefore costs nothing, which is the fact that made a literal acceptable; had the geometries disagreed it would not have been. `font_size_literal_guard_test.dart`'s entry for the theme file goes 4 → 6, and the two properties are pinned together in one test, so a future fix to either cannot silently drop the other.

**A 1.003:1 tint is invisible to everyone, and both of the open ones now carry a cue that is not colour.** §517's two figures survive re-derivation but were attributed to the wrong composites, which is worth recording because the two rows differ in what they paint *over*. `plan_detail`'s today row tints over its week card (`surfaceContainerHighest`), so tint-versus-neighbour is **1.003 / 1.141**; `segments_panel`'s viewer row tints over the enclosing `Card` (`surface`) while its neighbours are opaque `surfaceContainerHighest`, giving **1.078 / 1.013** — §517's 1.076 / 1.017 to rounding. Both took a marker plus a weight rather than a deeper tint, because §503 forbids the cheaper move: a label tinted a hue its own row does not draw is its own defect. The plan row gained a 6 px dot in a leading slot, wrapped in `Semantics(label: planDetailToday)` so the cue is not sighted-only, plus a w700 weekday; the leaderboard row gained a `navYou` label beside the name plus a w700 name. **Neither needed an ARB key** — both strings already exist in all seven locales, which is the second time in two rounds that the right cue was already localized (§517 reused `profileNotifUnread`), and is a reason to look before minting.

**The violet was a cartographic colour that had leaked into chrome, and the brief's surface was wrong.** `#8B5CF6` is at **4** sites, not 3, and none of the three chrome ones paints on `surfaceContainerHigh` — the results pill, the results sheet and the selection card are all `colorScheme.surface`, where it reads **3.828:1 light / 3.817:1 dark**. So it was *passing* 1.4.11 at every real site and the 3.452 figure was measured against a surface nothing used. That makes it the more interesting kind of defect: not a failure, but a fixed hex whose passing margin was luck about which container each site happened to sit in — one step deeper, on dark `surfaceContainerHighest`, it is **2.902:1**. The verdict is that it is **cartographic, like the cyan preview line and the casing under both**: chosen against arbitrary basemap tiles, where there is no theme surface to measure against, and therefore correctly a fixed hex **on the map and nowhere else**. Promoting it to a token would have been the wrong call — it is not per-brightness and cannot be made so without ceasing to be the colour the line draws. The three chrome sites take `colorScheme.primary` (**7.766–11.005:1**), completing a migration round 12 started when it moved two button *labels* off the same hex and left the border beside them violet; the legend link to the map line is carried by the filled-versus-outlined `push_pin` fork, which is a shape cue and was already there. Enforcement extends §480's guard rather than adding a scanner: the hex joins `_bannedHexes` and is count-pinned at exactly **1** in that file, so a fourth chrome site fails and removing the map line forces the entry out. That widens the guard's charter from "status roles" to "a colour literal that bypasses a measured palette", which is what it had always actually been doing. The cyan `#22D3EE` is the same class and needs nothing: it has no chrome site at all, which is the difference.

**Left open with numbers.** (1) The light navigation indicator is a **1.184:1** wash against its bar (dark **1.511:1**), so the pill is not the selected-state cue — the icon's colour and the label's w500→w600 weight are. That is a passing state today only because the weight fork exists; it is recorded so a future flattening of the type does not quietly make colour the only signal.
