(2) `AppTheme.primary`, `AppTheme.secondary` and `AppTheme.surface` are dead statics with zero readers in the tree, left alone because deleting them is not a colour change. (3) The `routes_heatmap_screen` map layers still hold thirteen un-count-pinned cartographic literals outside the ban list (`0x731E293B` ×2, `#22D3EE` ×3, `0xFF0F172A` ×4, `#F2A07B` ×2, `#7FB3C2` and the `#1A73E8` Google brand blue), each honestly tile-bound; §518 declined a "no hex in a border" rule for the same population, and the same reasoning applies here.

## 525. A boundary on a tinted card mixes the card's own accent into the line, § 518's eight cards were seven false positives and one hidden defect, and web takes mobile's 11 px type floor as a floor rather than as a literal ban

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 12 left § 518 with two numbered leftovers. Both closed here, and the first one closed by discovering that its own figure was measured in the wrong place.

**The eight cards, re-derived.** § 518 recorded the line token as failing 3:1 "on eight dark tinted-gradient cards: on `color-mix(--color-primary 12–14%, --color-surface)` it reads **2.551–2.998:1**", and concluded that "no single dark value fixes both those and the plain surfaces, and mobile is under the same squeeze." The eight are identifiable — they are exactly the `linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(<accent> N%, var(--color-surface)) …, var(--color-surface))` rules in the tree: `clubs/[slug]` `.next-event-card` (primary 10 %), `clubs/[slug]/events/[id]` `.hero` (12 %), `dashboard` `.plan-hero` (14 %) / `.welcome-back-card` (12 %) / `.plan-promo` (accent-orange 12 %) / `.goals-empty-card` (secondary 10 %), `plans/[id]` `.hero` (14 %), and `plans/[id]/workouts/[wid]` `.hero` (kind-tint 14 %, six kinds). The figure reproduces to 8-bit rounding — the bare token on those stops is **2.539–2.776** dark — but **seven of the eight do not paint the bare token.** They paint `color-mix(in srgb, <their own accent> 28–35%, var(--color-border))`, and composited at the tinted stop that lands **3.152–3.744:1 dark** and **3.388–4.579:1 light**: `.plan-hero` 3.302, `.welcome-back-card` 3.457, `events/[id] .hero` 3.390, `.plan-promo` 3.618, `.goals-empty-card` 3.744, `plans/[id] .hero` 3.302, and `workouts/[wid] .hero` 3.152–3.712 across all six kind tints. Every one of them clears. § 518 measured the token against the tint and attributed the result to call sites that do something else — **§ 503's "measure where it lands" trap, a fourth consecutive round**, and this time it produced a *pessimistic* finding rather than an optimistic one, which is why nobody caught it by looking.

**So the residue was six sites, five of which the token-level reading could not see and one of which it hid.** Composited per call site, in both themes: `clubs/[slug]` `.next-event-card` (the one of the eight that paints the bare token, **2.776** dark), `NotificationsList` `.item-wrap.unread` (primary 7 % over the card, **2.955** dark), `plans/[id]` `.day.completed` (success 12 %, **2.701** dark), and the two map placeholders on `/routes` and `/runs` (primary 6 % over `--color-bg-tertiary`, **2.872** light and **2.99972** dark — not "meeting the floor exactly" per § 522 but missing it by 0.0003, which only a computed check finds). The sixth is `.btn-secondary:hover` in `app.css` and it is a different defect entirely, described below. All five tint cases take the pattern already in the tree, and the numbers after are 3.330–4.246 light / 3.400–4.784 dark.

**The rule, and the arithmetic that ruled out every alternative.** A boundary drawn on an accent-tinted surface **mixes that surface's own accent into the line, at roughly twice the tint's share**. It works because the border mix moves the line further toward the accent (28–35 %) than the tint moved the surface (6–14 %), so the gap widens instead of closing, and it tracks the card's hue by construction rather than by a value someone tuned. Three alternatives were weighed and each fails on a number:

- **Raise the single dark line value.** Feasible in isolation — in dark, lighter is monotonically better against every dark surface — but the requirement is set by the palest tinted stop in the tree, kind-1 at 14 % over the card (`#3F3A57`, L = 0.04771), which needs the line at **L ≥ 0.24313** against `duskLine`'s **0.16634**: a 1.46× luminance raise. At that value (e.g. `#8F82B0`, L = 0.24939) the line reads **4.609:1 on the plain card** and **5.412:1 on the page** — a hairline with more contrast than the *content* separation § 487 designed it for, and only **3.171:1** from `--color-text` itself, so the rule starts competing with body type. It also breaks the § 518 lockstep the guard reads out of `app_theme.dart`, and it does not generalise: the next card at 20 % breaks it again.
- **A second token for a boundary on a tinted card.** This is where the brief's "mobile has precedent for two line values" needs correcting for the second time — § 487 pinned **one token per brightness** (`parchmentLine` *or* `duskLine`), simultaneously as `dividerColor`, `dividerTheme.color` and an `outlineVariant` override; there is no mobile precedent for two line values inside one theme. On the numbers a fixed pair is possible (light L ≤ 0.18997, dark L ≥ 0.24313) but buys nothing: it needs the same call-site edit as the mix, it goes stale the moment a tint deepens, and it restores exactly the fail-open default § 518 removed — a plain `border: 1px solid var(--color-border)` must be right everywhere by construction.
- **Change the cards' tints so one line value clears everything.** The caps for the bare token at 3:1 are **5 %** on a dark primary tint, **5 %** on secondary, **3 %** on kind-1, and **2 %** over `--color-bg-tertiary` in light. Taking the 10–14 % heroes to ≤ 5 % and the placeholders to ≤ 2 % is deleting the tint, not tinting less.

**Mobile does not owe this fix, and § 518's "mobile is under the same squeeze" is the third correction.** Scanned across `apps/mobile_android/lib`, **no** Flutter surface draws `parchmentLine`/`duskLine` (via `dividerColor`, `outlineVariant`, or a `Border`) on an accent-tinted fill. The tinted surfaces there are `primaryContainer` rows and chips with no hairline; the hairline cards sit on plain `parchment` / `duskDeep` / `midnight`, which § 487 already pinned. The single mobile surface that is both tinted and bordered — `route_detail_screen.dart`'s marker chip — already carries this ADR's rule, independently: `color: color.withValues(alpha: 0.10)` under `Border.all(color: color.withValues(alpha: 0.20))`, the same colour at twice the share. The four `surface.withValues(alpha: 0.95)` panels beside dividers are 95 % opaque, so their divider is effectively on the plain surface.

**The sixth site is the two tokens § 518 minted colliding, and it cannot be fixed from the fill's end.** `.btn-secondary` fills with `--color-bg-tertiary` and edges with `--color-border` (3.112 / 3.330, § 518's own figures); on hover the fill flips to `--color-fill-subtle` and the edge stays, at **2.678:1 light / 2.508:1 dark**. That is unavoidable by construction — `--color-fill-subtle` *holds the value `--color-border` shipped with*, so they are one generation apart in the same luminance family. Opening the gap from the fill's end is arithmetically impossible in dark: the fill would have to drop to **L ≤ 0.02211** to put 3:1 between them, and `--color-surface` is already at **0.01496**, so every neutral chip would fall from 1.328:1 to **1.110:1** against the card it sits on — which is the same trap the token's own comment already records for `--color-bg-tertiary`. So the corollary is a prohibition rather than a retune: **the line token may not edge the subtle fill.** `.btn-secondary:hover` moves its *edge* to `--color-primary` (**4.849 / 5.848** on the hover fill), following `.btn-outline:hover`, which also gives the state a visible affordance it did not have — the fill shift alone is 0.434 of ratio. A control losing its boundary in one state is a 1.4.11 failure the plain-surface floor cannot see.

**Enforcement is composited and per call site, which is the only shape that could have found any of this.** `contrast_guard.test.ts` gains a scan that, for every leaf CSS rule in `src/**/*.{svelte,css}`, resolves the tint stops it paints as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--A) N%, var(--SURFACE))` and the border colour that actually applies **to that rule's subject**, then asserts 3:1 per theme. Four pieces of that sentence are load-bearing and each was a bug while it was written: the *subject* is the last compound, not the whole selector (reading all of `.feature:nth-child(1) .feature-icon`'s classes attributed `.feature`'s border to the icon and made four landing tiles false positives); the border is tracked **per edge**, because the plan grid's `border-top` kind stripe would otherwise read as replacing the whole box; **pseudo-class subsets** decide applicability, which is why `.relink-run:hover` — whose own hover rule moves the edge to primary — is not a finding and `.btn-secondary:hover`, whose does not, is; and comments are stripped from rule *bodies*, because a `/* … */` between two declarations survives the `;` split and prefixes the next one, which silently hid the very `border-color` this ADR added. It resolves file-local custom properties **scoped to the winning rule** (`.day` draws its box and its kind stripe from one `--day-line`, and `.day.completed` re-points it), and it resolves **every** value an indirect property is pointed at rather than the one the author had in mind — `workouts/[wid] .hero`'s six kind tints, § 519's lesson. A tint over `transparent` is deliberately out of scope: the source does not name the backdrop, and asserting on a guess is how § 503 got its name. The one shape it cannot resolve — a `var(--x, var(--color-border))` per-instance default, the line `css_token_guard.test.ts` already draws — is count-pinned at one. Proved by a planted violation on the real tree plus a fixture test on the attribution machinery, and verified by reverting all six fixes at once: it names all six, in ten (site × theme) findings, at the figures above.

**Web's type floor is a floor, not mobile's literal ban, and that is structural.** § 482 pins **11 px** (`labelSmall`) as mobile's micro-label floor and § 517 moved 27 literals onto the scale; web had nothing, and **45** `font-size` declarations were below it, the narrowest **8 px**. The named case is `PlanCalendar`'s `.kind-pill` at 0.65rem (10.4 px) dropping to 0.55rem (**8.8 px**) under 40 rem — the narrowest text in the app, on the plan surface every phone user opens — and `.dist` beside it at 0.6rem (**9.6 px**) in the same media query, which the brief did not name and which any floor must catch. Both now take `--font-size-section-label` (0.7rem = **11.2 px**), the micro-label token 80 declarations already use; per § 522 it is worth saying that this **clears the floor by 0.2 px rather than meeting it exactly**, so unlike a value that lands on a floor it survives a small later adjustment. The narrow-viewport rule now tightens only the box. At 360 px the seven-column grid leaves ~29 px of content per cell, so `.dist` reflows to two lines and the row grows — which is what SC 1.4.4 and 1.4.10 ask for and what `min-height` already permits; the pill keeps its ellipsis.

Web **does** owe a guard, and it is a floor rather than mobile's "name the step" ban. Mobile's rule is enforceable because its scale is *closed*: seven steps on one `textTheme`, so a literal is always a step spelled by hand or a value between two. Web's CSS carries **1886** numeric `font-size` declarations against three named size tokens, so a literal ban would need an allowlist longer than the code and would assert nothing; what transfers is the conformance content, and a floor states it directly. `font_size_floor_guard.test.ts` reads **11** out of `app_theme.dart` (asserting it is the same number in both brightnesses) so the platforms cannot drift the way the line token did before § 518, converts `rem` at the un-overridden 16 px root, and count-pins the **42** remaining sub-floor declarations across **27** files in two labelled groups: text inside a graphic — the class mobile's guard exempts too, an 8 px numeral inside a 20 px map pin and SVG labels inside the elevation plot — and plain debt, pinned so the count can only shrink rather than to bless it. `em` is unresolvable by any static scan and is count-pinned at six so a micro-label cannot evade the floor by switching unit. The regex's `(?<![\w-])` lookbehind is load-bearing: without it the guard reads `--font-size-section-label: 0.7rem` as a 0.7 px violation, in the token that defines the floor. And because what failed here was a *higher-specificity media-query override winning over a compliant base rule*, the source scan alone could not prove the fix — a Playwright assertion at a 360 px viewport reads the resolved `getComputedStyle` on both labels, and fails at 8.8 px when the override is planted back.

**Left open, with numbers.** `CurrentWeekStrip` and `ThisWeekStrip` carry the identical 0.55rem / 0.6rem narrow-viewport shrink `PlanCalendar` just lost (4 and 3 declarations) and are the obvious next slice; the remaining 35 sub-floor declarations are 9.6–10.9 px micro-labels spread one or two per file. The composited boundary scan covers tints over a *named surface token* only — a `color-mix(<accent> N%, transparent)` fill has no resolvable backdrop in the source. That exclusion is small and was measured rather than assumed: of the **96** transparent-tint background declarations in the tree, exactly **two** sit on an element that also carries a `--color-border` edge (`CoachChat` `.archive-banner`, which already mixes primary 25 % into its line and reads 4.026 light / 3.607 dark over the card; and `routes/new` `.canvas-empty`, a 0.92-alpha surface veil over basemap tiles, so effectively the plain surface at 3.906 / 3.330). Both are fine today by hand, and closing the class properly needs the resolved-cascade approach (`getComputedStyle` in Playwright) rather than a bigger regex, because a translucent fill's backdrop only exists at render time.

## 526. The hex allowlist becomes a complete register, and the map overlay's ground turns out never to have been the theme

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§511 bounded itself honestly and logged what it left: **453** six-digit literals across **72** files, of which only **141** were even a status hue, and **172** literals across **29** files carrying hues *outside* the status vocabulary — exempt purely by never having been in scope. Re-measured on this commit after round 12: **345** literals in **30** files (364 counting the ones living only in comments), **146** of them `app.css` custom-property declarations — all 146 are declarations, none is a rule — leaving **199** in **29** files. By role: **89** cartographic, **31** gradient stops, **24** identity / data palettes (tier metals, medal metals, chart series), **21** brand marks and provider hues, **20** fixed-canvas, **10** SVG art, **4** on-brand-fill inks. Ended at **271** in **25** files, **125** outside `app.css`.

**A named-hue ban cannot close that hole, because the next frozen fill picks a fortieth hue.** So the ban is inverted: every six-digit literal outside `app.css`'s declaration lines must appear in `REGISTER` with an exact count and a role from a closed eight-value vocabulary (`cartographic`, `brand-mark`, `brand-hue`, `data`, `fixed-canvas`, `gradient-stop`, `svg-art`, `theme-pair`). The 39-hue rule stays for its *message* — for a status role "route it onto the token" is always the answer — not for its reach. **That decides the border question §511 deferred** when it considered a "no hex in a border" rule and declined it as a 12-entry allowlist duplicating its own: the register keys on `(file, hue)` and the scan reads every line whatever it declares, so a border literal is an entry like any other. One register, not two, pinned by a test naming both surviving border literals. Proven in all three directions before landing — a new hue in a registered file, a new hue in a clean file, and a *removed* registered literal — each fails, then reverted.

**Two roles §511 ran together are not the same exemption.** A third party's *logo geometry* is theirs to tone (the Google "G", Apple's required black) — `brand-mark`, genuinely fixed by external requirement. The same party's *hue reused as our own paint* carries no such requirement, and §503's trap was waiting: measured against the bare surface these looked like AA-text failures, but they are glyphs on a 12–14 % tint **of themselves**, which is the ground that matters. On it, five of six provider inks miss 1.4.11's 3:1 floor — Strava **2.375:1**, HealthKit 2.446, ultrasignup 2.799, runsignup 2.831, chronotrack 2.961 — and Garmin alone clears, at 3.087. Those five plus eleven more are recorded as **open debts, each with its figure and the ground it was measured on**, as a frozen set. A register whose point is completeness has to be able to say "known bad, not yet fixed"; the alternative is dropping the honest finding to keep the suite green, which is precisely how §511's hole opened.

**The largest class was cartographic, and mobile's data exemption did not apply to it — the bug was upstream of the hues.** §480 exempts map markers as data and the parallel looked defensible, but §489/§491 had already established that the basemap varies with the map-style preference, and web keyed all six map surfaces on `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`. That is not the basemap and not even the app theme: **the preference decouples basemap luminance from the OS in both directions** — `outdoors` is a light basemap under a dark OS, `dark` and `satellite` dark ones under a light OS — so every overlay painted its light-ground colours on dark ground and vice versa. `basemapIsDark` now sits beside `buildMapStyleUrl` sharing one slug switch (two switches would let URL and palette drift, which is the whole defect), classifying `satellite` as dark like mobile's `resolveBasemapIsDark` because imagery is not enumerable and the darker rung is the safe side, and the keyless OSM raster fallback as light on its own `#dcdcdc` backdrop. `basemap_contrast.ts` is the palette; the samples are lifted verbatim from mobile's `live_run_map_tile_url_test.dart` so the two platforms grade against the same ground.

Measured against those samples, **35 of 49 cartographic literals failed a basemap they were actually drawn over**, and the mismatch cost roughly a factor of two either way: the trace line reads **2.599:1** on light ground when keyed dark and **2.734:1** on dark ground when keyed light, against 5.763 and 5.479 keyed correctly. The unconditional failures were worse: the course-marker pins' white ring at **1.148:1** on every light basemap, the route and club pin rings at **1.038:1** on dark, the featured-route gold halo **1.334:1**, the hover-preview cyan **1.575:1**, the coarse last-seen amber ring **1.785:1**, the segment/replay amber **1.871:1** on land and 1.339 over water, the start cap 1.986, the un-snapped preview grey 2.234, the spectator trace 2.431 on dark, and every casing inverted on one of the two grounds. §511's allowlist entry for `RunMap` had justified `#F59E0B` on the grounds that "its contrast is carried by the white ring around it" — **that reason was wrong for the layer it was attached to**: the segment and replay line layers have no ring at all, and the white ring it referred to belongs to the CSS DOM markers, where it was itself failing at 1.148:1 on light ground.

**Two structural facts fell out of measuring rather than asserting, and both are pinned as tests.** A **translucent casing cannot carry the floor** — white at 0.25 over the dark sample is **2.273:1**, `#1E1B4B` at 0.45 over the light sample **2.710:1** — so no rung in the module is justified by "it has a casing"; every line clears its ground unaided and the casing is decoration that sharpens an already-compliant line. And a **label halo is ground-coloured on purpose** (1.038:1 dark, 1.148 light), because its job is to hold the glyph apart from mid-tone map *features* — road casings, building fills, other labels — not from the flat land fill; what that forbids is counting the halo as the label's contrast, so the ink is held to AA against the ground directly on both sides. A pin *fill* is the one place a separator genuinely does the work: a basemap-keyed ring at 17.191 / 13.930:1 makes the boundary discernible, which frees the fill to stay a fixed identity hue — and MapLibre paint cannot consume a CSS custom property, so a literal there is structural, not lazy.

**`.btn-primary` was not the only white-on-a-fill-that-goes-pale, and §519's 2.081:1 recurs three more times exactly.** The sign-in brand pane's copy on a ramp ending in `#F2A07B`: **2.081:1** (1.817 under the pane's own 18 % sheen). `.btn-email` filling with `--gradient-primary`, whose palest stop is `#F2A07B` in light and `#B9A7E8` in dark: **2.081** and **2.153** — no single ink clears it, so the button takes §506's `--color-primary` / `--color-on-primary` pair at 9.120:1, the same fix §511 applied to `.btn-primary`. The 1080×1080 share card, whose content is centred over the middle stop: 2.153, worst stop 2.081. And the marketing hero subhead at `rgba(255,255,255,0.65)`: **3.284:1** on the hero's palest stop, where 20 px normal weight is not WCAG large text so 4.5:1 applies. The two ramps deepen along their own hue paths — a fixed canvas is exempt from *theming*, not from contrast, which is §511's own print-sheet amber one surface over. The guard reads each ramp **out of the source**, measures every stop bare and under each declared veil at that veil's peak, and pins the expected stop **count** per ramp for the reason §511 gave about floors read out of the tree: a regex that matches nothing must not pass. Veils that peak at opposite corners are measured one at a time, because stacking them asserts a composite no pixel of the pane shows.

One finding was not cartographic at all despite living in a map component: the routes-heatmap "kept route" violet labels *list rows on a theme surface*, where one frozen `#8b5cf6` read **4.234:1** as text on the light surface, **3.374** on the row's own hover fill and **3.817** on the dark surface — under AA in all three. It becomes a theme-keyed pair, and lands on the same two rungs the map line uses, because "clear the ground you sit on" has the same answer at both ends of the violet even though the two are keyed off different questions. It wants a `--color-route-pinned` token pair; local until `app.css` mints one.

## 527. The nutrition target becomes a peer that shows its own derivation, and the Art 9 half stays a single consent surface

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 13 closed the structural half of issue #666's **M1**, "Nutrition targets live in Manage." Round 6 (§490) had closed its empty-state half on mobile, replacing an inert sentence that told mobile users to set body metrics "on the web app" with a CTA into `SettingsBodyMetricsScreen`. What remained was filed as a mobile IA finding — the round-4 audit's phase table put *Nutrition targets* at `You→Preferences→Body metrics`, a *plan*-phase tool parked under *manage* — but reading the same question on web found the canonical surface in a worse state than the additive one, so the fix landed there first per § 24.

**The state on web, verified before building.** `computeNutritionTargets` was already imported by `routes/nutrition/+page.svelte`, so the *values* were on the page: the four macro rings carried them as denominators, the calorie chip counted down against them, the week trend drew a goal line off them. Nothing else was true. There was no route to them, no view of how they were reached, and — the part that makes this a defect rather than a placement preference — no affordance of any kind in either state. When targets computed, the page showed the numbers and offered nothing; when they did not, it rendered a bare `<p>` reading *"Add your height, weight, age and sex in Settings"* — naming a destination it declined to link, three sections down a page it did not name. Mobile, post-§490, put a button there. **That is a § 24 inversion, and the narrow kind § 513 permits acting on**: not "the additive platform ships a surface, therefore the canonical one owes it" — the inference § 513 was written to forbid — but the same surface on both platforms, where one routes the user to the fix and the other only describes it. `git log -S` on the route confirms no targets peer was ever built and retired; the finding is a gap, not a reversal.

**The circular referral was the tell.** `prefs.nutritionTargetsHint`, written in `ec17520f2` (2026-06-04) and shipped in all six locales, ended *"Activity level and goal set your default targets; fine-tune them on the Nutrition page."* No such capability had ever existed. So Settings sent the user to `/nutrition` to fine-tune, and `/nutrition` sent them to Settings to enter metrics, and neither sentence was a link. A copy promise outliving — in this case preceding — the feature it describes is the same failure mode § 490 recorded on mobile, and it survived a year and five i18n sweeps because a false sentence in six catalogues is invisible to every guard we own.

**The shape is a reachable, editable peer, not a panel.** `multi_modal.md`'s own rule — *"each modality owns its planning assets ... nutrition owns targets/recipes"* — already prescribed this, and meal templates and recipes had honoured it as self-hiding sections on the day view. Targets could not follow them there: the anti-clutter checklist requires each screen to have exactly one primary action, and an inline editor with its own save is a second. So `/nutrition/targets` is a peer at its own URL, linked from the `/nutrition` header exactly as `/gym` links Routines / Sessions / Records. **The link is ungated, unlike those three**, which self-hide on data presence: a user with no targets is the one who needs the route, so gating it would hide the surface from its whole audience — the same entry-point-can't-be-data-gated rule § 63's amendment applied to the Fitness hub.

**The page shows the derivation, and owes the Dart twin nothing.** It renders BMR, the activity factor, the goal delta, the base, today's workout add-on and the macro split — composed entirely from what `nutrition_targets.ts` already exports (`mifflinStJeorBmr`, `ACTIVITY_LEVELS`, `GOAL_KCAL_DELTA`, `PROTEIN_G_PER_KG`, `FAT_KCAL_FRACTION`, `MIN_CALORIE_TARGET`) plus the `baseCalories` / `exerciseKcal` fields the result already carries. **No new arithmetic was written**, which is the point: a `missingMetrics` predicate or a derivation-breakdown builder would have been new pure logic on one side of a documented parity pair, and adding that is the defect this project guards against. A guard test pins it, forbidding the literals `1.8`, `0.3`, `1200` and `-500` in the page's script block. The one comparison the page does make is a rounding-honesty one: the engine rounds the base to the nearest 10 and floors it at `MIN_CALORIE_TARGET`, so for a small or older user the printed terms would visibly fail to sum to the printed base, and the page says the floor bound rather than leaving arithmetic that does not add up.

**Height and weight are not editable there, deliberately.** Activity level and weight goal are effort labels, not body measurements; they already auto-saved ungated, so they move onto the peer. Height, weight, date of birth and sex are Art 9 special-category data behind an explicit-consent checkbox and a save that is deliberately *not* auto — a second place to enter them is a second consent surface to keep correct, and the audit's own Move said to keep the Settings tile for exactly this reason. Both surfaces therefore deep-link `/settings/preferences#body-metrics`, and the guard asserts three things together: that the peer contains no `<input>` and none of the five consent-gated data calls, that both CTAs carry that href, and that the preferences page still carries the anchor — an anchor that silently stops existing is rot no other test would catch.

**The contrast guard caught the one real defect in the new page**, flagging `color: var(--color-danger)` on the save-failure line where the theme-aware `--color-danger-text` is required. Worth recording as evidence for § 515's converse: the pre-existing guard was the only thing that knew, and it knew immediately.

**Mobile is a follow-up, not drift to close first.** `nutrition_screen.dart` still reaches the body-metrics editor from its empty state alone; once targets exist there is no route to them on either twin. The Dart side already carries every constant and `mifflinStJeorBmr`, so the mobile peer is a screen composition with no pure-logic work and no parity-pair change.

## 528. A guard that pins a spelling fails on a reformat; a figure attributed to a token is not a figure measured at the call site

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 13's five agents merged without a single content conflict — the file-level partition between the two web colour agents (token *definitions* + `contrast_guard` on one side, literal call sites + the literal guard on the other) held, which is the practical answer to round 12's collisions. Two integration findings remain worth recording, and both are refinements of rules this issue already has.

**A guard must assert the property, not one spelling of it.** `security_guards.test.ts` pinned `RunMap.svelte`'s accessible wrapper as a single regex over one canonical line — `<div class="run-map-wrapper" role="region" aria-label={m('runMap.regionLabel')}>`. When map overlay paint began resolving off the basemap (§526) the element gained four `style:--map-*` bindings, the tag split across lines, and the guard failed **while both attributes were still present and correct**. The fix reads the wrapper's opening tag and asserts `role` and `aria-label` inside it, order- and whitespace-independent, re-proved by deleting `role="region"`. This is §515/§522's family — a guard is code, and a guard coupled to formatting reports a reformat as a defect, which is the failure mode that teaches a future round to loosen the *assertion* instead of fixing the *cause*. Pin what must be true.

**§503's trap now has a second direction, and it has caught four consecutive rounds.** Every prior instance was optimistic: a ratio measured on a convenient background, hiding a failure (§495's gridlines, §503's own chip, §510's plan numeral, §511's race-day inks). §525 found the mirror image. §518 recorded "the line token reads 2.551–2.998 on eight dark tinted-gradient cards" — true of the *token* on those stops, but **seven of the eight never paint the bare token**; they paint `color-mix(<their own accent> 28–35%, var(--color-border))`, which clears the floor. The figure was **pessimistic**, which is exactly why it survived a round: nobody re-checks a number that already looks bad. The rule generalises past colour — **a measurement attributed to a token is not a measurement taken where the token lands**, and a per-call-site scan is the only thing that knows the difference. §525's residue was six sites, two of which §518 had never counted at all.
## 529. The register's open debts close as one defect, and three of its five figures were the wrong ground or the wrong floor

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§ 526 registered five failures rather than half-fix them, and the honesty paid off twice over — once because the set could then be closed as a set, and once because re-deriving every figure on the surface each site actually paints found the register had been measuring **elsewhere**. All five were one defect: **an identity or brand accent frozen as a hex at its call site and then asked to be both the tint and the ink on that tint.** No single value can be, in two themes. `#8FBF9F` is a legible pastel disc on near-black and **2.075:1** as a 3 px rail on the light card; `#4E7C5E` is a legible glyph on white and **2.359:1** on the dark card's 18 % chip of that same pastel. The seven nav glyphs read **1.594–2.659:1** on their own 14 % disc over the light sidebar and **1.219–1.911** on the 24 % hover disc, while the same seven read 4.826–9.046 on the dark one. The fix is therefore not a value but a **shape**: each identity hue becomes a `--section-<x>` / `--provider-<x>` **fill** with a theme-keyed **`-ink`** rung beside it, the pattern § 503 minted for status roles and § 524 carried to mobile's marks; every glyph, thin rail, border and label takes the ink, the fill keeps doing the tints, and the two dark rungs that need no change (`gym`, `nutrition`) alias their accent rather than restating it. `dashboard` and `coach` needed no new values at all — `--color-accent-orange-text` and `--color-accent-cyan-text` already existed at exactly the right two rungs, which is the § 503 vocabulary paying for itself.

**Identity survives because the split moves lightness and nothing else.** Seven sections distinguished only by a hue that all become one ink would be a regression even at a perfect ratio, so what is pinned is the hue *angle*: every ink sits within **2.6°** of its accent (0° for four of the seven), and the seven remain seven distinct values in both themes. The reason that is sufficient — and the reason a luminance ladder like § 511's `--zone-*` / `--kind-*` was not attempted — is that **luminance was never the separator here**: seven categorical marks cannot be pairwise 3:1 (six such steps need 729:1 and sRGB offers 21:1) and the shipped accents sit **1.003:1** apart pairwise, the inks **1.002**. Hue is what a user reads, so hue is what the guard defends, per pair and capped at 12° — dashboard's peach and history's terracotta are **1.6°** apart as accents and are the closest pair either way, so seven-way separation is something the split must not *spend*, never something it could create. That in turn is why colour must stay a secondary cue on all five surfaces, which it already was: the glyph shape and the localized label carry the section. The e2e half pins the other thing a unit test cannot see — a `color-mix(…, transparent)` over a gradient has no single computed background, so the browser test asserts the cascade, and a typo'd token name (which leaves the custom property unset and drops every glyph to the inherited text colour, with no build error) fails it.

**Three of § 526's five figures were leads, not facts, which is § 525's finding recurring for the sixth consecutive round — and in the same *pessimistic* direction § 525 found it.** The provider glyphs are not on `--color-bg-tertiary`: the per-provider rule **replaces** `.integration-icon`'s background outright rather than tinting over it, so the ground is the card, which moves Strava from 2.375 to **2.921:1** and clears four of the six § 526 recorded — HealthKit 3.015, runsignup 3.679, chronotrack 4.059, ultrasignup 4.369. And the `VerifiedBadge` ribbon is `aria-hidden` SVG geometry inside a labelled span, so it owes 1.4.11's 3:1 and not AA text: at 5.169 light / **3.127** dark it was never failing. Its real problem is the opposite of the one recorded — it is clamped from **both** ends, because the check cut out of the ribbon owes 3:1 to the ribbon, so lightening for dark spends the check to buy the card. Each rung is now set at its own theme's balance point (5.169/5.169 light, 4.014/4.027 dark), and the inner tone stays the literal `#fff` because an SVG presentation attribute cannot take a `var()` — § 528's rule about a computed colour landing somewhere its consumer cannot parse, one consumer over. Two failures § 526 missed turned up in exchange: `.gym-footer-cta` is real **text** at 0.85 rem/600 — not WCAG large text — and read **4.346:1** light / **3.949** dark, and ultrasignup (2.690) and chronotrack (2.886) fail in **dark** where § 526 had only looked at light. A register that records the honest finding gets audited; one that drops it to stay green does not.

**§ 526's `brand-hue` distinction held, and the surface it was drawn on turned out to already contain the answer.** Five of the six provider inks were the brand hue reused as our paint, which carries no external requirement — but the *sixth* row, parkrun, had been painting `--color-secondary-text` for some time, i.e. the exact shape the other six needed, sitting unremarked in the same stylesheet. Its brand coral **is** the history section accent, so it now aliases that ink rather than re-spelling the value. `OPEN_DEBTS` is consequently empty, and stays a live rule: the figure format is pinned against fixtures in both directions so an empty set cannot pass for the reason § 511 gave about a floor read out of the tree, and each of the five closed files is asserted *absent* from the register so a hue cannot be re-frozen there under another name. The nav's **active** state was left as § 526 measured it — the full accent behind `--section-on-accent` at 5.757–10.291:1 — even though the pale disc itself sits 1.452–2.596:1 against the light sidebar, because the active row is marked five ways over (disc fill, `FILL 1` glyph axis, row background, label colour, and the 3 px rail, which does take the ink now) and 1.4.11 asks for the information *required* to identify a component, not for every decoration to clear a floor. That reasoning is § 526's own about the label halo, and naming it here keeps the next round from re-raising it as a finding.

**The defect has a mobile twin that web's fix now diverges from.** `activity_timeline_list.dart` carries the two inks web just retired as theme-independent `const Color`s — `0xFF4E7C5E` for the lift glyph, `0xFF9A6B2F` for the meal — under a `CircleAvatar` whose fill is `accent.withValues(alpha: 0.16)`, i.e. a 16 % tint of the **ink itself**, which is the tightest version of this ground there is. On dusk that reads **2.875:1** (lift) and **2.962** (meal); on parchment 3.585 / 3.473. Not fixed here — it is the Flutter side's file — and recorded so the next mobile round takes web's already-measured pair rather than minting a ninth guess, the way § 524's `coralMark` did.

## 530. The type floor's allowlist becomes nine named exemptions, an `em` turns out to be measurable rather than exempt, and a label near a drawing is not a label inside one

**Date:** 2026-08-05

§ 525 minted web's 11 px micro-label floor, closed `PlanCalendar`'s `.kind-pill`, and count-pinned what it could not reach: **42** sub-floor declarations, six unresolvable `em`s, and two named leftovers — the week ribbons and "the remaining 35 sub-floor declarations, 9.6–10.9 px". All three closed here, and re-deriving each figure moved it.

**The counts, re-derived.** 42 sub-floor declarations across **28** files, not the 27 § 525 recorded — the allowlist itself already summed to 28 entries, so the prose and the code it described disagreed on landing. The residue after the two ribbons is **35**, which § 525 got right, but its range is wrong in the direction that matters: the narrowest of the 35 is the **8 px** map-pin numeral, not 9.6 px. § 525 had described that numeral correctly one paragraph earlier and then excluded it from its own summary range — the same class of error as its "80 declarations already use" the token, which recomputes as **81** declarations spelling the literal `0.7rem` and **21** using the token. Those are different populations and the distinction is load-bearing: both land on 11.2 px today, but only the token moves if the floor does, and per § 522 a hand-spelled value sitting exactly *on* a floor is the fragile kind. The 81 literals are outside this guard's reach by construction — at the floor, not under it — and are recorded as remaining work rather than swept, because routing them through the token touches files four other agents held this round.

**The two ribbons carried `PlanCalendar`'s defect verbatim, and stay unmerged.** `CurrentWeekStrip` (4 declarations) and `ThisWeekStrip` (3) each held a `max-width: 40rem` media query dropping micro-labels to 0.55rem / 0.6rem (**8.8 / 9.6 px**), plus base rules at 0.65rem (10.4 px). All seven take `--font-size-section-label` and the narrow-viewport rule now tightens only the box, exactly as § 525 left `PlanCalendar`. The pair is deliberately **not** merged despite the identical CSS: § 509 established their duplication is presentation-only, and the windows differ in kind — `CurrentWeekStrip` anchors to `start_date + week_index * 7`, `ThisWeekStrip` to the real calendar week containing `now`. Both files leave the allowlist entirely rather than dropping a count, which is the merge-safe direction when five agents share one pin file.

**A Playwright assertion that passes while measuring nothing is worse than none, and the first draft of this one did.** § 525's reasoning for a resolved-cascade check is exact — a source scan cannot say which of a base rule and its media-query override paints — so the ribbons got one. It passed on `CurrentWeekStrip` **with the override planted back**, because `.kind` and `.dist` render only on a day carrying a workout and the seed's now()-relative slide lands the current plan week inside its deliberate week-5..10 workout gap. The selector matched zero elements and every size assertion over the empty set held. So the helper now pins an **expected count** beside the floor, and the spec seeds one workout into whichever week is current, resolved from the plan's `start_date` rather than hard-coded. Verified in both directions: planted, it fails at 8.8 px on both ribbons; reverted, both pass. This is § 525's own "a regex that matches nothing must not pass" arriving at the assertion layer, and it is the second consecutive round where the check, not the code, was the thing that was wrong.

**Nine remain, and classifying them required reading the site rather than the file.** § 525 split the allowlist into text-inside-a-graphic and plain debt, keyed per **file** — and a file holding one of each lands wholly in whichever group its comment describes. Two of its three "graphic" entries were exactly that: `RouteBuilder` pairs the 8 px `.km-marker` numeral with a keyboard-shortcut hint, `ElevationProfile` pairs SVG `.extreme-text` with its tooltip's label, and § 525's own comments named both hints as debt while the group header said otherwise. The third is a genuine miscategorisation: `PersonalHeatmap`'s "the heatmap's legend scale, inside the legend graphic" is two HTML `<span>`s of localized prose sitting *beside* an `aria-hidden` gradient bar, and the file contains **no SVG text at all**. **A label near a drawing is not a label inside one** — the exemption is for text whose size is a dimension of the drawing, which is why an 8 px numeral inside a 20 px pin qualifies and "Less"/"More" under a legend bar does not. So **26** declarations were plain debt in flowing layout — pills, badges, eyebrows, stat labels, tags, timestamps — and all took the token. Nine survive: `ElevationProfile` 1 (graphic), `RouteBuilder` 2 (one graphic, one debt), and 6 in three files this round's partition assigned elsewhere (`dashboard` 3, `+layout` 1, `runs/[id]` 2).

**The `em` pin was not an exemption, only an un-measured static scan.** § 525 count-pinned six `em` declarations as "unresolvable by any static scan" — true, and § 503's trap makes guessing an ancestor chain worse than declining to — then left it there. But § 525 had *already* built the tool: `getComputedStyle` prices an `em` exactly, and it is the same move the media-query check makes. Split by kind rather than counted: **three are Material Symbols glyph sizing** (`ChallengeProgressBar` 1.05em, `RunGearChips` 0.95em, `settings/gear` 1.1em), the `em` analogue of the graphic exemption, and are deliberately **not** asserted — an icon has no reading size to protect and holding one to a legibility floor would teach the next reader that icons owe it. **Three are real text** and are now resolved: `cookie-notice` `.manage-consent-hint` 0.9em → **14.4 px**, and CoachChat's inline `code` and `pre code` 0.85em → **13.6 px** each off a `.md` that resolves to 16 px. The one number worth keeping is that the two code rules **do not compound**: both set 0.85em on the same element and `.md pre` sets no size, so `pre code` is 13.6 px and not 0.85² = **11.56 px** — which is within 0.6 px of the floor, so the day `pre` gains a `font-size` the product goes under. That is precisely why the check is resolved rather than reasoned. The pin stays at six: it counts source declarations, and its job is still to stop a micro-label evading the floor by switching unit.

**Reaching the coach's markdown at all needed the page's no-plan sentinel**, worth recording because the surface looks unreachable and is not. The chat renders whatever `coach_messages` holds for the caller, so one seeded assistant row exercises both `code` rules with nothing calling Anthropic — but `resolvePlanId` defaults to the runner's *active* plan, so a row on the null-plan thread never loads until `?plan=none` is passed. The row is seeded and torn down inside the test rather than in a fixture.

**One pre-existing finding, out of this slice's partition.** At a 360 px viewport `/dashboard` lays out **752 px** wide — `main-content` and `.page` both overrun the viewport, with `.plan-hero` at 736 px — so the page scrolls horizontally, which is the 1.4.10 failure the type floor's own reflow rule exists to avoid. It is not caused by the ribbon: `.week-strip-row` measures `clientWidth` 648 = `scrollWidth` 648 with no internal overflow, and its cells resolve at 11.2 px. The overflowing selectors live in `routes/dashboard/+page.svelte` and `routes/+layout.svelte`, both held by another agent this round. Recorded rather than fixed, and worth a round of its own: a horizontal scroll at phone width defeats every micro-label decision above it.

**Left open, with numbers.** The 81 hand-spelled `0.7rem` declarations should route through the token; they are at the floor so no guard can see them drift, and § 522's argument says a value on a floor is where the next regression starts. Six sub-floor declarations sit in three files this round partitioned away (`dashboard`'s `.bar-label` still carries the same base-plus-narrow-shrink pattern all three calendar surfaces just lost, and its `.source-badge` is the last member of a four-surface family whose other three are now at or above the floor). `RouteBuilder`'s `.shortcuts-hint kbd` is plain debt in a graphic-labelled file and wants either the token or a `min()` against the hint's box. And the dashboard's 752 px reflow overrun is the largest single accessibility item this slice touched without owning.

## 531. A share URL's path is defined once and its base belongs to the caller; and the route builder's private slug table keeps its tiles but loses its private answer about the ground

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Two structural leftovers, both recorded in earlier rounds with the reason they
were left, and both closable now that the reason has been re-read rather than
re-quoted.

**§520 got the origin question right and that is precisely why the path
question survived.** It established that a *copy-to-clipboard* link
legitimately resolves against `location.origin` (a preview host has to yield a
preview link) while a `<head>` canonical must resolve against
`PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (the public home of the content is not whichever host the
reader is on). Having settled that the two uses want different origins, it read
`${window.location.origin}/share/run/${run.id}` on `/runs/[id]` as correct —
which it was, about the origin. The defect was one line up in the same file:
the canonical two hundred lines above it went through
`buildRunShareCanonical` while the copy-link spelled `/share/run/` by hand,
and `/routes/[id]` and `/u/[id]`'s badge link did the same. **The builders
already take the base as a parameter**, so the fix needed no new shape at all —
`buildRunShareCanonical(window.location.origin, run.id)` is the same one path
definition resolved against the origin this use wants. §520's own round had
already written the pattern on `/sessions/[id]` and `/gym/[id]`; the three
older surfaces just never got moved.

Grepping for the class found it was not three sites but **fourteen** — three
copy-links, five sitemap `<loc>`s, and six JSON-LD `url`s. `sitemap.ts`
assembled all five of its share `<loc>`s itself, which is the worst instance
rather than a lesser one: **a `<loc>` that disagrees with the target page's own
`<link rel="canonical">` hands a crawler a manifest of URLs that each point
somewhere else**, and nothing about that fails visibly — indexing just stalls.
Six more were second spellings *inside the builder modules*, where each
entity's JSON-LD `url` re-derived the path its own exported canonical builder
had just defined. Two entities had no extracted builder to call:
`buildBadgeShareCanonical` and `buildRecapShareCanonical` are minted here, the
latter pinning the shape that is easy to "correct" wrongly — a recap's public
page is `/recap/share/[id]`, the one entity whose URL does not sit under
`/share/`, so flattening it into the family form would 404 every link ever
pasted.

`share_url_source_guard.test.ts` takes §526's register form rather than a ban:
every place a share path is assembled appears with an exact count and a
reason, the nine builder modules as definitions and the two recap pages as
**named open debts** (their fix is a two-line call, left standing only because
the round's file partition put them in another agent's tree). Proven in three
directions before landing — a reverted copy-link, a second spelling inside a
builder, and a register entry whose site disappears — each fails, then
reverted. The count direction matters as much as the name direction: a count
that rises is a new spelling of a path that already has a builder, one that
falls is a builder that has lost its last caller.

What is deliberately *not* in scope: the root-relative in-app hrefs
(`SocialFeed.svelte`'s three, `notification_link.ts`'s two, `/live/[id]`'s
one). They are navigations, not shareable URLs, and they cannot get the origin
wrong — the failure the class is about. Routing them through a builder would
read as `href={buildRunShareCanonical('', entry.id)}` at every call site, which
trades a legible template for an obscure one.

**§526's reason for leaving the route builder alone was true of the URL and
false of the classification, and the two had been fused.** It routed five map
surfaces through `basemapIsDark` and left `RouteBuilder.svelte` resolving its
own `darkBasemap`, noting that "routing it through the shared resolver would
silently change which satellite tiles it requests" — because the builder's
switcher offers `hybrid` (imagery *with labels*, which is what makes it usable
for placing waypoints) where the preference union's `satellite` member resolves
to bare `satellite`, plus a `terrain` key the union has no member for at all.
Measured before touching anything: of the builder's three rungs, `streets`
resolves to exactly the shared slug pair (`streets-v2` / `streets-v2-dark`),
`terrain` to `outdoor-v2` — the same tiles the union's `outdoors` requests,
under a different local name — and only `satellite` genuinely differs. And the
*luminance verdict* was already identical in every one of the five branches
(override, keyless, imagery, terrain, streets). So the divergence was one slug
in the URL and nothing in the classification.

The resolution widens the **slug** vocabulary, not the preference union: a
fifth `MapStyle` member would be a value no settings surface ever writes, while
`MaptilerSlug` is simply the set of slugs the app requests, and `slugIsDark` is
an exhaustive switch over it — adding a slug is a compile error until it is
classified, because an unclassified ground is an overlay palette picked by coin
toss. `basemapIsDarkForSlug` shares the override and keyless *precedence* too,
so all a surface with its own table still owns is which slug it asked for.
`maptilerStyleUrl` is the one spelling of the style-document endpoint. **No
surface's tiles change**, and the guard proves it by reading the builder's slug
table out of its source and pinning the URL each rung produces rather than
trusting the diff.

The deliverable that outlasts the reconciliation is
`map_surface_basemap_guard.test.ts`, because §526 fixed five instances of a
class nothing prevented a sixth of. It registers every file that instantiates
MapLibre and checks both directions — a new map surface must be added, and an
entry must resolve its ground through the shared resolver — and then pins the
load-bearing property mechanically: **the OS colour preference may reach a
style URL, a basemap classifier, or a slug table, and nothing else.** That is
the checkable form of "the OS may pick the basemap; it may not pick the paint",
and it finds the symbol by walking back from the media query to its nearest
declaration rather than pinning the name `prefersDark`, per §528. The
component `<style>` blocks are excluded on purpose and for a reason worth
recording: a map component's stylesheet also dresses list rows, which *are*
theme surfaces — §526's own `--kept-accent` violet on `RouteHeatmap` keys on
`prefers-color-scheme` correctly — so a guard that banned the media query
outright would be wrong about half its matches. The same suite fails a `var()`
or `color-mix()` in a MapLibre paint value, which MapLibre's own parser throws
out of `addLayer` on (§528), taking the map down with it.

**`PrivacyZonePicker` is the sixth map surface and it has no ground question to
get wrong.** §526 recorded its `#dc2626` at 3.011:1 over light-basemap water as
the thinnest margin in the register; re-derived here, all three figures
reproduce exactly (4.208 light land, 3.560 dark, 3.011 water, and 3.522 on the
OSM backdrop). It is registered as `unkeyed` rather than exempt, and the guard
fails if it ever calls a `basemap_contrast` rung — an unkeyed surface that
starts painting a keyed colour has acquired the question. **The verdict on
moving it: the single hue is defensible and the margin is not.** Of the red
ladder, `#dc2626` is the *only* rung that clears 3:1 on every ground this app
resolves to — `#B91C1C` fails the dark basemap at 2.657 and `#EF4444` fails
water at 2.346 — so a surface that wants one fixed danger hue has exactly one
choice, and the 0.4 % margin over water is the price. A basemap-keyed pair
would buy real headroom on both sides (`#EF4444` at 4.568 on dark ground,
`#B91C1C` at 5.638 land / 4.034 water on light), which is the recommendation;
it wants a `mapZoneColour` rung in `basemap_contrast.ts` and a register-count
edit, and is left as a named debt rather than landed here because the register
entry lives in a file another agent held this round.

## 532. A localized vocabulary is reused, not re-derived; a §486 row's treatment is read off its shape; and the catalogue nobody reads is the one the audit kept translating

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 14's mobile leftovers were five small live defects. Three closed at the root, two turned out to have the wrong premise, and the two corrections outlast the fixes.

**Two labels, one vocabulary, and the vocabulary is the whole answer.** `coaching_athlete_screen`'s `_workoutLabel` capitalised the raw `plan_workouts.kind` string and fell back to the literal `'Run'`, so all seven locales read English. The fix is not a new switch: `workoutKindLabel(l10n, workoutKindFromDb(kind))` already backs the plan grid, the workout detail, the week strip, the calendar, the today card and the edit sheet, and it is the Dart twin of web's `workout_labels.ts`. Nothing was missing from it — the `workout_kind` enum is exactly nine values (`20260419_001` plus `walk_run` from `20261020_001`) and `workoutKindLabel` covers nine, so **no kind lacks a key**. The `'Run'` fallback was unreachable: the column is `not null` over an enum with no empty member. Its sibling `_activityLabel` could *not* take the same treatment and that is the durable finding — `ActivityType` is five values including `stroller`, and the app carries two partial vocabularies (`prefsActivity*`, four, no `stroller`, hand-rolled title-case fallback; `feedActivity*`, five, but the fifth is `lift` and the fallback is "All"). Reusing either would have deepened the duplication, so it is left open for one shared `activityTypeLabel`. **The same defect is live on web** at `coaching/athletes/[id]/+page.svelte`'s `workoutLabel`, one line from the `workoutKindLabel` in its own `workout_labels.ts`.

**§486's taxonomy is read off the row's shape, and the two sheets in this round are one of each.** The gym composer's `Spacer` + Cancel + Save is a *run of buttons with nothing at the opposite end*, so it becomes an `OverflowBar` exactly as `event_form_sheet` already is. The goal editor's Delete + `Spacer` + Cancel + Save *keeps opposing ends*, so the grouped end moves into an `Expanded(Wrap(alignment: end))` and Delete keeps the leading edge — an `OverflowBar` there would have stacked all three end-aligned and put Delete beside Save, which is the one adjacency a destructive action must not have. Measured pre-fix at 320 dp / 2.0x the goal row overflowed by **248 px** and the gym row by **114 px at 480 dp**, both under `flutter_test`'s fixed-advance font, so per §500 neither number is quotable as a device figure and neither guard asserts a fit. Each pins the derivation instead: one run at 1.0x on a comfortable surface (the mechanism only fires when it must), and a second run at 2.0x narrow (it fires), plus that the anchor held. Two facts came out of writing them. Both mechanisms **bound the child's width** — `RenderWrap` lays children out at `maxWidth: mainAxisLimit` and `OverflowBar`'s overflow path passes the incoming constraints — so a button label wider than the lane *wraps inside the button* rather than striping, which is why `takeException(), isNull` is a legal assertion here at all. And the 2.0x gym case had to be pumped at **480 dp, not 320**: below ~470 the sheet's set-type dropdown and exercise header overflow on their own account under the test font, so a 320 pin would have failed for a reason this round does not own. §501's own comments in both test files had recorded these two rows as known-and-deferred; both notes are now removed.

**A required parameter closes a locale-free package's only English, and the trap was the default rather than the literal.** `ActivityLoader.label ?? 'Loading'` shipped an English screen-reader announcement out of ui_kit, which has no catalogue and never will. Nothing was broken — *every* production construction goes through `FullBodyLoader`, which already required the label, so there were **zero** direct call sites and only the package's own test omitted it. That is precisely why it survived: the first caller to omit the argument would have shipped English silently. Auditing for it turned up four more, in two widgets with **no callers anywhere in the repo** — `ImportSheet` ("Import a route", "GPX, KML, or GeoJSON", "Choose file") and `RunMap` ("Map"), the latter still documenting itself as a placeholder until MapLibre was configured. Both are deleted. The guard that keeps the class shut fires two ways, and the second is the load-bearing one: a word-bearing literal reaching a `Text` / `label:` / `semanticLabel:` / `hintText:` / `tooltip:`, **and any `?? 'literal'` fallback** — no sink pattern would have caught `label: widget.label ?? 'Loading'`, because the sink's argument is an expression. Symbol-only literals are exempt by construction (`identity_avatar`'s `?? '?'` carries no language).

**The unknown-distance notification doubled its own possessive in all seven locales.** `profileNotifYourRun` is the `{dist}` fallback when a kudos or comment notification has no run distance, and it carried a possessive while every consuming template supplies one: `"gave kudos to your your run"`, `"hat deinen deinen Lauf kommentiert"`, `"a tu tu carrera"`, `"à votre votre course"`, `"あなたのあなたのラン"`, `"à sua sua corrida"`. The fallback becomes a bare noun. It is pinned in `l10n_parity_test` as a derivation rather than seven copy assertions — substitute the fallback into the template and reject any back-to-back repeat of three or more characters, which needs no possessive vocabulary and works on the space-free `ja` catalogue. The guard reproduces the failure in six of the seven directly and flags the seventh (`de` differs by case, `deinem` vs `deinen`, so only its comment template repeats). **Web carries the identical defect** at `notificationBell.yourRun` + `notificationsList.yourRun`.

**The catalogue this round was asked to translate is not reachable at runtime, and the brief's premise about it was wrong twice.** The brief held that `app_pt.arb` is European Portuguese everywhere except its `profileNotif*` block. Measured: **3,251 of its 3,477 keys are byte-identical to `app_pt_BR`** — it began as a copy, and successive rounds have Europeanised 226. Its own lexicon is mixed (`Salvar` 63 vs `guardar` 13, `excluir` 70 vs `eliminar` 8, `você` 134 vs `teu`/`tua` 19), so the `profileNotif*` block being identical was the norm, not an anomaly. Worse: `locale_support.dart`'s `supportedLocales` omits `Locale('pt')` and `_baseToLocale` maps `'pt'` → `Locale('pt','BR')`, and `main.dart` passes *that* list to `MaterialApp` rather than gen-l10n's (which does contain `pt`). `negotiateLocale` returns `pt_BR` for a `pt-PT` device, a bare `pt` device, and a stored `pt` preference alike — so **no user has ever read `app_pt.arb`.** The block was Europeanised anyway (19 of 30 keys: the `-ndo` gerund → `estar a` + infinitive, `você` as a post-verbal object → the `-te` clitic, and `seu`/`sua` → `teu`/`tua` matching the file's own pt-PT strings), because the content is right and the file is the *de facto* pt-PT catalogue the day anything wires it up. Eleven keys are deliberately untouched: eight are identical in both varieties, and three (`e mais {count}`, its `{name}` variant, `Mostrar menos`) are forms this round is not confident differ — a wrong translation is worse than a known-stale one. The real item is a decision, not a translation pass: either ship pt-PT properly, or admit `app_pt` is gen-l10n's required base fallback and guard it identical to `app_pt_BR`, making every partial Europeanisation drift.

**A gesture that is the only route to a capability gets a caption, and the caption goes where both layouts read it.** Long press is the sole entry into multi-select on History and Routes; there is no hover, no menu entry, and nothing changes until the press lands. `SelectionHint` (ui_kit, `label` required for the same reason `ActivityLoader`'s now is) captions each list under the filters while something is selectable, and drops out once the selection app bar takes over — restating a mode the reader is already in is noise. On Routes the condition is narrower than "non-empty": only **owned** routes are selectable, so a library of nothing but bookmarks shows no hint. On History it rides `_filterHeader`, which *both* the single-column list and the ≥840 dp grid build through, so the two paths cannot diverge — inserting at the list's `index == 0` would have covered one and not the other. A visible `Select` button mirroring web's is deliberately not added: mobile's app bar already transforms on entry, and a permanent second affordance would compete with the two FABs.

**Correction to the round-14 brief.** It said every current `ActivityLoader` call site passes a label; there are no direct production call sites at all, only `FullBodyLoader`. It said `followups.md` tracks the native review of the five non-English locales — it does, at the item of that name, and the archive carries the older note. And the two overflow line numbers it quoted (`gym_compose_sheet.dart:471`, `goal_editor_sheet.dart:237`) are correct.

## 533. A tab strip's scrollability, a hero map's height and a card stack's rhythm are all derived; the run row was forked four ways, not three

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 14 closed the round-2 composition cluster — C6, C7, C8, C9 — four findings filed twelve rounds earlier and never re-measured. **Two of the four figure sets did not survive re-measurement**, and both errors ran in the direction of understating the defect.

**C6 reproduced exactly, and the mechanism is Material's own default.** `fitness_hub_screen` left `isScrollable` unset, so Material 3 gave it `TabAlignment.fill` at `_kTabHeight + indicatorWeight` = **48 dp**, flush at x=0; `social_screen` set it true, which defaults to `TabAlignment.startOffset` — a **52 dp** `EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:)` on the scroll view — and its icon-and-text tabs report `_kTextAndIconTabHeight + 2` = **74 dp**. Switching between two sibling hubs therefore moved the strip **26 dp** vertically and the first tab **52 dp** horizontally at once. `profile_screen` and `club_detail_screen` were on the scrollable side too, so three strips indented and one did not. The fix is not a `tabBarTheme`: `TabAlignment` is asserted valid *against* `isScrollable` (`start`/`startOffset` are illegal when false, `fill` when true), so a single themed value cannot serve both, and the choice would remain per-screen. `AppTabBar` (ui_kit) measures the labels with a `TextPainter` at `MediaQuery.textScalerOf` against the width a `LayoutBuilder` hands it and derives the flag, taking `TabAlignment.start` when it scrolls — a strip that fits shares the width, one that does not scrolls without indenting its leading tab, and the same labels flip with the width and with the OS text scale rather than with the author's guess. **Icons are not a parameter**, because they are the only thing that makes a strip 74 dp instead of 48 and `club_detail`'s six text tabs are the evidence that tab count is not what earns it; the widget takes labels, so an icon cannot come back. The strip is also the reason a guard has to ban `Tab(` and not merely `TabBar(`.

**C7's figures were wrong in an interesting way: the rhythm had three values, not one missing gap.** The audit reported 8 → 12 → 16 → 16 dp against 28 above. Measured on a 400 dp surface the analytics seams are **64 / 32 / 8** against **32**, and the 32 above is `_kSectionGap`'s 24 plus two card margins rather than a 28 anybody wrote. The 64 and the 32 came from a mechanism the audit had not identified at all: `FitnessCard` and `RacePredictorCard` each ended their `Column` with `const SizedBox(height: 24)` — a card padding *itself*, which § 482 had already banned — and each hand-rolled a `titleMedium` heading *above* its own `Card`, so the dashboard carried **five** header grammars in one scroll: an external `_SectionHeader`, that internal hand-rolled twin of it, `ChartCardHeader` inside four cards, `ReadinessCard`'s byte-for-byte inline copy of `ChartCardHeader`'s typography beside a band pill, and `RecentLiftsCard`'s `titleMedium` beside a `TextButton`. The resolution came from web, which had already decided it: every dashboard card there is `<section class="card-elevated"><h2>…`, a card that names itself. So all of them take `ChartCardHeader` — the streak and personal-bests cards fold the two external headers *inside* and reuse their existing keys — and the whole card stack then separates by the card theme's own vertical margin, one gap repeated, with `_kSectionGap` left for the one thing an external header is for: a heading over a **group** of cards plus that group's action, which is the goals section. `dashboard_card_rhythm_test` asserts the stack's gaps are a one-element set *and* that the element equals `AppTheme.light.cardTheme.margin.vertical`, so raising the card margin moves the expectation with it rather than failing.

Moving four title-case section titles into the eyebrow slot beside three that shouted (`MILEAGE`, `ACTIVITY`, `READINESS` — uppercase baked into the ARB *values*, in every locale that has case) created a new inconsistency, which web again settled: `"dash.mileageTitle": "Mileage"`. The three keys come down to title case in all seven ARBs rather than `ChartCardHeader` gaining a `toUpperCase()`, because casing is a locale-dependent copy decision and the widget's contract is that it carries none.

**C8 undercounted: the same run rendered four ways, and one of the five shapes was dead.** Beyond the three the audit named, `period_summary_screen` had its own `_RunTile` — a `Card` + `ListTile` with a `CircleAvatar` that is never a thumbnail, an unstyled distance, and a `•` where the others use a `·`. And ui_kit exported a `RunListTile` that had been referenced by nobody since the scaffold commit: a fifth shape, deleted rather than adopted, exactly as § 509 did with `StatCard`. Three of the four surfaces now draw one `RunListTile` with **two named constructors** — `.owned` from a local `Run` (selection mode, unsynced marker, inline track) and `.public` from a `RunRow` plus the profile owner's id — because per § 509 the surfaces differ in which fields *exist*, not in their values. The extraction shipped one bug worth recording: resolving a field as `_run?.x ?? _row!.x` reads the absent source whenever the present one's value is legitimately null, so a run with no metadata threw. **The discriminator is which constructor ran, never whether a value happens to be null.** `activity_timeline_list`'s `_ActivityRowTile` is deliberately left and the reason is pinned in both directions: it renders runs, lifts and meals from the `activities` view's thin `summary` jsonb, which carries no `track_url` for a thumbnail to read, and its tinted avatar is what names the modality — adopting the run row there would delete the cross-modal axis, and forking a run list back out of it would reopen C8. Consolidating also moved the privacy obligation: `architecture_guards_test`'s "profile_screen threads `ownerUserId` into `RunTrackPreview`" now reads the shared row for the mount and the screen for the argument, which is the honest split.

**C9 reproduced, and § 502's lesson applied without amendment.** Four screens picked 320 / 320 / 300 / 280 and none reflowed; `widthClassOf`'s wide branch only fires at ≥ 840 dp, so a 667×375 landscape phone keeps the compact layout with a **295 dp** viewport (375 − 24 status bar − 56 app bar) that a 320 dp map fills outright — no peek, no signal that anything follows. `detailMapHeight` takes **0.45 of the scroll viewport**, calibrated so the reference 360×800 phone's 720 dp viewport reproduces the largest shipped figure, then caps at 400 so a tablet does not get a 540 dp hero, and applies the peek floor **last** so content is always visible below the map. The height comes from a `LayoutBuilder` around the scroll view rather than from `MediaQuery`: a `Scaffold` with an app bar has already removed the status bar and the toolbar from its body's constraints, so subtracting either again double-counts, and which insets an enclosing `SafeArea` consumed is not knowable from the leaf — the constraints are the answer both approximations were reaching for. This is the same shape as `fabScrollClearance` and the opposite reading of `MediaQuery`, and the difference is principled: `padding` is authoritative about an *inset*, and nothing is authoritative about a height a parent has already reduced.

The change broke one test in a way worth writing down, because it is a class of test bug rather than a one-off: `route_review_report_test` dragged the route-detail list by a fixed `Offset(0, -600)` to reach the reviews section. Shortening the map moved the drag's start point off the map and onto the list, which changed *which recognizer won the gesture* — `FlutterMap` claims a drag that begins on it — so the same constant reached a different place. The harness now pumps a tall surface so the whole body builds, as `dashboard_card_alignment_test` does. **A fixed drag offset is an absolute fit in disguise**, and § 500's rule against them covers gestures too.

Enforcement is four guards, each proved to fire by perturbation: `tab_strip_guard_test` (bare `TabBar(`, bare `Tab(`, and each host still on `AppTabBar`), `detail_map_height_test` (a `height:` literal on a box whose child is a map, plus the derivation's ratios, monotonicity, clamps and peek invariant), `chart_surface_guard_test` extended with a header-only surface set, a per-file zero-count on `textTheme.titleMedium` in a card, and `_SectionHeader` count-pinned at its one group use, and `run_row_guard_test` (the run-surface list, no thumbnail outside the shared row, no local shadow of it, no leading-slot literal, and the cross-modal exclusion asserted both ways). **Left open with numbers:** `route_detail_screen` and `public_route_screen` still have no expanded branch at all, so a 1280×800 landscape tablet gets a 324 dp strip where run detail gets a full-height left pane — unchanged by this round, since a side-by-side pane is a new layout rather than a consistency fix. The dashboard's expanded two-column branch gaps its blocks with `_kSectionGap` per column via `addBlock(gapAfter:)` and was left as is: a grid column is not the stack the rhythm test measures.

## 534. A number is measured against the wrong ground more often than it is wrong, and a test over an empty set passes

**Date:** 2026-08-06

Round 14's five agents merged with one trivial conflict (two agents editing the ui_kit barrel — one adding an export, the other having deleted a zero-caller widget the first still listed). The findings worth keeping are about measurement and about tests.

**§503's trap has now caught six consecutive rounds, and the majority of its instances are not "the ratio was wrong" but "the ground was wrong."** §529 re-derived the five `OPEN_DEBTS` figures §526 had registered and three did not survive: the provider glyphs were measured over `--color-bg-tertiary` when the per-provider rule *replaces* that background and composites over the card (on the real ground only **Strava** fails in light at 2.921, while **two dark failures nobody had looked at** — ultrasignup 2.690, chronotrack 2.886 — were live); `VerifiedBadge`'s 3.127 was judged against 4.5:1 when the mark is `aria-hidden` SVG geometry owing 1.4.11's 3:1, so it was **never failing**; and the worst nav figure is **1.219:1** (a 24 % hover disc), a state the register had not sampled, while the registered 1.460 is not reproducible on any ground the sidebar paints. The same round found §525's own summary contradicting its own allowlist (28 files, not 27) and understating its own narrowest case (8 px, not 9.6 — described correctly one paragraph earlier and then excluded from the range). **The rule to carry: record the ground and the floor beside every figure, because a bare ratio cannot be re-checked.** A figure with its ground attached is auditable; one without is folklore, and five rounds have now inherited folklore.

**A test can pass because it asserted over nothing.** §530's first draft of its type-floor Playwright spec passed with the 8.8 px override planted back: the selectors it measured (`.kind`, `.dist`) only render on a day carrying a workout, and the seeded plan's week gap meant the locator matched **zero elements**, so every assertion over the empty set held. The fix pins an expected count and seeds a workout into whichever week is current. This is the same family as §522's broken guard file — machinery that has silently stopped checking — and the same detection rule applies: **assert the population, not only the property.** A selector-based assertion needs a count; a source scan needs a non-zero match; a guard file needs its test total compared across a merge.

Two smaller lessons, both from perturbation testing rather than review. **An extraction that discriminates with `?? `on a nullable source is a null bug waiting**: §533's shared run row wrote `_run?.x ?? _row!.x`, which dereferences the absent source whenever the present one's value is legitimately null — a run with no metadata threw, and only a test with a null-metadata fixture found it. And **a fixed drag offset is an absolute fit in disguise** (§500's rule, on a new axis): shortening a hero map moved a test's drag start point off the map onto the list below, changing which gesture recognizer won, so the failure looked like a map bug and was a harness bug.

## 535. The 320px reflow failure was one flex item's default minimum, not fifty page bugs; content that cannot reflow scrolls inside its own box

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 14's index named `/dashboard` laying out **752 px wide at a 360 px viewport** as the strongest remaining candidate, with `.plan-hero` at 736. Both figures reproduced exactly on the current tree (`documentElement.scrollWidth` 752 against a `clientWidth` of 360 — and the *same* 752 at 320, which is the tell: the document width was not a function of the viewport at all). The diagnosis in the index was the wrong layer, though. `.plan-hero` was not a cause; it was one of six siblings all stretched to 648, the content width of a `main` that had stopped tracking the viewport. `.main-content` is `flex: 1` inside `.app-shell`, and a flex item's default `min-width: auto` floors it at its content's min-content width — so the page box grew to fit its widest descendant and the whole document scrolled sideways, a WCAG **1.4.10** failure that no amount of per-card work could have fixed. `min-width: 0` on that one rule took `/dashboard` from **752 to 472** at both viewports in a single declaration.

What the remaining 472 exposed is that the sweep the finding asked for was worth doing: **34 of 47 static routes and 8 of 24 dynamic ones overflowed at 320 px**, in five mechanical classes, none of them route-specific. (1) `repeat(auto-fit|auto-fill, minmax(X, 1fr))` with a fixed `X` cannot reflow below `X` — 47 sites, the widest being `/history`'s timeline at `minmax(30rem, …)`, all now `minmax(min(X, 100%), 1fr)`. (2) A bare fraction track floors at min-content, so `1fr 1fr` and `repeat(n, 1fr)` behave the same way — 43 more sites, now `minmax(0, 1fr)`; the residue includes a `fieldset`, whose UA `min-width: min-content` is the same bug shipped by the browser. (3) `--page-padding-x` resolved to `--space-2xl` at every width: 3 rem each side, which on a 320 px screen costs 96 px on top of the 72 px rail and leaves **152 px of canvas**. Forty-eight page wrappers had hardcoded that token pair rather than reading `--page-padding-*`, so they moved onto the tokens and the tokens narrow at the same 40 rem breakpoint the sidebar already locks to its rail — one declaration, 152 px of canvas becomes 216. (4) Title-plus-actions rows, chip rows and stat rows without `flex-wrap`. (5) Two shells that reserved more width than the screen has: the settings layout's 14 rem nav rail (its content column measured **0 px** of usable width at 320) and `SplitPane`'s `min = 280` per pane; both stack below 40 rem, and the settings nav wraps rather than scrolls so its heading, group labels and legal links all stay reachable.

Two decisions are worth naming because they went the other way. **The canonical `.btn`'s `white-space: nowrap` is relaxed only below 40 rem, not removed.** A label like "Download my data (JSON)" measures past 200 px at 0.875 rem against 166 px of canvas, so on a phone nowrap can only widen the document; above that breakpoint the canvas is wide enough and the single line is the better default, and a global change would have altered every button in the app on evidence gathered at one width. And **content whose axis is its information is allowed to scroll inside itself** — 1.4.10 exempts exactly this.
